SP of x items = CP of 32 items
Profit % = 28

Concept used:

SP = CP + CP × profit%
SP = selling price
CP = cost price

Calculation:
Let CP of each item be Rs. 100a
So, CP of x item = Rs. 100xa
SP of each item = 128xa

According to the question,

x.SP = 32.CP
⇒ 128ax = 3200a
⇒ x = 3200a/128a
⇒ x = 25
So, x = 25 items
∴ The value of x is 25.

questions.question: What should be the least five digit number that on dividing by 3, 7, 13 and 37 give 2 as remainder?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
The numbers 3, 7, 13, and 37 are all prime numbers.

Their LCM is simply their product: 3 × 7 × 13 × 37 = 10101.

This is already the least five-digit number divisible by all four.

To get a remainder of 2, simply add 2 to this LCM: 10101 + 2 = 10103.
∴ The correct answer is 10103.

Alternate Method
Given:
Divisors: 3, 7, 13, 37
Remainder: 2
Formula: Required Number = LCM(Divisors) × k + Remainder

Calculations:
⇒ LCM(3, 7, 13, 37) = 3 × 7 × 13 × 37
⇒ 21 × 13 × 37
⇒ 273 × 37
⇒ 10101

The number must be of the form 10101k + 2.

For the least five-digit number, we take k = 1:
⇒ Number = 10101 × 1 + 2
⇒ Number = 10101 + 2
⇒ Number = 10103
∴ The correct answer is 10103.

Additional Information
General Remainder Rule

If a number gives the same remainder R when divided by a, b, and c, then the general form is LCM(a, b, c) × k + R.

LCM of Prime Numbers

The Least Common Multiple of any set of prime numbers is always equal to their product.

Divisibility by 10101

The number 10101 is a unique number that can be expressed as 3 × 7 × 13 × 37 or 101 × 100 + 1.

questions.question: In a school auditorium 2/7 of the students are girls. If there are 111 more boys than girls, how many boys are there in the school auditorium?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Given Fraction = 2/7
Total Students = 7 units
Girls = 2 units
Boys = 7 - 2 = 5 units

Also Given, there are 111 more boys than girls

According to the fraction,

More Number = 5 - 2 = 3 units
3 units = 111
1 unit = 37
Number of boys = 5 units = 5 × 37 = 185

Given:
Total number of girls = 2/7 of total students

The total number of boys is 111 more than girls.

Calculation:
Suppose, the total number of girls in the school auditorium = x
Then, total number of boys in the school auditorium = (x + 111)
Total students in the school auditorium = x + (x + 111) = 2x + 111
Therefore, x = 2/7 × (2x + 111)
⇒ x = (4x + 222)/7
⇒ 7x = 4x + 222
⇒ 7x - 4x = 222
⇒ 3x = 222
⇒ x = 222/3 = 74
Total number of boys = 74 + 111 = 185
∴ Total of 185 boys are there in the school auditorium.

questions.question: The compound interest accrued on an amount of Rs. 25,500 at the end of three years is Rs. 8,440.50. What would be the simple interest accrued on the same amount at the same rate in the same period?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of Amount to Principal for 3 years = (25500 + 8440.50) ÷ 25500 = 33940.5 ÷ 25500 = 1331 / 1000.
Equivalent ratio for 1 year = 3√(1331 / 1000) = 11 / 10.
Interest rate
(R) = (11 − 10) ÷ 10 × 100% = 10%.
Simple Interest for 3 years = 30% of Principal = 30% of 25500 = 7650.
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7650.

Alternate Method
Given:
Principal
(P) = Rs. 25,500
Time (T) = 3 years
Compound Interest (CI) = Rs. 8,440.50

Formula Used:
Amount (A) = P(1 + R / 100)T
Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:
⇒ Amount (A) = P + CI
⇒ A = 25500 + 8440.50 = 33940.50
⇒ 33940.50 = 25500 × (1 + R / 100)3
⇒ (1 + R / 100)3 = 33940.50 ÷ 25500
⇒ (1 + R / 100)3 = 339405 / 255000
⇒ (1 + R / 100)3 = 1331 / 1000 (dividing by 255)
⇒ (1 + R / 100)3 = (11 / 10)3
⇒ 1 + R / 100 = 11 / 10
⇒ R / 100 = 1 / 10
⇒ R = 10%
⇒ SI = (25500 × 10 × 3) ÷ 100
⇒ SI = 255 × 30 = 7650
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7650.

Additional Information
Effective Compound Interest Rate

For a 10% per annum rate, the effective CI for 2 years is 21%, and for 3 years, it is 33.1%.

Difference Between CI and SI (2 Years)
Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)2. It determines the extra interest earned through compounding over exactly two years.
Difference Between CI and SI (3 Years)
Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)2 × (3 + R ÷ 100). Essential formula for efficiently finding the three-year CI and SI differences without complete calculations.

questions.question: A leaves from a place X at 10 a.m. at 40 km/h. B leaves from the same place at 2 p.m. at 80 km/h, and chases A. When and how far from X will B meet A?
questions.solution:
Solution

Given:
The speed of A is 40 km/h

The speed of B is 80 km/h

Concept used:

Speed = Distance/Time

When two trains are moving in the same direction then their relative speed = Difference of their individual speeds

Calculation:
Distance travelled by A till 2 pm = 4 × 40 = 160 km
A and B travelled in the same direction then relative speed = 80 - 40 = 40 km/h
Time taken by B to meet A = 160/40 = 4 hours or at "6 pm"
In 4 hours travelled distance by B = 4 × 80 = 320 km
∴ The required result will be "320 km and at 6 pm".

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026: Officer’s Friday - Mega Live Test
questions.question: In case of a particular transaction, the profit earned is 14 2/7%. What fraction is the cost price of the selling price?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Convert Profit % to fraction: 14 2/7% = 1/7.

Here, Denominator (7) represents the Cost Price (CP) and Numerator (1) represents the Profit.

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = 7 + 1 = 8 units.
Required fraction (CP/SP) = 7/8.
∴ The correct answer is 7/8.

Alternate Method
Given: Profit percentage = 14 2/7% = (100/7)%.
Formula Used: Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) + Profit; Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100
⇒ Profit fraction = (100/7) ÷ 100 = 1/7
⇒ This implies that for every 7 units of Cost Price, the Profit earned is 1 unit.
⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) = 7x
⇒ Profit = 1x
⇒ Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = 7x + 1x = 8x
⇒ Fraction of CP to SP = CP ÷ SP = 7x ÷ 8x
⇒ Fraction = 7/8
∴ The correct answer is 7/8.

Additional Information
Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Common percentages like 14 2/7% = 1/7, 12 1/2% = 1/8, and 11 1/9% = 1/9 are essential for solving Profit and Loss questions quickly.

CP and SP Relationship

If Profit % is expressed as a fraction a/b, then the ratio of C
P : SP is always b : (b + a). For a Loss % of a/b, the ratio of C
P : SP is b : (b − a).

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price can also be calculated using Marked Price (MP): SP = MP × (1 − Discount%/100).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: 12 men complete a work in 9 days. After they have worked for 6 days, 6 more men join them. How many days will they take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Remaining days of work for the initial 12 men = 9 − 6 = 3 days.
Remaining work in terms of man-days = 12 men × 3 days = 36 man-days.
New number of men working = 12 + 6 = 18 men.
Days required to complete the remaining work = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 days.
∴ The correct answer is 2 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
Initial number of men = 12
Total days required = 9
Days they worked before others joined = 6
New men joined = 6

Formula Used:
Total Work = Number of Men × Days

Person	Days	Total Work	Efficiency
12 Men	9	108	12

Calculations:
⇒ Let the efficiency of 1 man be 1 unit/day.
⇒ Total work to be done = 108 units
⇒ Work completed by 12 men in 6 days = 12 × 6 = 72 units
⇒ Remaining work = 108 − 72 = 36 units
⇒ Total men present after 6 days = 12 + 6 = 18 men
⇒ Combined efficiency of 18 men = 18 units/day
⇒ Time taken to complete the remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ Combined Efficiency
⇒ Time taken = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 days
∴ The correct answer is 2 days.

Additional Information
MDH Rule (Chain Rule)

If M1 men can do W1 work in D1 days working H1 hours/day, and M2 men can do W2 work in D2 days working H2 hours/day, then the relation is given by: (M1 × D1 × H1) ÷ W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2) ÷ W2.

Work and Men Proportionality

The number of men required is inversely proportional to the number of days needed to complete the same amount of work. More men take fewer days, and fewer men take more days to complete identical work.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person. If all individuals work for the same number of days, their wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their daily efficiencies.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: Ramesh purchases 75 articles for ₹ 10800 and sells them at a loss equal to the selling price of 5 articles. What will be the selling price of one article?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Loss = CP of 75 articles − SP of 75 articles = SP of 5 articles
⇒ CP of 75 articles = SP of (75 + 5) articles = SP of 80 articles
⇒ SP of 80 articles = Total CP = ₹10800
⇒ SP of 1 article = 10800 ÷ 80 = 135
∴ The correct answer is ₹135.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total articles purchased = 75
Total Cost Price (CP) = ₹10800
Loss incurred = Selling Price (SP) of 5 articles

Formula Used:
Loss = Total CP − Total SP

Calculations:
⇒ Total CP of 75 articles − Total SP of 75 articles = Loss
⇒ ₹10800 − SP of 75 articles = SP of 5 articles
⇒ ₹10800 = SP of 75 articles + SP of 5 articles
⇒ ₹10800 = SP of 80 articles
⇒ SP of 1 article = 10800 ÷ 80
⇒ SP of 1 article = 135
∴ The correct answer is ₹135.

Additional Information
Profit and Loss Equation
Profit occurs when SP > CP (Profit = SP − CP), and Loss occurs when CP > SP (Loss = CP − SP).

Similar Concept (Profit in terms of SP)

If there is a profit equal to the SP of y articles on selling x articles, then CP of x articles = SP of (x − y) articles.

Profit and Loss Percentage
Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 | Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Both are computed on the Cost Price by default.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: What is the simple interest on Rs. 32,000 at 8.5% per annum for period from 10th Feb., 2019 to 24th April, 2019?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total time from 10th Feb to 24th April = 18 + 31 + 24 = 73 days = 1/5 year.
Effective interest rate for 1/5 year = 8.5% ÷ 5 = 1.7%.
Simple Interest = 1.7% of 32000 = (1.7 × 32000) ÷ 100 = Rs. 544.
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 544.

Alternate Method
Given:
Principal
(P) = Rs. 32000
Rate
(R) = 8.5% p.a.
Time (T) = 10th Feb., 2019 to 24th April, 2019

Formula Used:
SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:
⇒ Number of days in February (2019 is a non-leap year) = 28 − 10 = 18 days
⇒ Number of days in March = 31 days
⇒ Number of days in April = 24 days
⇒ Total Time (T) = 18 + 31 + 24 = 73 days
⇒ Time in years = 73 ÷ 365 = 1/5 years
⇒ SI = (32000 × 8.5 × 1) ÷ (100 × 5)
⇒ SI = 320 × 1.7
⇒ SI = Rs. 544
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 544.

Additional Information
Counting of Days in SI Calculation

Generally, the day the money is deposited is not counted, but the day the money is withdrawn is counted. Total days are then converted to years by dividing by 365.

Leap Year Consideration

If the given period falls within a leap year and includes the month of February, 29 days are considered for February. For the year 2019, it is a non-leap year so February has 28 days.

Standard Day Fractions

Exam questions frequently use exact multiples of 73 days for simple calculations because 73 days = 1/5 year, 146 days = 2/5 year, 219 days = 3/5 year, and 292 days = 4/5 year.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: Rahul has a bag which contains Rs. 1, 50 paisa, and 25 paisa coins and the ratio of number of coins is 1 ∶ 1/2 ∶ 1/3. If Rahul has a total amount of Rs 1120, then find the total value of 25 paisa coins.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of number of coins (Rs 1 : 50p : 25p) = 1 : 1/2 : 1/3 = 6 : 3 : 2
Ratio of their values = (6 × 1) : (3 × 1/2) : (2 × 1/4) = 6 : 1.5 : 0.5 = 12 : 3 : 1
Total value = 12 + 3 + 1 = 16 units
16 units = Rs 1120 ⇒ 1 unit = 1120 ÷ 16 = Rs 70
Value of 25 paisa coins = 1 unit = Rs 70
∴ The correct answer is Rs 70.

Alternate Method
Given:
Types of coins: Rs 1, 50 paisa (Rs 1/2), and 25 paisa (Rs 1/4).
Ratio of the number of coins = 1 : 1/2 : 1/3
Total amount in the bag = Rs 1120

Formula Used:
Total Value = Number of coins × Denomination Value

Calculations:
⇒ Multiply the given coin ratio by the LCM of denominators (6) to convert to integers.
⇒ Number of coins ratio = (1 × 6) : (1/2 × 6) : (1/3 × 6) = 6 : 3 : 2
⇒ Let the number of Rs 1, 50 paisa, and 25 paisa coins be 6x, 3x, and 2x respectively.
⇒ Value of Rs 1 coins = 6x × 1 = 6x
⇒ Value of 50 paisa coins = 3x × 0.5 = 1.5x
⇒ Value of 25 paisa coins = 2x × 0.25 = 0.5x
⇒ Total value = 6x + 1.5x + 0.5x = 8x
⇒ According to the given data, total amount is Rs 1120.
⇒ 8x = 1120
⇒ x = 1120 ÷ 8 = 140
⇒ Total value of 25 paisa coins = 0.5x = 0.5 × 140 = 70
∴ The correct answer is Rs 70.

Additional Information
Ratio of Coins vs Value

When the ratio of the number of coins is given, multiply it by the respective denomination to find the ratio of their values. Conversely, divide the value ratio by the denomination to find the number of coins ratio.

Common Denominations

It is a standard rule to convert all coins into rupees: 50 paisa = Rs 1/2, 25 paisa = Rs 1/4, 20 paisa = Rs 1/5, and 10 paisa = Rs 1/10.

Consistency of Units

Always ensure that both individual denominations and the total final amount are measured in the same unit (either entirely in Rupees or entirely in paise) to avoid calculation errors.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 17 : 45. One-third of the smaller is less than one-fifth of bigger by 15. The smaller number is?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the two numbers be 17 units and 45 units.
1/3 of the smaller number = 17/3 units, and 1/5 of the bigger number = 45/5 = 9 units.
Difference = 9 − 17/3 = (27 − 17) / 3 = 10/3 units.
Given, 10/3 units = 15 ⇒ 1 unit = 15 × 3 ÷ 10 = 4.5
Smaller number = 17 units = 17 × 4.5 = 76.5
∴ The correct answer is 76.5.

Alternate Method
Given:
Ratio of the two numbers = 17 : 45

The difference between 1/5 of the bigger number and 1/3 of the smaller number = 15

Calculation:
⇒ Let the smaller number be 17x and the bigger number be 45x.
⇒ One-third of the smaller number = 17x / 3
⇒ One-fifth of the bigger number = 45x / 5 = 9x
⇒ According to the question, 9x − 17x / 3 = 15
⇒ (27x − 17x) / 3 = 15
⇒ 10x / 3 = 15
⇒ 10x = 45
⇒ x = 4.5
⇒ Smaller number = 17x = 17 × 4.5 = 76.5
∴ The correct answer is 76.5.

Additional Information
Compound Ratio

If two ratios are a : b and c : d, then their compound ratio is given by ac : bd.

Duplicate & Sub-duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a : b is a2 : b2, and the sub-duplicate ratio is √a : √b.

Componendo and Dividendo

If a : b = c : d, then by the rule of componendo and dividendo (a + b) : (a − b) = (c + d) : (c − d).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: The average age of a class of 40 students and a teacher reduces by 0.5 years, if we exclude the teacher. If the initial average age is 18 years, then what is the age of the teacher?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Age of excluded person = Initial Average + (Remaining members × Drop in average)
⇒ Age of teacher = 18 + (40 × 0.5)
⇒ Age of teacher = 18 + 20
⇒ Age of teacher = 38 years
∴ The correct answer is 38 years.

Alternate Method
Given:
Number of students = 40
Total persons initially (40 students + 1 teacher) = 41
Initial average age = 18 years
New average age (teacher excluded) = 18 − 0.5 = 17.5 years

Formula Used:
Total Age = Average Age × Number of Persons
Age of Teacher = (Total age of 41 persons) − (Total age of 40 students)

Calculations:
⇒ Total age initially = 41 × 18 = 738 years
⇒ Total age after excluding teacher = 40 × 17.5 = 700 years
⇒ Age of teacher = 738 − 700
⇒ Age of teacher = 38 years
∴ The correct answer is 38 years.

Additional Information
Weighted Average

When two or more groups with different averages are combined, the combined average is calculated as (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Concept of Replacement

When a person is replaced by a new person, the change in total value is: New Value − Old Value = Total Members × Change in Average.

Concept of Inclusion

When a new person joins a group, their value = Old Average + (New Total Members × Increase in Average).

questions.question: In what ratio should rice costing Rs. 67.5 per kg be mixed with rice costing Rs. 60 per kg to get an average price of Rs. 64 per kg?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
By using the direct alligation cross-multiplication rule:

Quantity Ratio = (Mean Price − Cheaper Price) : (Dearer Price − Mean Price)
⇒ Ratio = (64 − 60) : (67.5 − 64)
⇒ Ratio = 4 : 3.5
⇒ Ratio = 8 : 7
∴ The correct answer is 8 : 7.

Alternate Method
Given:
Price of first rice type = ₹67.5 per kg
Price of second rice type = ₹60 per kg
Average mean price = ₹64 per kg

Formula Used:
If two types of items of price p1 and p2 are mixed to get an average mean price pm, the ratio of their quantities q1 : q2 is (pm − p2) : (p1 − pm).

Calculations:
Let the required ratio be x : y.
⇒ Quantity ratio = (Mean Price − Price of Cheaper) : (Price of Dearer − Mean Price)
⇒ x : y = (64 − 60) : (67.5 − 64)
⇒ x : y = 4 : 3.5

Multiply both sides by 2 to convert into integer ratio:

⇒ x : y = 8 : 7
∴ The correct answer is 8 : 7.

Additional Information
Alligation Rule

It is a quick method to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at given prices must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired median price.

Weighted Average Formula

Average Price = (q1 × p1 + q2 × p2) ÷ (q1 + q2)

Replacement Method

If from a vessel containing volume V of pure liquid, volume x is removed and replaced n times, then Final Volume = V × (1 − x ÷ V)n.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: In a circular race of 840 m, A and B start running in the same direction at the same time from the same point at the speeds of 6 m/s and 12 m/s, respectively. After how much time will they meet next?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Since A and B are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their speeds.

Relative Speed = 12 − 6 = 6 m/s
Time to meet next = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed
Time = 840 ÷ 6 = 140 s
∴ The correct answer is 140 s.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Length of circular track (D) = 840 m
⇒ Speed of A (SA) = 6 m/s
⇒ Speed of B (SB) = 12 m/s

Formula Used:
⇒ Relative Speed (same direction) = |SB − SA|
⇒ Time to meet = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Calculations:
⇒ Relative Speed = 12 m/s − 6 m/s = 6 m/s
⇒ Time to meet = 840 ÷ 6
⇒ Time to meet = 140 s
∴ The correct answer is 140 s.

Additional Information
First Meeting Anywhere on Track

When two persons run in the same direction, they meet for the first time when the faster person covers exactly one more round than the slower person. Time = Length of Track ÷ Relative Speed.

First Meeting at Starting Point

The time taken to meet for the first time at the starting point is the LCM of the individual times taken by each person to complete one full round. Time = LCM(T1, T2).

Running in Opposite Directions

If two runners move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S1 + S2). The time for their first meeting anywhere on the track is Track Length ÷ (S1 + S2).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: In a division sum, the divisor is 13 times the quotient and 6 times the remainder. If the remainder is 39, then the dividend is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Given Remainder = 39
Divisor = 6 × 39 = 234
Quotient = 234 ÷ 13 = 18
Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder
Dividend = (234 × 18) + 39 = 4212 + 39 = 4251
∴ The correct answer is 4251.

Alternate Method
Given:
Remainder
(R) = 39
Divisor (D) = 13 × Quotient
(Q)
Divisor (D) = 6 × Remainder
(R)

Formula Used:
Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

Calculations:
⇒ Divisor (D) = 6 × 39
⇒ D = 234
⇒ 234 = 13 × Q
⇒ Q = 234 ÷ 13
⇒ Q = 18
⇒ Dividend = (234 × 18) + 39
⇒ Dividend = 4212 + 39
⇒ Dividend = 4251
∴ The correct answer is 4251.

Additional Information
Division Algorithm

The fundamental relation in division is: Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder, where the remainder is always strictly less than the divisor.

Divisibility Rule for 13

To quickly check if a number is divisible by 13, multiply the last digit by 4 and add it to the remaining truncated number. If the new result is divisible by 13, the original number is also divisible.

Remainder Theorem

In polynomial algebra, when a polynomial P(x) is divided by a linear polynomial (x − a), the remainder obtained is equal to the value of P(a).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question:
Simplify the following expression:
((32)^4 - 1) / [3^3 × 31 × (2^10 + 1)]
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Express 32 as 25, making the numerator (25)4 − 1 = 220 − 1.
Rewrite the product 33 × 31 as (32 + 1)(32 − 1) = 322 − 1 = (25)2 − 1 = 210 − 1.
The denominator becomes (210 − 1)(210 + 1) = (210)2 − 12 = 220 − 1.
Divide the numerator by the denominator: (220 − 1) ÷ (220 − 1) = 1.
∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method
Given:
Expression: (324 − 1) ÷ [33 × 31 × (210 + 1)]

Formula Used:
a2 − b2 = (a − b)(a + b)
(am)n = am × n

Calculations:
⇒ Let's expand and simplify the denominator first.
⇒ 33 × 31 = (32 + 1) × (32 − 1)
⇒ Applying the a2 − b2 formula, we get 322 − 12.
⇒ Since 32 = 25, we have (25)2 − 1 = 210 − 1.
⇒ Now substitute this back into the denominator expression: (210 − 1) × (210 + 1).
⇒ Again applying the a2 − b2 formula, the denominator becomes (210)2 − 12 = 220 − 1.
⇒ Next, simplify the numerator: 324 − 1 = (25)4 − 1 = 220 − 1.
⇒ The complete expression simplifies to (220 − 1) ÷ (220 − 1).
⇒ Since the numerator and denominator are exactly the same, they cancel out to leave 1.
∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information
BODMAS Rule

It dictates the precise order of mathematical operations to follow: Brackets, Orders (powers and roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Laws of Exponents

Key rules to quickly handle base numbers include am × an = am+n, am ÷ an = am−n, and (am)n = am×n.
Difference of Squares
The algebraic identity a2 − b2 = (a − b)(a + b) is an essential tool frequently used to simplify large mathematical products mentally.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: A motorboat, whose speed is 15 km/h in still water goes 20 km downstream and comes back in a total of 4 hours. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total Time = [ 2 × Distance × Boat Speed ] ÷ [ (Boat Speed)2 − (Stream Speed)2 ]
4 = [ 2 × 20 × 15 ] ÷ [ 152 − v2 ]
4 × (225 − v2) = 600
225 − v2 = 150 ⇒ v2 = 75
v = √75 = 5√3 km/h
∴ The correct answer is 5√3 km/h.

Alternate Method
Given:
Speed of motorboat in still water (u) = 15 km/h
Distance (d) = 20 km
Total time taken (T) = 4 hours
Let the speed of the stream be v km/h.

Formula Used:
Time = Distance ÷ Speed
Downstream Speed = u + v
Upstream Speed = u − v

Calculations:
⇒ Downstream Speed = (15 + v) km/h
⇒ Upstream Speed = (15 − v) km/h
⇒ Total Time = [Distance ÷ Downstream Speed] + [Distance ÷ Upstream Speed]
⇒ 20 ÷ (15 + v) + 20 ÷ (15 − v) = 4
⇒ 20 × [ (15 − v + 15 + v) ÷ (152 − v2) ] = 4
⇒ 20 × [ 30 ÷ (225 − v2) ] = 4
⇒ 600 ÷ (225 − v2) = 4
⇒ 225 − v2 = 150
⇒ v2 = 75
⇒ v = √75 = 5√3 km/h
∴ The correct answer is 5√3 km/h.

Additional Information
Downstream Speed

When the boat moves in the direction of the stream, speeds are added. Downstream Speed = Speed of Boat + Speed of Stream.

Upstream Speed

When the boat moves against the direction of the stream, speeds are subtracted. Upstream Speed = Speed of Boat − Speed of Stream.

Speed in Still Water
If downstream and upstream speeds are given, Speed of Boat = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.
Speed of Stream
If downstream and upstream speeds are given, Speed of Stream = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: The ages of A and B are in the ratio 4 : 7, respectively. After 8 years, the ratio of their ages will be 2 : 3. What is the sum of the ages of A and B (in years)?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Present ratio A : B = 4 : 7 (Gap = 7 − 4 = 3)
Future ratio A : B = 2 : 3 (Gap = 3 − 2 = 1) → Multiply by 3 to equalize gaps ⇒ 6 : 9
Increase in ratio parts for both A and B = 6 − 4 = 2 parts.
2 parts ≡ 8 years ⇒ 1 part = 4 years.
Sum of present ages = (4 + 7) = 11 parts = 11 × 4 = 44 years.
∴ The correct answer is 44 years.

Alternate Method
Given:
Present ages of A and B are in the ratio 4 : 7
After 8 years, the ratio of their ages will be 2 : 3

Method Used:

Equating the age ratios using algebraic variables to find the exact multiplier.

Calculations:
⇒ Let the present ages of A and B be 4x and 7x respectively.
⇒ After 8 years, A's age = (4x + 8) and B's age = (7x + 8)
⇒ According to the condition: (4x + 8) ÷ (7x + 8) = 2 ÷ 3
⇒ Cross-multiplying: 3 × (4x + 8) = 2 × (7x + 8)
⇒ 12x + 24 = 14x + 16
⇒ 14x − 12x = 24 − 16
⇒ 2x = 8 ⇒ x = 4
⇒ Sum of their present ages = 4x + 7x = 11x
⇒ Total sum = 11 × 4 = 44 years
∴ The correct answer is 44 years.

Additional Information
Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals remains constant regardless of the years passed. This property is heavily used to equalize ratio gaps in age-related problems.

Cross-Multiplication in Ratios

When a constant value is added to both terms of a ratio a : b to form a new ratio c : d, the equation (a+x)÷(b+x) = c÷d is used to directly solve for the unknown variable.

Finding Present Ages

Always assume the present ages as multiples of the given ratio parts (e.g., 4x and 7x). Calculate the exact value of x before deriving final quantities like sum, difference, or future ages.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: If A : B = 8 : 13, B : C = 5 : 8 and C : D = 4 : 5, then A : B : C : D is equal to:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the vertical and cross multiplication shortcut for continuous ratios:

A = 8 × 5 × 4 = 160, B = 13 × 5 × 4 = 260
C = 13 × 8 × 4 = 416, D = 13 × 8 × 5 = 520
A : B : C : D = 160 : 260 : 416 : 520 ⇒ 40 : 65 : 104 : 130
∴ The correct answer is 40 : 65 : 104 : 130.

Alternate Method
Given:
A : B = 8 : 13
B : C = 5 : 8
C : D = 4 : 5

Concept Used:

We use the adjacent block fill method. Write the given ratios in rows and fill the empty spaces with the adjacent number in that row, then multiply the columns downwards.

Calculations:
⇒ Multiply the values in each column to get the combined ratio.
⇒ Column A = 8 × 5 × 4 = 160
⇒ Column B = 13 × 5 × 4 = 260
⇒ Column C = 13 × 8 × 4 = 416
⇒ Column D = 13 × 8 × 5 = 520
⇒ A : B : C : D = 160 : 260 : 416 : 520
⇒ Dividing each term by 4 to simplify the ratio, we get:
⇒ A : B : C : D = 40 : 65 : 104 : 130
∴ The correct answer is 40 : 65 : 104 : 130.

Additional Information
Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are multiplied together, it is known as a compound ratio. For ratios a : b and c : d, the compound ratio is ac : bd.

Duplicate & Sub-duplicate Ratio

For a ratio a : b, its duplicate ratio is a2 : b2, and its sub-duplicate ratio is √a : √b.

Componendo and Dividendo

If a : b = c : d, then by the componendo and dividendo rule, (a + b) : (a − b) = (c + d) : (c − d).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: A group of 25 tourists consume 5 containers of food in 8 days in a hotel. How many containers will be required for 10 tourists to eat for 16 days?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the Chain Rule (MDH) formula: M1 × D1 / W1 = M2 × D2 / W2
Where M = tourists, D = days, W = containers of food.
⇒ (25 × 8) / 5 = (10 × 16) / W2
⇒ 40 = 160 / W2 ⇒ W2 = 4
∴ The correct answer is 4 containers.

Alternate Method
Given:
Group 1: M1 = 25 tourists, D1 = 8 days, W1 = 5 containers
Group 2: M2 = 10 tourists, D2 = 16 days, W2 = ?

Formula Used:
M1 × D1 / W1 = M2 × D2 / W2

Calculations:
⇒ (25 × 8) / 5 = (10 × 16) / W2
⇒ 200 / 5 = 160 / W2
⇒ 40 = 160 / W2
⇒ W2 = 160 / 40
⇒ W2 = 4
∴ The correct answer is 4 containers.

Additional Information
Chain Rule (MDH Formula)

The foundational formula for equivalence is M1 × D1 × H1 / W1 = M2 × D2 × H2 / W2, where M is the number of people, D is the number of days, H is the number of hours, and W is the total work done or resource consumed.

Direct Proportion

Two quantities are directly proportional if they increase or decrease together at the same rate. For example, keeping the days constant, more tourists will predictably consume a proportionally higher amount of food.

Inverse Proportion

Two quantities are inversely proportional if an increase in one factor automatically causes a decrease in the other. For instance, given a fixed amount of food, increasing the number of tourists reduces the number of days that food will last.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: A dealer sells an article at ₹850 after offering a cash discount of 15% on its marked price. Without discount, he would have earned a profit of 25%. What is the cost price of the article (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Selling Price (SP) = ₹850, Discount = 15% ⇒ MP = 850 × (100 ÷ 85) = ₹1000
Without discount, SP = MP = ₹1000.
Profit = 25% ⇒ CP = 1000 × (100 ÷ 125) = ₹800.
∴ The correct answer is ₹800.

Alternate Method
Given:
Selling price with discount (SP) = ₹850
Discount percentage = 15%
Profit percentage without discount = 25%

Formula Used:
MP = SP × [100 ÷ (100 − Discount%)]
CP = SPnew × [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)]

Calculations:
⇒ Let Marked Price be MP.
⇒ SP = MP − 15% of MP = 0.85 × MP
⇒ 850 = 0.85 × MP
⇒ MP = 850 × (100 ÷ 85) = ₹1000
⇒ Without any discount, the dealer sells the article at its Marked Price.
⇒ So, New Selling Price (SPnew) = MP = ₹1000
⇒ At this price, Profit = 25%
⇒ CP + 25% of CP = SPnew
⇒ 1.25 × CP = 1000
⇒ CP = 1000 × (100 ÷ 125)
⇒ CP = ₹800
∴ The correct answer is ₹800.

Additional Information
Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The formula directly yields: Selling Price = MP × (1 − Discount%).

Profit/Loss Without Discount

When a shopkeeper gives no discount on an item, the Selling Price becomes equal to the Marked Price (SP = MP). Under this condition, Profit or Loss percentage is directly estimated over the Cost Price leading up to the MP.

Effective Multipliers Rule

For a given profit of P%, the selling price multiplier translates to SP = CP × (1 + P/100). Similarly, for a discount of D%, SP = MP × (1 − D/100). Equating both sides helps find any missing variable quickly.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: If x + y = 12 and xy = 6, then the value of x/y + y/x is equal to:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
We need to find the value of x/y + y/x, which simplifies to (x2 + y2) ÷ xy.

Using the identity: x2 + y2 = (x + y)2 − 2xy
Substitute the given values (x + y = 12, xy = 6) directly into the combined formula.
Required value = (122 − 2 × 6) ÷ 6 = (144 − 12) ÷ 6.
Required value = 132 ÷ 6 = 22.
∴ The correct answer is 22.

Alternate Method
Given:
x + y = 12
xy = 6

Formula Used:
(x + y)2 = x2 + y2 + 2xy

Calculations:
⇒ (12)2 = x2 + y2 + 2 × 6
⇒ 144 = x2 + y2 + 12
⇒ x2 + y2 = 144 − 12
⇒ x2 + y2 = 132
Now, we need to find the value of the given expression:
⇒ x/y + y/x = (x2 + y2) ÷ xy
⇒ x/y + y/x = 132 ÷ 6
⇒ x/y + y/x = 22
∴ The correct answer is 22.

Additional Information
Square of Difference

(x − y)2 = x2 + y2 − 2xy. This identity helps find the difference of variables when their sum and product are given.
Difference of Squares
x2 − y2 = (x − y)(x + y). A fundamental algebraic identity used widely in factorisation and simplification.

Sum of Cubes

x3 + y3 = (x + y)(x2 − xy + y2) or equivalently, x3 + y3 = (x + y)3 − 3xy(x + y).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: Male and female population of a city is increased by 50% and 20% respectively in 2017 from 2016 and male population in 2016 was 40% more than female population, then by what percent total population of the city is increased in 2017?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of Male to Female population in 2016 = 140 : 100 = 7 : 5.

We can use the weighted average method to find the net percentage change directly:

Overall % increase = [(Ratio of Male × % change in Male) + (Ratio of Female × % change in Female)] ÷ Total Ratio
Overall % increase = [(7 × 50) + (5 × 20)] ÷ (7 + 5)
Overall % increase = (350 + 100) ÷ 12 = 450 ÷ 12 = 37.5%.
∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Male population in 2016 is 40% more than female population.

Male population increased by 50% and female population increased by 20% in 2017.

Formula Used:
Percentage Increase = (Net Increase ÷ Initial Value) × 100

Calculations:
⇒ Let the female population in 2016 be 100x.
⇒ Male population in 2016 = 100x + (40% of 100x) = 140x.
⇒ Total population in 2016 = 100x + 140x = 240x.
⇒ In 2017, male population = 140x + (50% of 140x) = 140x + 70x = 210x.
⇒ In 2017, female population = 100x + (20% of 100x) = 100x + 20x = 120x.
⇒ Total population in 2017 = 210x + 120x = 330x.
⇒ Net increase in total population = 330x − 240x = 90x.
⇒ Percentage increase = (90x ÷ 240x) × 100 = (9 ÷ 24) × 100
⇒ Percentage increase = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%.
∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.

Additional Information
Percentage Change

The formula for finding the net percentage change of any value is calculated as: [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

Weighted Average in Percentage

If a total quantity is split into multiple parts in the ratio w1 : w2, and their individual percentage changes are p1% and p2%, the net percentage change of the entire group is (w1p1 + w2p2) ÷ (w1 + w2).

Base Shift Concept

When calculating percentage increases for two different components, always remember that their percentage values act upon their respective initial base numbers, not on the combined group total.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: 6 persons running around a ground complete one round in 6, 10, 12, 18, 30 and 40 minutes respectively. After how much time will they meet for the first time if they started running at the same time?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
The time taken by the runners to meet for the first time at the starting point is simply the LCM of their individual round times.

Required time = LCM(6, 10, 12, 18, 30, 40)
Required time = 360 minutes
Time in hours = 360 ÷ 60 = 6 hours
∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.

Alternate Method
Given:
Times taken by 6 persons to complete one round = 6, 10, 12, 18, 30, and 40 minutes.

Formula Used:
Time to meet again at the starting point = LCM of individual times to complete one round.

Calculations:
⇒ We need to find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of 6, 10, 12, 18, 30, and 40.
⇒ Prime factorization of 6 = 2 × 3
⇒ Prime factorization of 10 = 2 × 5
⇒ Prime factorization of 12 = 22 × 3
⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 32
⇒ Prime factorization of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5
⇒ Prime factorization of 40 = 23 × 5
⇒ LCM is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors involved.
⇒ Highest power of 2 = 23
⇒ Highest power of 3 = 32
⇒ Highest power of 5 = 5
⇒ LCM = 23 × 32 × 5 = 8 × 9 × 5 = 360 minutes.
⇒ Converting the time into hours = 360 ÷ 60 = 6 hours.
∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.

Additional Information
Meeting at the Starting Point on Circular Track

When multiple people are moving around a circular track starting at the same time and place, they meet at the starting point simultaneously after a time equal to the LCM of the times taken by each to complete one round independently.

First Meeting Anywhere on Circular Track

If two runners move in the same direction, the time to meet for the first time anywhere on the track = Track Length ÷ (S1 − S2). If they move in opposite directions, Time to meet = Track Length ÷ (S1 + S2).

LCM Formula for Fractions

If the individual completion times are given as fractions, you can find the meeting time using: LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: The length of a minute hand of a wall clock is 9 cm. What is the area swept (in cm^2) by the minute hand in 20 minutes ? (Take π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
The minute hand covers a full 360° circle in 60 minutes.

Fraction of circle swept in 20 minutes = 20 ÷ 60 = 1/3 of the total area.
Area swept = (1 ÷ 3) × π × r2
Area = (1 ÷ 3) × 3.14 × (9)2
Area = 3.14 × 27 = 84.78 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 84.78 cm2.

Alternate Method
Given:
Length of minute hand (radius), r = 9 cm
Time = 20 minutes
Value of π = 3.14

Formula Used:
Angle swept by minute hand in 1 minute = 360° ÷ 60 = 6°
Area of a sector = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr2

Calculations:
⇒ Angle swept in 20 minutes (θ) = 20 × 6° = 120°
⇒ Area swept = (120° ÷ 360°) × 3.14 × (9)2
⇒ Area swept = (1 ÷ 3) × 3.14 × 81
⇒ Area swept = 27 × 3.14
⇒ Area swept = 84.78 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 84.78 cm2.

Additional Information
Clock Angles

The minute hand of a clock moves 6° per minute, while the hour hand moves 0.5° per minute. This relative speed concept is key to solving all clock-based angle problems.

Area of Sector

The area of a sector of a circle with radius r and central angle θ is directly proportional to the angle and is calculated using the formula (θ ÷ 360°) × πr2.

Length of an Arc

The length of an arc corresponding to a central angle θ represents the distance moved along the circumference and is given by (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: Mukesh sells almonds at the cost price but uses a false weight and thus gains a 23% profit. How many grams of almonds is he giving for 3.075 kg?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Since the shopkeeper sells at cost price, the profit of 23% is entirely due to false weight.

Ratio of Claimed Weight (SP) to Actual Weight (CP) = (100 + 23) : 100 = 123 : 100
Here, Claimed Weight = 3.075 kg = 3075 g

123 units → 3075 g

1 unit → 25 g

Actual Weight (100 units) = 25 × 100 = 2500 g
∴ The correct answer is 2500 g.

Alternate Method
Given:
Claimed Weight = 3.075 kg = 3075 g
Profit = 23%

Formula Used:
Profit % = [(Claimed Weight − Actual Weight) ÷ Actual Weight] × 100

Calculations:
Let the actual weight given by Mukesh be x grams.
⇒ 23 = [(3075 − x) ÷ x] × 100
⇒ 23x = 307500 − 100x
⇒ 123x = 307500
⇒ x = 307500 ÷ 123
⇒ x = 2500
∴ The correct answer is 2500 g.

Additional Information
Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells goods at Cost Price (CP) but uses a false weight, his Profit % is determined directly by the error in weight. Formula: Profit % = [Error ÷ (Claimed Weight − Error)] × 100.

Net Profit with Markup

If the dealer marks up his goods by a certain percentage and simultaneously cheats by using a false weight, the net profit is calculated by combining both effects using the ratio method or successive percentage formula.

Selling Price and Markup
Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × [(100 − Discount%) ÷ 100]. This relationship helps identify the final price when a dealer offers a discount while committing weight fraud.

questions.question: If cos θ - sin θ = 0, then (sin^8 θ + cos^8 θ) is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Given cos θ − sin θ = 0, which implies tan θ = 1.
This means the angle θ = 45°.
At θ = 45°, sin θ = 1/√2 and cos θ = 1/√2.
Substitute the values: (1/√2)8 + (1/√2)8
⇒ 1/16 + 1/16 = 2/16 = 1/8.
∴ The correct answer is 1/8.

Alternate Method
Given:
cos θ − sin θ = 0

Calculations:
⇒ cos θ = sin θ

Squaring both sides, we get:

⇒ cos2 θ = sin2 θ

Using the standard trigonometric identity:

⇒ sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1

Substituting cos2 θ with sin2 θ:

⇒ sin2 θ + sin2 θ = 1
⇒ 2sin2 θ = 1
⇒ sin2 θ = 1/2   and   cos2 θ = 1/2
Now, we need to find the value of (sin8 θ + cos8 θ):
⇒ (sin2 θ)4 + (cos2 θ)4
⇒ (1/2)4 + (1/2)4
⇒ 1/16 + 1/16
⇒ 2/16 = 1/8
∴ The correct answer is 1/8.

Additional Information
Pythagorean Identities

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1 | sec2θ − tan2θ = 1 | cosec2θ − cot2θ = 1

Important Higher Power Expansions

sin4θ + cos4θ = 1 − 2sin2θ cos2θ | sin6θ + cos6θ = 1 − 3sin2θ cos2θ

Equalities at 45°

In the first quadrant, sin θ = cos θ only when θ = 45°. Similarly, tan θ = cot θ and sec θ = cosec θ are equal at θ = 45°.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 4
questions.question: The height of a right pyramid and the side length of its square base are equal. The perimeter of the base is 36 inches. Give its volume in cubic inches.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Side of the square base = Base Perimeter ÷ 4 = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 inches.
Height of the pyramid = Side of the base = 9 inches.
Volume of right pyramid = (1/3) × Base Area × Height
Volume = (1/3) × (9 × 9) × 9 = 243 cubic inches.
∴ The correct answer is 243 cubic inches.

Alternate Method
Given:
Perimeter of the square base = 36 inches.
Height of the pyramid (h) = Side length of the square base (a).

Formula Used:
Perimeter of square = 4 × a
Area of square base = a2
Volume of a pyramid (V) = (1/3) × Base Area × Height (h)

Calculation:
⇒ 4 × a = 36
⇒ a = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 inches
⇒ Height (h) = a = 9 inches
⇒ Area of square base = 9 × 9 = 81 sq. inches
⇒ Volume (V) = (1/3) × 81 × 9
⇒ Volume = 27 × 9
⇒ Volume = 243 cubic inches
∴ The correct answer is 243 cubic inches.

Additional Information
Right Pyramid

A 3D shape where the apex aligns directly above the geometric center of the base. In a regular right pyramid, all lateral faces are identical isosceles triangles.

Slant Height (l)

The altitude of the triangular faces on the side. For a square pyramid of base length 'a' and height 'h', the slant height is determined using the Pythagorean theorem: l = √(h2 + (a ÷ 2)2).

Total Surface Area (TSA)
TSA = Base Area + Lateral Surface Area = a2 + 2 × a × l

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 4
questions.question: A solid sphere of radius 3 cm is melted to form a right circular cone such that the height of the cone is half the radius of the cone. Find the radius of the cone.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When a solid object is melted to form another, the total volume remains conserved.

⇒ Volume of Sphere = Volume of Cone
⇒ (4/3) × π × (3)3 = (1/3) × π × r2 × (r / 2)
⇒ 4 × 27 = r3 / 2
⇒ r3 = 216 ⇒ r = 6 cm
∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Radius of the sphere
(R) = 3 cm
Let the radius of the cone be r cm.
Height of the cone (h) = r / 2

Formula Used:
Volume of Sphere = (4/3) × π × R3
Volume of Cone = (1/3) × π × r2 × h

Calculations:
⇒ Volume of Cone = Volume of Sphere
⇒ (1/3) × π × r2 × h = (4/3) × π × R3

Substituting the given values into the equation:

⇒ (1/3) × π × r2 × (r / 2) = (4/3) × π × 33

Canceling out (π / 3) from both sides of the equation:

⇒ r3 / 2 = 4 × 27
⇒ r3 / 2 = 108
⇒ r3 = 216
⇒ r = (216)1/3
⇒ r = 6 cm
∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.

Additional Information
Principle of Melting and Recasting

Whenever a 3D solid figure is melted and converted into another solid, the initial volume is exactly equal to the final volume regardless of the shape.

Total Surface Area of Cone

The total surface area of a cone involves the curved area plus the circular base area: TSA = π × r × l + π × r2, where l is the slant height.

Surface Area of Sphere

A complete sphere has a continuous curved surface with an area given by the formula: SA = 4 × π × R2.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 4
questions.question: If 15 men can do a piece of work in 12 days working 7 hours a day. How many men are needed to complete another work, which is thrice the first one, in 14 days working 9 hours a day?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the MDH rule for compound proportion directly:

(M1 × D1 × H1) / W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2) / W2
⇒ (15 × 12 × 7) / 1 = (M2 × 14 × 9) / 3
⇒ 1260 = M2 × 42
⇒ M2 = 30
∴ The correct answer is 30 men.

Alternate Method
Given:
Case 1: M1 = 15 men, D1 = 12 days, H1 = 7 hours, W1 = 1 unit
Case 2: M2 = ? men, D2 = 14 days, H2 = 9 hours, W2 = 3 units

Formula Used:
Chain Rule: (M1 × D1 × H1) / W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2) / W2

Calculations:
⇒ (15 × 12 × 7) / 1 = (M2 × 14 × 9) / 3
⇒ 1260 = (M2 × 126) / 3
⇒ 1260 = M2 × 42
⇒ M2 = 1260 ÷ 42
⇒ M2 = 30
∴ The correct answer is 30 men.

Additional Information
Chain Rule (MDH Rule)

Used when multiple variables affect the total work. Formula: (M1 × D1 × H1 × E1) / W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2 × E2) / W2, where M is Men, D is Days, H is Hours, E is Efficiency, and W is Work done or Wages earned.

Work and Wages

When multiple workers complete a job together, the total wages are divided strictly in the ratio of the actual work done by each individual. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Time and Efficiency Ratio

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work. If the efficiency ratio of person A to person B is x:y, then the ratio of time taken by them to complete the same work is y:x.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 4
questions.question: A worker covers a distance of 81 km in 11 hours. He travels partly on foot at 4.5 km/h and partly on bicycle at 15 km/h. What is the distance covered on the cycle?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
If the worker travelled the entire 11 hours on foot, the distance covered = 11 × 4.5 = 49.5 km.

Extra distance remaining to be covered = 81 − 49.5 = 31.5 km.
Difference in speeds between the cycle and foot = 15 − 4.5 = 10.5 km/h.
Time spent travelling on the cycle = 31.5 ÷ 10.5 = 3 hours.
Distance covered on the cycle = 3 × 15 = 45 km.
∴ The correct answer is 45 km.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total distance = 81 km
Total time = 11 hours
Speed on foot = 4.5 km/h
Speed on cycle = 15 km/h

Formula Used:
Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:
⇒ Let the time travelled on foot be t hours.
⇒ Time travelled on the cycle = (11 − t) hours.
⇒ Distance covered on foot + Distance covered on cycle = Total distance
⇒ (4.5 × t) + 15 × (11 − t) = 81
⇒ 4.5t + 165 − 15t = 81
⇒ 10.5t = 165 − 81
⇒ 10.5t = 84
⇒ t = 84 ÷ 10.5 = 8 hours
⇒ Time travelled on cycle = 11 − 8 = 3 hours.
⇒ Distance covered on cycle = Speed × Time = 15 × 3 = 45 km.
∴ The correct answer is 45 km.

Additional Information
Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. It represents the constant speed required to cover the whole distance in the given timeframe without any variations.

Alligation Method in Speed

When applying the cross-alligation method directly on two different speeds to obtain an average speed, the resulting ratio strictly represents the ratio of time taken, not the distance.

Shift / Minimum Value Trick

When a total value is comprised of two parts, assuming the entire operation happens at the minimum rate allows finding the specific remainder. Dividing this remainder by the unit rate difference reveals the proportion of the higher rate component.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 4
questions.question: What is the value of ((1 + sec^2 A) / (1 + cos^2 A)) × ((1 + sin^2 A) / (1 + cosec^2 A))?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Assume an angle, say A = 45°, to quickly evaluate the expression.
⇒ sec245° = 2, cos245° = 1/2, sin245° = 1/2, cosec245° = 2
⇒ Expression = [(1 + 2) ÷ (1 + 1/2)] × [(1 + 1/2) ÷ (1 + 2)]
⇒ Expression = (3 ÷ 3/2) × (3/2 ÷ 3) = 2 × 1/2 = 1
From the given options, tan245° = (1)2 = 1.
∴ The correct answer is tan2 A.

Alternate Method
Given:
Expression = [(1 + sec2A) ÷ (1 + cos2A)] × [(1 + sin2A) ÷ (1 + cosec2A)]

Formula Used:
sec A = 1 / cos A, cosec A = 1 / sin A, tan A = sin A / cos A

Calculations:
⇒ First part = (1 + 1/cos2A) ÷ (1 + cos2A)
⇒ First part = [(cos2A + 1) / cos2A] ÷ (1 + cos2A) = 1 / cos2A
⇒ Second part = (1 + sin2A) ÷ (1 + 1/sin2A)
⇒ Second part = (1 + sin2A) ÷ [(sin2A + 1) / sin2A] = sin2A
⇒ Complete Expression = (1 / cos2A) × sin2A
⇒ Expression = sin2A / cos2A = tan2A
∴ The correct answer is tan2 A.

Additional Information
Reciprocal Trigonometric Identities

Functions that are inverted forms of each other: sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ and cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ.

Quotient Identities

These identities relate tan and cot to sine and cosine: tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ and cot θ = cos θ ÷ sin θ.

Value Putting Technique

In the simplification of trigonometric expressions, substituting an angle like θ = 45° easily converts complex variables into numerals, aiding rapid elimination of wrong options.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 4
questions.question: Vinay sells an article at a profit of 20 percent. If both the cost price and selling price are reduced by Rs. 20, then the profit becomes 40 percent. What is the initial cost price?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Initial ratio of C
P : SP = 100 : 120 = 5 : 6
New ratio of C
P : SP = 100 : 140 = 5 : 7 (since both CP and SP are reduced by ₹20)
Applying the cross-multiplication method: Difference in ratio units = (5 × 7) − (5 × 6) = 5 units.
Absolute difference in value = (7 × 20) − (5 × 20) = 40.
⇒ 5 units = ₹40 (Since initial CP is exactly 5 units, Initial CP = ₹40).
∴ The correct answer is ₹40.

Alternate Method
Given:
Initial profit = 20%

Both Cost Price (CP) and Selling Price (SP) are reduced by ₹20.

New profit = 40%

Formula Used:
SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100
Initial Scenario
CP = 5x
+20% Profit
SP = 6x
− ₹20
− ₹20
New Scenario
CP = 5x − 20
+40% Profit
SP = 6x − 20
Equation: (6x − 20) = 1.4 × (5x − 20)

Calculations:
Let the initial Cost Price (CP) be 5x and Selling Price (SP) be 6x (from the 20% profit ratio of 100:120).

⇒ New CP = 5x − 20
⇒ New SP = 6x − 20

The new profit is 40%, so the ratio of new CP to new SP is 100 : 140 = 5 : 7.

⇒ (5x − 20) ÷ (6x − 20) = 5 ÷ 7
⇒ 7 × (5x − 20) = 5 × (6x − 20)
⇒ 35x − 140 = 30x − 100
⇒ 35x − 30x = 140 − 100
⇒ 5x = 40
⇒ Initial Cost Price = 5x = ₹40.
∴ The correct answer is ₹40.

Additional Information
Profit and Loss Ratios

Profit or loss is always calculated on the base of Cost Price (CP) unless specifically mentioned otherwise. Profit % = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.

Cross Multiplication Method

When two related quantities (like CP and SP) change by equal or unequal amounts, their final ratio can be determined smoothly using cross-product differences directly equated to the absolute magnitude of change.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is exclusively given on the Marked Price (MP). The relationship connecting Cost Price, Marked Price, Profit% and Discount% is MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

questions.question: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 3 cm, then its surface area increases by 156π cm^2. The radius of the sphere before the increase was:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Increase in surface area = 4π[(r + 3)2 − r2] = 156π
⇒ (r + 3)2 − r2 = 39
⇒ r2 + 6r + 9 − r2 = 39
⇒ 6r = 30 ⇒ r = 5 cm
∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Increase in radius = 3 cm
Increase in surface area = 156π cm2

Formula Used:
Surface area of a sphere = 4πr2

Calculations:
Let the original radius of the sphere be r cm.
⇒ Original surface area = 4πr2
⇒ New radius = (r + 3) cm
⇒ New surface area = 4π(r + 3)2

According to the given condition:

⇒ 4π(r + 3)2 − 4πr2 = 156π

Dividing the entire equation by 4π:

⇒ (r + 3)2 − r2 = 39
⇒ (r2 + 6r + 9) − r2 = 39
⇒ 6r + 9 = 39
⇒ 6r = 30
⇒ r = 5 cm
∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.

Additional Information
Volume of a Sphere

The volume of a sphere is given by V = (4÷3)πr3, where r is the radius.

Hemisphere Surface Area

The curved surface area of a solid hemisphere is 2πr2, and its total surface area is 3πr2.

Volume of a Hemisphere

The volume of a hemisphere is exactly half that of a full sphere, given by V = (2÷3)πr3.

questions.question: The average age of 35 children of the class is 16 years. 15 more children joined whose average age is 14 years. What is the average age of all the 50 children together?

Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of number of children = 35 : 15 = 7 : 3.
Let base average be 14 years.
Deviation of the first group from 14 = +2 years.
Net deviation per child = (7 × 2) ÷ (7 + 3) = 14 ÷ 10 = +1.4 years.
Combined Average = Base average + Net deviation = 14 + 1.4 = 15.4 years.
∴ The correct answer is 15.4 years.

Alternate Method
Given:
Number of children in group 1 = 35, Average age = 16 years.
Number of children in group 2 = 15, Average age = 14 years.

Formula Used:
Combined Average = (Total age of all groups) ÷ (Total number of members)
35 children, Avg = 16
15, Avg = 14
Combined 50 children, Avg = 15.4
Total Age = (35 × 16) + (15 × 14) = 770

Calculations:
⇒ Total age of 35 children = 35 × 16 = 560 years
⇒ Total age of 15 children = 15 × 14 = 210 years
⇒ Total age of 50 children = 560 + 210 = 770 years
⇒ Combined Average age = 770 ÷ 50
⇒ Combined Average age = 15.4 years
∴ The correct answer is 15.4 years.

Additional Information
Combined Average Formula

When two groups of sizes n1 and n2 have averages A1 and A2 respectively, their combined average is given by: A = (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Deviation Method for Averages

Assume a base average and calculate the net deviation. Combined Average = Base Average + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Items). This reduces calculation time significantly.

Weighted Average Ratio Trick

Instead of using the actual number of items, use the simplified ratio of the number of items in each group to calculate the combined average or net deviation.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: If twice the son's age (in years) is added to the age of his father, the sum is 91. If twice the age (in years) of father is added to the age of the son, the sum is 119. What is the difference (in years) between the ages of father and son?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When coefficients of variables are swapped, subtract the smaller equation from the larger one to find the difference directly.

⇒ (2F + S) − (F + 2S) = 119 − 91
⇒ F − S = 28
∴ The correct answer is 28 years.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Father's age = F years
⇒ Son's age = S years
⇒ F + 2S = 91   --- (Equation 1)
⇒ 2F + S = 119   --- (Equation 2)

Calculations:
⇒ Multiply Equation 1 by 2:
⇒ 2F + 4S = 182   --- (Equation 3)
⇒ Subtract Equation 2 from Equation 3:
⇒ (2F + 4S) − (2F + S) = 182 − 119
⇒ 3S = 63
⇒ S = 21 years
⇒ Substitute the value of S in Equation 1:
⇒ F + 2(21) = 91
⇒ F + 42 = 91
⇒ F = 91 − 42 = 49 years
⇒ Difference = F − S = 49 − 21 = 28 years
∴ The correct answer is 28 years.

Additional Information
Swapped Coefficients Rule

For equations like ax + by = c and bx + ay = d, directly adding them easily finds (x + y), and subtracting them directly finds (x − y). This heavily bypasses complex algebraic substitution steps.

Ages Problems Concept

Always assume the present age as a variable. Past ages are represented by subtraction (x − n) and future ages by addition (x + n). The difference between the ages of two people always remains constant over time.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: The length, breadth, height of a room are 6 m 40 cm, 4 m 80 cm and 3 m 20 cm respectively. Find the longest tape which can measure the dimensions of the room exactly.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
The longest tape required to measure the dimensions exactly is the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the dimensions.

Convert all dimensions to cm: 640 cm, 480 cm, 320 cm.
All numbers are clear multiples of 160: 640 = 160 × 4, 480 = 160 × 3, and 320 = 160 × 2.
HCF = 160 cm = 1 m 60 cm.
∴ The correct answer is 1 m 60 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Length of the room = 6 m 40 cm
Breadth of the room = 4 m 80 cm
Height of the room = 3 m 20 cm

Formula Used:
Longest tape = HCF of Length, Breadth, and Height
1 m = 100 cm

Calculations:
⇒ Length = 600 cm + 40 cm = 640 cm
⇒ Breadth = 400 cm + 80 cm = 480 cm
⇒ Height = 300 cm + 20 cm = 320 cm
⇒ Prime factorization of 640 = 27 × 5
⇒ Prime factorization of 480 = 25 × 3 × 5
⇒ Prime factorization of 320 = 26 × 5
⇒ HCF = 25 × 5
⇒ HCF = 32 × 5 = 160 cm
⇒ Longest tape = 160 cm = 1 m 60 cm
∴ The correct answer is 1 m 60 cm.

Additional Information
Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The HCF of given numbers is the largest number that divides all of them without leaving a remainder. It is primarily used to find the maximum possible size of identical parts.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The LCM is the smallest number that is a multiple of all given numbers. It is typically used for questions where simultaneous events or minimum repeating intervals are asked.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers A and B: LCM × HCF = A × B. Note that this specific relation is valid only for two numbers and does not apply to three or more.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: A retailer bought 50 kg of Arhar Dal at a discount of 20%. Besides 2 kg dal was freely offered to him by the wholesaler at the purchase of 50 kg. Now he sells the dal at the marked price to a customer. Find the profit percentage of the retailer?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the marked price (MP) of 1 kg dal be 10 units.
Cost Price (CP) for retailer = 50 kg × 8 units (due to 20% discount) = 400 units.
Total quantity to sell = 50 kg + 2 kg free = 52 kg.
Selling Price (SP) of 52 kg at MP = 52 × 10 units = 520 units.
Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100 = [(520 − 400) ÷ 400] × 100 = 30%.
∴ The correct answer is 30%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Quantity purchased by the retailer = 50 kg
Discount on purchase = 20%
Free quantity received = 2 kg

Retailer sells the entire dal at the marked price.

Formula Used:
Profit = Selling Price − Cost Price
Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

Calculations:
Let the marked price of 1 kg of Arhar Dal be ₹100.
⇒ Marked Price of 50 kg = 50 × 100 = ₹5000
⇒ Discount given to the retailer = 20% of 5000 = ₹1000
⇒ Cost Price (CP) for the retailer = 5000 − 1000 = ₹4000
⇒ Total quantity the retailer gets = 50 kg + 2 kg free = 52 kg
⇒ Since he sells at the marked price, Selling Price (SP) of 52 kg = 52 × 100 = ₹5200
⇒ Profit earned = SP − CP = 5200 − 4000 = ₹1200
⇒ Profit % = (1200 ÷ 4000) × 100
⇒ Profit % = 30%
∴ The correct answer is 30%.

Additional Information
Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price of an article. Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount.

Profit and Loss Calculation

Profit and Loss are strictly calculated on the total out-of-pocket Cost Price unless specified otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Buy X Get Y Free

In any promotional scheme where items are given free, the actual effective discount percentage is given by (Free Items ÷ Total Items Received) × 100.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: An inlet pipe fills up a cistern in 2 hours, while an outlet pipe empties it in 4 hours. The empty cistern was being filled up with both the pipes open for 1 hour, after which someone closed the outlet. How long will it take in total to fill up the cistern?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total capacity = LCM of 2 and 4 = 4 units.
Efficiency: Inlet = +2 units/hr, Outlet = −1 unit/hr.
Volume filled in the 1st hour (both open) = 2 − 1 = +1 unit.
Remaining capacity to be filled = 4 − 1 = 3 units.
Total time = 1 hr (initial) + (3 ÷ 2) hr (remaining filled by inlet) = 2.5 hours.
∴ The correct answer is 2 hours 30 minutes.

Alternate Method
Given:
An inlet pipe fills the cistern in 2 hours.

An outlet pipe empties the cistern in 4 hours.

Both pipes are opened together for the first 1 hour.

Calculations:
Let Total Capacity be the LCM of given times (2 and 4).

Pipe	Hours	Total Capacity	Efficiency
Inlet Pipe	2	4	4 ÷ 2 = 2
Outlet Pipe	4	4 ÷ 4 = −1
⇒ Combined efficiency of both pipes when open = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hr.
⇒ Part of the cistern filled in the 1st hour = 1 × 1 = 1 unit.
⇒ Remaining capacity to be filled = 4 − 1 = 3 units.
⇒ After 1 hour, the outlet pipe is closed, meaning only the inlet pipe operates with an efficiency of 2 units/hr.
⇒ Time taken by the inlet pipe to fill the remaining cistern = 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5 hours.
⇒ 1.5 hours is equal to 1 hour 30 minutes.
⇒ Total time taken = 1 hour (initial time) + 1 hour 30 minutes (later time) = 2 hours 30 minutes.
∴ The correct answer is 2 hours 30 minutes.

Additional Information
Pipes and Cisterns Basics

An inlet pipe fills a tank, so its work is taken as positive. An outlet pipe (or leak) empties it, so its work is taken as negative.

Net Part Filled in 1 Hour

If an inlet pipe fills a tank in x hours and an outlet pipe empties it in y hours (where y > x), the net part filled in 1 hour is (1/x) − (1/y).

Time and Work Equivalence

Pipes and cisterns problems follow the exact same rules as standard Time & Work problems. Total capacity acts as total work, and the rate of filling/emptying acts as efficiency.

questions.question: Amit borrowed a sum of ₹25,000 on simple interest. Bhola borrowed the same amount on compound interest (interest compounded yearly). At the end of 2 years, Bhola had to pay ₹160 more interest than Amit. The rate of interest charged per annum is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Difference (2 years) = P × (R / 100)2
⇒ 160 = 25000 × (R / 100)2
⇒ (R / 100)2 = 160 ÷ 25000 = 16 / 2500 = (4 / 50)2
⇒ R = (4 × 100) ÷ 50 = 8
∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Principal
(P) = ₹25,000
Time (T) = 2 years
Difference between CI and SI (D) = ₹160

Formula Used:
For 2 years, D = P × (R / 100)2

Calculations:
⇒ 160 = 25000 × (R / 100)2
⇒ 160 = 25000 × (R2 / 10000)
⇒ 160 = 2.5 × R2
⇒ R2 = 160 ÷ 2.5
⇒ R2 = 1600 ÷ 25
⇒ R2 = 64
⇒ R = √64 = 8%
∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Additional Information
Difference between CI and SI for 3 years

For 3 years, the difference between CI and SI is calculated as: D = P × (R / 100)2 × ((300 + R) / 100).

Effective Compound Interest Rate

The effective compound interest rate for 2 years is calculated using the successive percentage formula: Rate = 2R + (R2 / 100)%.

Rule of 72

To quickly estimate the number of years required to double an investment at a given annual compound interest rate, use the formula: Time ≈ 72 ÷ R.

questions.question: There are two sections A and B of a class, consisting of 48 and 60 students respectively. If the average weight of section A is 51kg and that of section B is 42 kg, find the average weight of the whole class.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of students in sections A and B = 48 : 60 = 4 : 5.
Let the assumed average be 42 kg (the lower average).
Deviation of section A from assumed average = 51 − 42 = +9 kg.
Total deviation distributed over total parts = (4 × +9) ÷ (4 + 5) = 36 ÷ 9 = +4 kg.
Combined average = 42 + 4 = 46 kg.
∴ The correct answer is 46 kg.

Alternate Method
Given:
Number of students in section A (n1) = 48, Average weight (A1) = 51 kg
Number of students in section B (n2) = 60, Average weight (A2) = 42 kg

Formula Used:
Combined Average = (n1 × A1 + n2 × A2) ÷ (n1 + n2)

51 kg
Section A
42 kg
Section B
x
Mean Avg
x − 42
51 − x
Student Ratio = 48 : 60 = 4 : 5

Calculations:
⇒ Combined Average = (48 × 51 + 60 × 42) ÷ (48 + 60)
⇒ Combined Average = (2448 + 2520) ÷ 108
⇒ Combined Average = 4968 ÷ 108 = 46 kg

Using Alligation (from diagram):

⇒ Ratio of students = (x − 42) ÷ (51 − x) = 48 ÷ 60
⇒ (x − 42) ÷ (51 − x) = 4 ÷ 5
⇒ 5 × (x − 42) = 4 × (51 − x)
⇒ 5x − 210 = 204 − 4x
⇒ 9x = 414 ⇒ x = 46 kg
∴ The correct answer is 46 kg.

Additional Information
Combined Average Formula

When two groups of sizes n1 and n2 have averages A1 and A2 respectively, their combined average is given by: A = (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Alligation Rule

It is a quick method used to find the ratio in which two groups are mixed. The ratio of the quantities is given by the cross-difference of their values from the mean average.

Net Deviation Method

A trick to minimize calculation by assuming an arbitrary average. The actual average is the assumed average plus the total net deviation divided by the total number of observations.

questions.question: John sold a watch to Sue at a gain of 20%, and Sue sold it to Rima at a profit of 10%. If Rima paid Rs. 2,178 for it, how much did John pay (in Rs.) for the watch?

Shortcut Trick

20% profit = +1/5 ⇒ Multiplier = 6/5

Initial Price × (6/5) × (11/10) = Final Price

Alternate Method
Given:

Profit% earned by Sue = 10%
Amount paid by Rima = ₹2178

Formula Used:
Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Calculations:
⇒ Let the cost price for John be x.
⇒ Selling price of John = Cost price of Sue = x × (100 + 20)/100 = 1.2x
⇒ Selling price of Sue = Cost price of Rima = 1.2x × (100 + 10)/100 = 1.32x
⇒ As Rima paid ₹2178, we can equate the values:
⇒ 1.32x = 2178
⇒ x = 2178 ÷ 1.32 = 217800 ÷ 132
⇒ x = 1650
∴ The correct answer is ₹1650.

Additional Information
Successive Profit/Loss Formula

If an article is sold successively at profits of p1% and p2%, the final price is calculated as CP × (1 + p1/100) × (1 + p2/100).

Net Effective Profit%

When two successive profits p1% and p2% are applied, the effective net profit is given by (p1 + p2 + p1p2/100)%. Here, 20 + 10 + (200/100) = 32% overall profit.

Multiplier Method

Multiplying factors streamline successive changes. A 20% gain gives a multiplier of 1.2, and a 10% gain gives 1.1. Combined multiplier = 1.2 × 1.1 = 1.32.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: A completes one-third of the work in 5 days. He is then assisted by B, and they together finish the remaining work in 6 days. B alone can complete the entire piece of work in _________.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Time to complete full work: A = 5 × 3 = 15 days, (A + B) = 6 × (3/2) = 9 days.
Total work = LCM(15, 9) = 45 units.
Efficiency: A = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 units/day, (A + B) = 45 ÷ 9 = 5 units/day.
Efficiency of B = 5 − 3 = 2 units/day.
Time taken by B alone = 45 ÷ 2 = 22.5 days.
∴ The correct answer is 22.5 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ A completes 1/3 of the work in 5 days.
⇒ Remaining work = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3.
⇒ A and B together complete the remaining 2/3 of the work in 6 days.

Calculations:
⇒ Time taken by A alone for the whole work = 5 × 3 = 15 days.
⇒ Time taken by (A + B) together for the whole work = 6 × (3/2) = 9 days.
⇒ Let the total work be the LCM of 15 and 9.

Person	Days	Total Work	Efficiency
A	15	45	45 ÷ 15 = 3
A + B	9	45 ÷ 9 = 5
⇒ Efficiency of B = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A
⇒ Efficiency of B = 5 − 3 = 2 units/day.
⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B
⇒ Time taken by B alone = 45 ÷ 2 = 22.5 days.
∴ The correct answer is 22.5 days.

Additional Information
Pipes and Cisterns

It operates on the same logic as Time and Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (filling), and outlet pipes or leaks have negative efficiency (emptying).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the exact ratio of the actual work completed by each person. If everyone works for the same number of days, the wages are divided in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

Find the total work done in a complete cycle of days (for example, 2 days if two people are alternating). Multiply the cycle to get as close to the total work as possible, and calculate the remaining work for the next turns manually.

questions.question: Ram, Shyam and Ghanshyam have ₹30, ₹40 and ₹60, respectively, with them. Their mother asks them to give her equal amounts so that the money held by them now are in continued proportion. Find the amount taken from each of them.
questions.solution:
Solution

Given:
Ram has ₹30.

Shyam has ₹40.

Ghanshyam has ₹60.

They give equal amounts to their mother such that the remaining amounts are in continued proportion.

Formula Used:
For continued proportion: a/b = b/c or b2 = a ⋅ c

Calculation:
Let the amount given by each of them to their mother be x .

Then, the remaining amounts are:

Ram: ₹(30 - x)
Shyam: ₹(40 - x)
Ghanshyam: ₹(60 - x)

For continued proportion:

(30 - x)/(40 - x) = (40 - x)/(60 - x)

By cross-multiplication:

(40 - x)2 = (30 - x) ⋅ (60 - x)

Expanding both sides:

⇒ 1600 - 80x + x2 = 30 × 60 - 30x - 60x + x2
⇒ 1600 - 80x + x2 = 1800 - 90x + x2

Cancel out x2 from both sides:

⇒ 1600 - 80x = 1800 - 90x

Simplify:

⇒ 90x - 80x = 1800 - 1600
⇒ 10x = 200
⇒ x = 20

The amount taken from each of them is ₹20.

questions.question: A candidate who scores 20% of the marks falls short by 10 marks to pass the exam, while another candidate who scores 42% of the marks surpasses the passing marks by 12%. What is the maximum number of marks?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Difference in percentage = 42% − 20% = 22%

In terms of marks, 42% is 12% of total marks above passing and 20% is 10 marks below passing.

Let maximum marks be M. Passing marks = 0.20M + 10. Also, 0.42M = (Passing marks) + 0.12M.

⇒ 0.42M − 0.12M = 0.20M + 10 ⇒ 0.30M = 0.20M + 10 ⇒ 0.10M = 10.
∴ The correct answer is 100 marks.

Alternate Method
Let maximum marks be x.
Candidate 1: Score = 20% of x = 0.20x
Passing Marks = Score + Deficit = 0.20x + 10 --- (Equation 1)
Candidate 2: Score = 42% of x = 0.42x

This score is 12% of maximum marks more than passing marks.

⇒ Passing Marks = 0.42x − 12% of x = 0.42x − 0.12x = 0.30x --- (Equation 2)

Equating Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ 0.20x + 10 = 0.30x
⇒ 0.30x − 0.20x = 10
⇒ 0.10x = 10
⇒ x = 10 / 0.10 = 100
∴ The correct answer is 100 marks.

Additional Information
Passing Percentage

It is the minimum percentage required to pass. Passing % = (Passing Marks / Maximum Marks) × 100.

Percentage Change

When comparing two scores, the difference in percentage points relates directly to the difference in actual marks via the base of Maximum Marks.

Solution
Shortcut Trick
Use the direct relation: C
P : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)
C

Relationship between CP and MP

Effective Discount

questions.question: The distance between two stations A and B is 700 km. A train covers the journey from A to B at a speed of 80 km/h and returns back to A with a uniform speed of 65 km/h. The average speed of train during the whole journey, is closest to:

Solution

Given:
Distance between A and B = 700 km
Speed of train from A to B = 80 km/h
Speed of train from B to A = 65 km/h

Concept used:

Distance = Speed × Time
Average speed = Total distance travelled/Total time taken

Calculation:
Time taken by train from A to B = Distance/Speed = 700/80
Time taken by train from B to A = 700/65
Average speed during the whole journey = Total distance/Total time
⇒ (700 + 700)/[(700/80 + 700/65)]
⇒ (700 + 700)/[700 × (1/80 + 1/65)]
⇒ (2 × 700)/[700 × (13 + 16)/1040]
⇒ 2/(29/1040)
⇒ (1040 × 2)/29 = 71.72 km/h
∴ The average speed of the train during the whole journey is 71.72 km/h.

Shortcut Trick
If the distance travelled in both the cases is same, then we can apply this formula,

Average speed = (2 × product of the two speeds)/(Sum of the two speeds)
⇒ (2 × 80 × 65)/(80 + 65)
⇒ 10400/145 = 71.72 km/h
∴ The average speed of the train during the whole journey is 71.72 km/h.

questions.question: The LCM and HCF of two positive numbers are 96 and 8, respectively. If the sum of the numbers is 56, then the difference between the numbers is:
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Let the numbers be 8x and 8y, where x and y are co-prime.
Product of ratios (x × y) = LCM ÷ HCF = 96 ÷ 8 = 12.
Sum of ratios (x + y) = Sum ÷ HCF = 56 ÷ 8 = 7.

Find two numbers that multiply to 12 and add to 7 → 3 and 4.

Difference between numbers = HCF × (x − y) = 8 × (4 − 3) = 8.
∴ The correct answer is 8.

Alternate Method
Given:
LCM = 96, HCF = 8, Sum (a + b) = 56.

Formula Used:
Product of two numbers (a × b) = LCM × HCF
Algebraic identity: (a − b)2 = (a + b)2 − 4ab

Calculations:
⇒ Product (ab) = 96 × 8 = 768
⇒ Sum (a + b) = 56
⇒ (a − b)2 = (56)2 − 4 × (768)
⇒ (a − b)2 = 3136 − 3072
⇒ (a − b)2 = 64
⇒ (a − b) = √64 = 8
∴ The correct answer is 8.

Additional Information
Product Rule of HCF and LCM

For any two positive integers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

Co-prime Factors Property

If HCF of two numbers is h, the numbers can be written as hx and hy, where LCM = h × x × y and gcd(x, y) = 1.

Difference and Sum Relationship

The relationship between sum and difference is given by the identity (a + b)2 − (a − b)2 = 4ab.

questions.question: The income of A is 40% more than the income of B, and the income of C is 30% less than the total incomes of A and B. The income of A is what per cent less than the income of C?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Let Income of B = 100
Income of A = 140 (40% more than B)
Income of C = 70% of (140 + 100) = 0.7 × 240 = 168
Difference between C and A = 168 − 140 = 28
Required % = (28 ÷ 168) × 100 = 1/6 × 100 = 16(2/3)%
∴ The correct answer is 16(2/3)%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Income of A = 1.4 × Income of B
Income of C = 0.7 × (Income of A + Income of B)

Calculations:
⇒ Let Income of B = 100 units
⇒ Income of A = 100 + 40% of 100 = 140 units
⇒ Total Income of A + B = 140 + 100 = 240 units
⇒ Income of C = 240 − 30% of 240 = 240 − 72 = 168 units
⇒ Difference between C and A = 168 − 140 = 28 units
⇒ Percentage less = (Difference ÷ Income of C) × 100
⇒ Percentage less = (28 ÷ 168) × 100 = (1 ÷ 6) × 100 = 16.66%
∴ The correct answer is 16(2/3)%.

Additional Information
Percentage Comparison

To find what percent X is less than Y, use the formula: [(Y − X) ÷ Y] × 100.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

Common fractions like 1/6 are equivalent to 16.66% or 16(2/3)%, which helps in faster calculation during exams.

Base Value Selection

Always assume the base value (usually 100) for the variable that other variables are compared to (in this case, B).

questions.question: If the 11-digit number 79x6402087y is divisible by 72, then for smallest value of x, what is the value of (x + 2y)?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
For a number to be divisible by 72, it must be perfectly divisible by both 8 and 9.

Rule of 8: The last three digits (87y) must be divisible by 8 ⇒ 872 is divisible by 8, so y = 2.
Rule of 9: The sum of digits (45 + x) must be divisible by 9 ⇒ The smallest possible value for x is 0.
Required value = (x + 2y) = 0 + 2 × 2 = 4.
∴ The correct answer is 4.

Alternate Method
Given:
The 11-digit number 79x6402087y is divisible by 72.

Method Used:

If a number is divisible by 72, it must be divisible by its co-prime factors 8 and 9.

Divisibility rule of 8: The number formed by the last three digits must be divisible by 8.
Divisibility rule of 9: The sum of all the digits must be divisible by 9.

Calculations:
⇒ Consider the last 3 digits for divisibility by 8: 87y
⇒ 87y = 800 + 70 + y
⇒ 800 is perfectly divisible by 8, so (70 + y) must also be divisible by 8.
⇒ The closest multiple of 8 to 70 is 72, which gives y = 2.
⇒ So, y = 2. The number now becomes 79x64020872.
⇒ Now, apply the divisibility rule of 9 to the entire number.
⇒ Sum of digits = 7 + 9 + x + 6 + 4 + 0 + 2 + 0 + 8 + 7 + 2
⇒ Sum of digits = 45 + x
⇒ For (45 + x) to be divisible by 9, x can either be 0 or 9 (since 45 is a multiple of 9).
⇒ Since we need the smallest value of x, we take x = 0.
⇒ We need to find the final value of (x + 2y).
⇒ (x + 2y) = 0 + 2 × 2
⇒ (x + 2y) = 4
∴ The correct answer is 4.

Additional Information
Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is perfectly divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 9.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Co-prime Divisibility Theorem

If a number is divisible by two co-prime numbers a and b, it is always divisible by their product (a × b). For example, 72 = 8 × 9.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: If α + θ = 7π/12 and tan θ = √3, then the value of tan α is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Given, tan θ = √3 ⇒ θ = π/3
It is given that α + θ = 7π/12
⇒ α = 7π/12 − π/3 = 7π/12 − 4π/12 = 3π/12 = π/4
Now, tan α = tan(π/4) = 1
∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method
Given:
α + θ = 7π / 12
tan θ = √3

Calculations:
⇒ tan θ = √3
⇒ θ = 60° (since tan 60° = √3)
We know that π radians = 180°
⇒ Total Angle = 7π / 12 = (7 × 180°) ÷ 12 = 105°

Substitute the value of θ in the given equation:

⇒ α + 60° = 105°
⇒ α = 105° − 60°
⇒ α = 45°

We need to find the value of tan α:

⇒ tan α = tan 45° = 1
∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information
Radian to Degree Conversion

To convert an angle from radians to degrees, multiply the value by 180° ÷ π. Conversely, to convert from degrees to radians, multiply by π ÷ 180°.

Compound Angle Formula

The tangent of the sum of two angles is expressed as: tan(A + B) = (tan A + tan B) ÷ (1 − tan A × tan B).

Standard Trigonometric Values

Some frequently used tangent values are: tan(30°) = 1 ÷ √3, tan(45°) = 1, and tan(60°) = √3.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle. Find the ratio of area of circle to the area of that portion which is not covered by the hexagon?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Radius of circumcircle = side of inscribed regular hexagon = r
Area of circle = πr2
Area of regular hexagon = (3√3/2)r2
Uncovered Area = πr2 − (3√3/2)r2 = r2(2π − 3√3) / 2
Ratio = Area of circle ÷ Uncovered Area = 2π / (2π − 3√3)
∴ The correct answer is 2π/(2π − 3√3).

Alternate Method
Given:
A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle.

Formula Used:
Area of a circle = πr2
Area of a regular hexagon = 6 × (√3 / 4)a2 (where a is the side length)

For a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle, the side length (a) equals the radius (r).

O
r
Shaded blue region = Area not covered by hexagon

Calculations:
⇒ Let the radius of the circle be r.
⇒ Side of the inscribed regular hexagon = r
⇒ Area of the circle = πr2
⇒ Area of the hexagon = 6 × (√3 / 4)r2 = (3√3 / 2)r2
⇒ Area not covered by hexagon = Area of circle − Area of hexagon
⇒ Area not covered = πr2 − (3√3 / 2)r2
⇒ Area not covered = r2(2π − 3√3) / 2
⇒ Required Ratio = (Area of circle) ÷ (Area not covered)
⇒ Ratio = πr2 ÷ [r2(2π − 3√3) / 2]
⇒ Ratio = 2π / (2π − 3√3)
∴ The correct answer is 2π/(2π − 3√3).

Additional Information
Circumcircle of a Regular Hexagon

The circumcenter and incenter of a regular hexagon coincide. The radius of the circumscribed circle is exactly equal to the side length of the hexagon (R = a).

Incircle of a Regular Hexagon

The radius of a circle inscribed inside a regular hexagon is given by r = (a√3)/2. The ratio of the area of the circumcircle to the incircle is 4:3.

Area of an Equilateral Triangle

A regular hexagon is composed of exactly 6 identical equilateral triangles. The area of one such triangle with side a is (√3 / 4)a2.
