questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: The whole surface area of a pyramid whose base is a regular polygon is 260 cm^2 and the area of its base is 120 cm^2. The area of each lateral face is 20 cm^2. Then the number of lateral faces is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total Lateral Surface Area = Total Surface Area − Base Area
⇒ Total Lateral Area = 260 − 120 = 140 cm2
Number of Lateral Faces = Total Lateral Area ÷ Area of each lateral face
⇒ Number of faces = 140 ÷ 20 = 7
∴ The correct answer is 7.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total surface area of the pyramid = 260 cm2
Area of its base = 120 cm2
Area of each lateral face = 20 cm2

Formula Used:
Total Surface Area = Base Area + (Number of lateral faces × Area of each lateral face)

Calculations:
Let the number of lateral faces be n.
⇒ 260 = 120 + (n × 20)
⇒ n × 20 = 260 − 120
⇒ 20n = 140
⇒ n = 140 ÷ 20
⇒ n = 7
∴ The correct answer is 7.

Additional Information
Volume of a Pyramid

The volume of a pyramid is one-third of the product of its base area and perpendicular height. Formula: V = (1 ÷ 3) × Base Area × Height.

Lateral Surface Area (Regular Pyramid)

It is the total area of all its lateral faces. For a regular pyramid: LSA = (1 ÷ 2) × Perimeter of Base × Slant Height.

Euler's Formula for Polyhedra

For any convex polyhedron, the number of faces (F), vertices (V), and edges (E) are related by the formula: F + V − E = 2.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: A thief was spotted by a policeman from a distance of 225 metres. When the policeman started the chase, the thief also started running. If the speed of the thief was 11 km/h and that of the policeman was 13 km/h, how far would the thief have run, before the policeman caught up with him?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When the time taken by both moving objects is constant, the ratio of the distance covered is equal to the ratio of their speeds.

Speed ratio (Thief : Policeman) = 11 : 13
Distance ratio (Thief : Policeman) = 11 : 13
Difference in distance covered = 13 parts − 11 parts = 2 parts
Given the initial distance difference is 225 m ⇒ 2 parts = 225 m ⇒ 1 part = 112.5 m
Distance run by the thief = 11 parts = 11 × 112.5 = 1237.5 metres
∴ The correct answer is 1237.5 metres.

Alternate Method
Given:
Initial distance between policeman and thief = 225 m
Speed of thief = 11 km/h
Speed of policeman = 13 km/h

Formula Used:
Relative speed (same direction) = Speed1 − Speed2
Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed
Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:
⇒ Relative speed = 13 − 11 = 2 km/h
⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 2 × (5/18) = 5/9 m/s
⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 225 ÷ (5/9)
⇒ Time taken = 225 × (9/5) = 45 × 9 = 405 seconds
⇒ Speed of thief in m/s = 11 × (5/18) = 55/18 m/s
⇒ Distance covered by thief before getting caught = Speed of thief × Time taken
⇒ Distance = (55/18) × 405 = 55 × 22.5
⇒ Distance = 1237.5 m
∴ The correct answer is 1237.5 metres.

Additional Information
Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: S = S1 − S2.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies are moving in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: S = S1 + S2.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: The ratio of the outer and the inner circumference of a circular path is 17 ∶ 15. If path is 40 metres wide, then what is the radius of the inner circle?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
The ratio of circumferences of two circles is identical to the ratio of their radii.

Ratio of outer radius
(R) to inner radius (r) = 17 ∶ 15
Width of the path in ratio units = 17 − 15 = 2 units.
Given width = 40 metres, so 2 units = 40 metres ⇒ 1 unit = 20 metres.
Inner radius = 15 units = 15 × 20 = 300 metres.
∴ The correct answer is 300 metres.

Alternate Method
Given:
Ratio of outer and inner circumference = 17 ∶ 15
Width of the path = 40 metres

Formula Used:
Circumference of a circle = 2×π×r
Width of circular path = R − r

Calculations:
⇒ Let the outer radius be R and the inner radius be r.
⇒ Ratio of circumferences = (2×π×R) ÷ (2×π×r)
⇒ R / r = 17 / 15
⇒ Let R = 17x and r = 15x
⇒ Width of the circular path = Outer Radius − Inner Radius
⇒ 17x − 15x = 40
⇒ 2x = 40
⇒ x = 20
⇒ Inner radius (r) = 15x = 15 × 20 = 300 metres
∴ The correct answer is 300 metres.

Additional Information
Area of a Circular Path

The total area located strictly between two concentric circles is given by Area = π×(R2 − r2), where R and r are the respective outer and inner radii.

Length of an Arc

An arc is a fraction of the full circumference. The length is determined by the central angle θ: (θ ÷ 360) × 2πr.

Area of a Sector

The region bounded by two radii and an adjoining arc is called a sector. Its area is: (θ ÷ 360) × πr2.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: Three friends A, B, C invested in a business in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 6. After 6 months C withdraw half his capital. If the total profit earned for the year is Rs. 53010, then profit made by A is (in Rs.):
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Profit ratio = (Capital × Time)
A : B : C = (3 × 12) : (2 × 12) : (6 × 6 + 3 × 6)
⇒ A : B : C = 36 : 24 : 54 = 6 : 4 : 9
Total profit = 19 parts = ₹53010 ⇒ 1 part = ₹2790
A's profit = 6 parts = 6 × 2790 = ₹16740
∴ The correct answer is ₹16740.

Alternate Method
Given:
Ratio of initial investments of A, B and C = 3 : 2 : 6

C withdraws half of his capital after 6 months.

Total profit for the year = ₹53010

Formula Used:
Profit Ratio = Product of Capital and Time Period

Calculations:
⇒ Equivalent capital for A = 3 × 12 = 36 units
⇒ Equivalent capital for B = 2 × 12 = 24 units
⇒ Equivalent capital for C = (6 × 6) + (3 × 6) = 36 + 18 = 54 units
⇒ Ratio of profits (A : B : C) = 36 : 24 : 54
⇒ Simplified profit ratio = 6 : 4 : 9
⇒ Total ratio parts = 6 + 4 + 9 = 19
⇒ A's share = (6 ÷ 19) × Total Profit
⇒ A's share = (6 ÷ 19) × 53010
⇒ A's share = 6 × 2790 = 16740
∴ The correct answer is ₹16740.

Additional Information
Partnership Profit Sharing

Profit is distributed directly in proportion to the product of capital invested and the time duration of the investment. Ratio = C1T1 : C2T2.

Active vs Sleeping Partner

An active partner manages the business and receives a fixed salary or percentage of the total profit. The remaining profit is divided among all partners based on their capital-time ratio.

Capital Adjustments Mid-Year

When capital is added or withdrawn midway, the effective capital is found by calculating (Capital × Time) for each phase independently and summing them up.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: The average salary of the entire staff in an office is Rs. 130 per month. The average salary of officers is Rs. 450 and that of non-officers is Rs. 120. If the number of officers is 15, then find the number of non-officers in the office?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the method of Alligation:

Ratio of Officers to Non-officers = (130 − 120) : (450 − 130)
Ratio = 10 : 320 = 1 : 32
Given 1 ratio unit = 15 officers, then 32 ratio units = 15 × 32 = 480 non-officers.
∴ The correct answer is 480 non-officers.

Alternate Method
Given:
Average salary of overall staff = Rs. 130
Average salary of officers = Rs. 450
Average salary of non-officers = Rs. 120
Number of officers = 15

Formula Used:
Overall Average = (Total salary of all staff) ÷ (Total number of staff)
Officers: 450
Non-Off: 120
130
130 − 120 = 10
450 − 130 = 320
Ratio → 10 : 320 = 1 : 32

Calculations:
Let the number of non-officers be x.
⇒ Total salary of officers = 450 × 15 = 6750
⇒ Total salary of non-officers = 120 × x = 120x
⇒ Total staff members = 15 + x
⇒ Overall Average = (6750 + 120x) ÷ (15 + x)
⇒ 130 = (6750 + 120x) ÷ (15 + x)
⇒ 130 × (15 + x) = 6750 + 120x
⇒ 1950 + 130x = 6750 + 120x
⇒ 130x − 120x = 6750 − 1950
⇒ 10x = 4800
⇒ x = 480
∴ The correct answer is 480 non-officers.

Additional Information
Weighted Average

Used when calculating the combined average of groups with different sizes. Formula: Aw = (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Rule of Alligation

A rapid visual method to find the ratio in which two groups with different averages are mixed to yield a desired overall combined average.

Average & Net Deviation

The sum of the net deviations of all individual values from their mean is always equal to zero, which is a useful property to solve unknown value problems quickly.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: A cylindrical hole with the radius of its base given as 3.5 cm is made in a solid cube each of whose edge is 14 cm. Find the total surface area (in cm²) of the cube with the hole. [Use π = 22/7]
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When a hole is drilled completely through a solid, the net Total Surface Area (TSA) is:

Net TSA = (TSA of Cube) − (2 × Base Area of Hole) + (Curved Surface Area of Hole)
Net TSA = 6a2 − 2πr2 + 2πrh
Net TSA = 6 × 142 − 2 × (22/7) × (3.5)2 + 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 14
Net TSA = 1176 − 77 + 308 = 1407 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 1407 cm2.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Edge of the solid cube (a) = 14 cm
⇒ Radius of the cylindrical hole (r) = 3.5 cm
⇒ Height of the cylindrical hole (h) = Edge of cube = 14 cm

Formula Used:
⇒ Total Surface Area = (TSA of solid cube) − (2 × Area of circular bases of hole) + (CSA of cylindrical hole)
⇒ TSA = 6a2 − 2πr2 + 2πrh

Calculations:
⇒ TSA of cube = 6 × 14 × 14 = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm2
⇒ Area of 2 circular bases = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 = 77 cm2
⇒ CSA of cylindrical hole = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 14 = 308 cm2
⇒ Total Surface Area = 1176 − 77 + 308 = 1407 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 1407 cm2.

Additional Information
Effect of Drilling a Hole on Surface Area

When a hole is drilled completely through a solid, the flat surface area corresponding to the base cuts is lost, but the newly created inner curved surface is exposed and must be added to the total area.

Important Formulas for a Cube

Volume = a3 | Total Surface Area = 6a2 | Length of Body Diagonal = a√3.

Important Formulas for a Cylinder

Volume = πr2h | Curved Surface Area = 2πrh | Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: The radii of the two concentric circles are 27 cm and 18 cm. The area (in cm²) of the closed figure bounded by the boundaries of the circle is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Area of a circular ring = π × (R − r) × (R + r)
Substitute R = 27 and r = 18 into the formula:
⇒ Area = π × (27 − 18) × (27 + 18)
⇒ Area = π × 9 × 45
⇒ Area = 405π
∴ The correct answer is 405π cm2.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Outer radius of the circle
(R) = 27 cm
⇒ Inner radius of the circle (r) = 18 cm

Formula Used:
⇒ Area of the bounded region (Ring) = Area of outer circle − Area of inner circle
⇒ Area = πR2 − πr2 = π(R2 − r2)

Calculations:
⇒ Area = π × (27)2 − π × (18)2
⇒ Area = π × (729 − 324)
⇒ Area = 405π
∴ The correct answer is 405π cm2.

Additional Information
Concentric Circles

Concentric circles are circles that share the exact same center point but have different radii. The region enclosed between two concentric circles is often referred to as an annulus or a circular ring.

Width of the Circular Ring

The thickness or width of the ring is uniformly distributed and can be calculated by subtracting the inner radius from the outer radius: Width = R − r.

Algebraic Identities

When solving questions involving the difference of squares, applying the algebraic identity a2 − b2 = (a − b)(a + b) will severely reduce the calculation time and prevent squaring large values.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: The simple interest on a sum of money is 9/45 of the sum. If the number of years is numerically 5 times of rate per cent per annum, then find the rate per cent per annum.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Effective Rate % over the entire period = (SI ÷ P) × 100
Rate × Time = (9 ÷ 45) × 100
Given Time (T) = 5R, we substitute T directly:
R × 5R = (1 ÷ 5) × 100
5R2 = 20 ⇒ R2 = 4 ⇒ R = 2
∴ The correct answer is 2%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Simple Interest (SI) = 9/45 of Principal
(P) = P / 5
Time (T) = 5 × Rate
(R)

Formula Used:
Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:
⇒ P / 5 = (P × R × 5R) ÷ 100

Dividing both sides by
P:

⇒ 1 / 5 = 5R2 / 100
⇒ 1 / 5 = R2 / 20
⇒ R2 = 20 / 5
⇒ R2 = 4
⇒ R = √4 = 2
∴ The correct answer is 2%.

Additional Information
Simple Interest (SI) Basics

Simple interest is charged only on the initial principal for the entire duration. The formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Important Variation Formulas

Principal
(P) = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T) | Time (T) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × R)

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

SI grows linearly over time, whereas Compound Interest (CI) grows exponentially because interest is calculated on both the principal and the accumulated interest.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: If P sin 60° = Q cosec 45°, then the value of (P^2 + Q^2) / (P^2 - Q^2) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
From the given equation: P/Q = cosec 45° ÷ sin 60° = √2 ÷ (√3/2) = 2√2/√3
Squaring both sides gives: P2/Q2 = 8/3

Applying the Componendo and Dividendo rule directly:

(P2 + Q2) / (P2 − Q2) = (8 + 3) / (8 − 3) = 11/5
∴ The correct answer is 11/5.

Alternate Method
Given:
P sin 60° = Q cosec 45°

Concept Used:

Standard trigonometric values: sin 60° = √3/2 and cosec 45° = √2

Calculations:
⇒ P × (√3/2) = Q × √2
⇒ P/Q = √2 ÷ (√3/2)
⇒ P/Q = (2√2) / √3

Squaring both sides of the equation:

⇒ P2/Q2 = (2√2)2 / (√3)2
⇒ P2/Q2 = 8/3
Let P2 = 8k and Q2 = 3k. Substituting these into the required expression:
⇒ (P2 + Q2) / (P2 − Q2)
⇒ (8k + 3k) / (8k − 3k)
⇒ 11k / 5k
⇒ 11/5
∴ The correct answer is 11/5.

Additional Information
Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If a/b = c/d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This property is highly useful for simplifying algebraic equations and expressions involving the sum and difference of terms.

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

It is essential to remember key angle values: sin 30° = 1/2, sin 45° = 1/√2, and sin 60° = √3/2. The cosecant function is the reciprocal of sine, meaning cosec θ = 1 / sin θ.

Basic Pythagorean Identities

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1 | 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ | 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: P drives a car for 5 hours and after every hour he doubles the speed. In the fifth hour, his speed is 128 km/h. What is his average speed of the journey in km/h?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When time intervals are equal, Average Speed = Arithmetic mean of all speeds.

The speeds for the 5 hours form a geometric sequence ending in 128: 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 km/h.

Sum of speeds = 8 + 16 + 32 + 64 + 128 = 248 km/h.
Average Speed = 248 ÷ 5 = 49.6 km/h.
∴ The correct answer is 49.6 km/h.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total time taken for the journey = 5 hours
Speed in the 5th hour = 128 km/h

The speed doubles after every hour.

Formula Used:
Distance = Speed × Time
Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Calculations:
Let the speed in the 1st hour be v km/h.
Speeds in consecutive hours follow the pattern: 2v, 4v, 8v, 16v.
⇒ Speed in the 5th hour = 16v = 128
⇒ v = 128 ÷ 16 = 8 km/h

The distance covered in each 1-hour interval is numerically equal to the speed:

⇒ Distance in 1st hour = 8 × 1 = 8 km
⇒ Distance in 2nd hour = 16 × 1 = 16 km
⇒ Distance in 3rd hour = 32 × 1 = 32 km
⇒ Distance in 4th hour = 64 × 1 = 64 km
⇒ Distance in 5th hour = 128 × 1 = 128 km
⇒ Total Distance = 8 + 16 + 32 + 64 + 128 = 248 km
⇒ Average Speed = 248 ÷ 5 = 49.6 km/h
∴ The correct answer is 49.6 km/h.

Additional Information
Average Speed

Average speed is defined as the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. It is not the simple average of individual speeds unless the time intervals for each speed are strictly equal.

Equal Time Intervals Rule

If an object travels at different speeds v1, v2, ..., vn for equal durations of time, the average speed is simply the arithmetic mean of all the speeds: (v1 + v2 + ... + vn) ÷ n.

Geometric Progression (GP)

A sequence of numbers where each term after the first is found by multiplying the previous one by a fixed, non-zero number (common ratio). The sum of a GP is computed as Sn = a(rn − 1) ÷ (r − 1) for r > 1.
questions.conceptTested: Average speed for equal time intervals is the arithmetic mean of individual speeds, combined with geometric progression.

questions.question: A square pyramid with side 10 cm has a volume of 400 cm^3. Find the total surface area of the pyramid.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Volume = 1/3 × a2 × h ⇒ 400 = 1/3 × 100 × h ⇒ h = 12 cm.
Slant height l = √(h2 + (a/2)2) = √(122 + 52) = 13 cm.
Total Surface Area (TSA) = Base Area + Lateral Surface Area
⇒ TSA = a2 + 2al
⇒ TSA = 102 + 2 × 10 × 13 = 100 + 260 = 360 cm2.
∴ The correct answer is 360 cm2.

Alternate Method
Given:
Base side (a) = 10 cm
Volume (V) = 400 cm3

Formula Used:
Volume = 1/3 × a2 × h
Slant height (l) = √(h2 + (a/2)2)
Total Surface Area = a2 + 2al

Calculations:
⇒ 400 = 1/3 × 102 × h
⇒ 400 = 1/3 × 100 × h
⇒ h = (400 × 3) ÷ 100
⇒ h = 12 cm
Now, finding the slant height (l):
⇒ l = √(122 + (10/2)2)
⇒ l = √(144 + 25)
⇒ l = √169 = 13 cm
Now, finding the Total Surface Area (TSA):
⇒ TSA = (10)2 + 2 × 10 × 13
⇒ TSA = 100 + 260
⇒ TSA = 360 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 360 cm2.

Additional Information
Volume of a Pyramid

The volume of any pyramid is defined as exactly one-third of the volume of the corresponding prism: V = 1/3 × Base Area × Height.

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

For a regular pyramid, the lateral surface area is formed by identical isosceles triangles: LSA = 1/2 × Perimeter of Base × Slant Height.

Euler's Formula for Polyhedrons

For any solid polyhedron (like a pyramid), the number of Faces (F), Vertices (V), and Edges (E) are related by the formula: F + V = E + 2.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: Two trains start at the same time from Bangalore and Chennai and proceed towards each other at the speeds of 80 km/h and 95 km/h. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 180 km more than the other. The distance between Bangalore and Chennai is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When time is constant, Distance ∝ Speed.

Difference in Speed = 95 − 80 = 15 km/h.
Total Speed = 95 + 80 = 175 km/h.
Total Distance = (Total Speed ÷ Difference in Speed) × Difference in Distance
Total Distance = (175 ÷ 15) × 180 = 175 × 12 = 2100 km.
∴ The correct answer is 2100 km.

Alternate Method
Given:
Speed of first train = 80 km/h
Speed of second train = 95 km/h
Difference in distance travelled at meeting time = 180 km

Formula Used:
Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:
⇒ Let the time taken for both trains to meet be t hours.
⇒ Distance covered by first train = 80 × t
⇒ Distance covered by second train = 95 × t
⇒ The difference in distance covered = 95t − 80t = 15t
⇒ 15t = 180
⇒ t = 180 ÷ 15 = 12 hours
⇒ Total distance between Bangalore and Chennai = 80t + 95t = 175t
⇒ Total distance = 175 × 12
⇒ Total distance = 2100 km
∴ The correct answer is 2100 km.

Additional Information
Relative Speed (Opposite Directions)

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S1 + S2).

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (|S1 − S2|).

Constant Time Property

If two objects travel for the exact same amount of time, the ratio of distances they cover is equal to the ratio of their respective speeds (D1 ÷ D2 = S1 ÷ S2).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: Rs. 1092 is divided among 2 men, 6 women and 8 boys so that the share of a man, a woman and a boy are in the ratio 3 ∶ 2 ∶ 1. Then, how much does a man get? (In Rs.)
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total equivalent ratio units = (2 × 3) + (6 × 2) + (8 × 1) = 6 + 12 + 8 = 26 units.
Value of 26 units = ₹1092.
Value of 1 unit = 1092 ÷ 26 = ₹42.
Share of 1 man = 3 units = 3 × 42 = ₹126.
∴ The correct answer is ₹126.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total amount to be divided = ₹1092
Number of people = 2 men, 6 women, and 8 boys
Ratio of individual shares (1 Man : 1 Woman : 1 Boy) = 3 : 2 : 1

Calculations:
Let the share of 1 man, 1 woman, and 1 boy be 3x, 2x, and 1x respectively.
⇒ Total share of 2 men = 2 × 3x = 6x
⇒ Total share of 6 women = 6 × 2x = 12x
⇒ Total share of 8 boys = 8 × 1x = 8x
⇒ Total amount distributed = 6x + 12x + 8x = 26x
⇒ 26x = 1092
⇒ x = 1092 ÷ 26 = 42
⇒ Share of a man = 3x = 3 × 42 = 126
∴ The correct answer is ₹126.

Additional Information
Amount Distribution

When dividing a total amount among different groups of people, always multiply the individual share ratio by the number of people in each group to find the overall ratio in which the total sum is split.

Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are multiplied together, it is known as a compound ratio. For a : b and c : d, the compound ratio is (a × c) : (b × d).

Proportion

Four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion if a : b = c : d, which means the product of the extremes equals the product of the means (a × d = b × c).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: Two individuals, A and B, have rented a field. A places 12 horses for 5 months and 20 sheep for 4 months. B places 15 cows for 6 months and 30 sheep for 3 months. If 3 horses consume the same food as 5 cows and 6 cows consume the same food as 10 sheep, find what portion of the rent A should pay?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Convert all animals to Cows (C) to find the total equivalent consumption ratio.

Given 3H = 5C ⇒ 1H = 5/3 C, and 10S = 6C ⇒ 1S = 3/5 C.
A's usage = [12 × (5/3) × 5] + [20 × (3/5) × 4] = 100 + 48 = 148 cow-months.
B's usage = (15 × 6) + [30 × (3/5) × 3] = 90 + 54 = 144 cow-months.
Ratio of rent A : B = 148 : 144 = 37 : 36.
∴ The correct answer is 37/73.

Alternate Method
Given:
A places 12 horses for 5 months and 20 sheep for 4 months.

B places 15 cows for 6 months and 30 sheep for 3 months.

3 horses consume same as 5 cows, and 6 cows consume same as 10 sheep.

Formula Used:
Rent Share Ratio = (Number of animals × Time × Consumption rate)

Calculations:
⇒ Let us convert the number of all animals into equivalent number of Cows (C) for simplicity.
⇒ 3 Horses = 5 Cows ⇒ 1 Horse = 5/3 Cows
⇒ 10 Sheep = 6 Cows ⇒ 1 Sheep = 3/5 Cows
⇒ Equivalent animals placed by A in terms of cows:
⇒ 12 Horses = 12 × (5/3) = 20 Cows
⇒ 20 Sheep = 20 × (3/5) = 12 Cows
⇒ Total equivalent consumption by A = (20 Cows × 5 months) + (12 Cows × 4 months)
⇒ A's total units = 100 + 48 = 148 cow-months
⇒ Equivalent animals placed by B in terms of cows:
⇒ 15 Cows = 15 Cows
⇒ 30 Sheep = 30 × (3/5) = 18 Cows
⇒ Total equivalent consumption by B = (15 Cows × 6 months) + (18 Cows × 3 months)
⇒ B's total units = 90 + 54 = 144 cow-months
⇒ Ratio of rent (A : B) = 148 : 144
⇒ Simplifying by dividing both terms by 4, Ratio = 37 : 36
⇒ Portion of rent A should pay = A's share ÷ (A's share + B's share)
⇒ A's portion = 37 ÷ (37 + 36) = 37/73
∴ The correct answer is 37/73.

Additional Information
Partnership Rent Rule

When multiple people rent a common property (like a pasture), the rent paid by each person is directly proportional to the number of resources used multiplied by the duration of usage (Rent ≈ Animals × Time).

Compound Ratio Equivalency

If distinct categories are given (like Horses, Cows, and Sheep), establish a single common base unit by utilizing equivalent ratios. Converting all distinct variables into one unified variable simplifies compound calculations.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: Mohan can complete the work in 28 days, and Rohan can complete the work in 56 days, if Sohan is 60% more efficient than Rohan then in how many days Mohan and Sohan can complete the 90% of the work?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let Total Work = LCM(28, 56) = 56 units.
Efficiency of Mohan = 56 ÷ 28 = 2 units/day, and Rohan = 56 ÷ 56 = 1 unit/day.

Sohan is 60% more efficient than Rohan, so Sohan's efficiency = 1 × 1.6 = 1.6 units/day.

Combined efficiency of Mohan and Sohan = 2 + 1.6 = 3.6 units/day.
Time = (90% of Total Work) ÷ (Combined Efficiency) = 50.4 ÷ 3.6 = 14 days.
∴ The correct answer is 14 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
Time taken by Mohan to complete the work = 28 days
Time taken by Rohan to complete the work = 56 days

Sohan is 60% more efficient than Rohan.

Formula Used:
Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:
Let Total Work be the LCM of the time taken by Mohan and Rohan.

Person	Days	Total Work	Efficiency
Mohan	28	56	2
Rohan	56	1

⇒ Efficiency of Rohan = 1 unit/day
⇒ Sohan's efficiency = Rohan's efficiency + 60% of Rohan's efficiency
⇒ Sohan's efficiency = 1 + 0.6 = 1.6 units/day
⇒ Combined efficiency of Mohan and Sohan = 2 + 1.6 = 3.6 units/day
⇒ Work to be completed = 90% of Total Work = (90 ÷ 100) × 56 = 50.4 units
⇒ Time taken by Mohan and Sohan = Work to be completed ÷ Combined Efficiency
⇒ Time taken = 50.4 ÷ 3.6 = 14 days
∴ The correct answer is 14 days.

Additional Information
Work and Efficiency Ratio

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If a person is x% more efficient, their time taken will be proportionally less. Ratio of efficiency = 100 : (100 + x).

Combined Work Rule

When multiple people work together, their one-day work (efficiency) is simply added up. The total time taken to complete a specific task is derived by Total Target Work ÷ Sum of their individual efficiencies.

questions.question:
What will be the difference between mean and median of the given data?
21, 11, 27, 8, 5, 12, 7, 23, 3, 14, 9, 19
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Mean of the given data = Sum of data ÷ Total numbers = 159 ÷ 12 = 13.25
Arranging data in ascending order: 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 19, 21, 23, 27
Median = Average of 6th and 7th terms = (11 + 12) ÷ 2 = 11.5
Difference = 13.25 − 11.5 = 1.75
∴ The correct answer is 1.75.

Alternate Method
Given:
Data set: 21, 11, 27, 8, 5, 12, 7, 23, 3, 14, 9, 19
Total number of observations (n) = 12

Formula Used:
Mean = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations
Median (for even n) = Average of the (n/2)th and (n/2 + 1)th observations in sorted data

Mean vs Median Comparison
0
10
20
30
Median 11.5
Mean 13.25
1.75
Difference

Calculations:
⇒ Sum of observations = 21 + 11 + 27 + 8 + 5 + 12 + 7 + 23 + 3 + 14 + 9 + 19 = 159
⇒ Mean = 159 ÷ 12 = 13.25
⇒ Arranging the given data in ascending order: 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 19, 21, 23, 27
⇒ Since n = 12 (an even number), the median lies between the 6th and 7th terms.
⇒ 6th term = 11, and 7th term = 12
⇒ Median = (11 + 12) ÷ 2 = 23 ÷ 2 = 11.5
⇒ Difference = Mean − Median
⇒ Difference = 13.25 − 11.5 = 1.75
∴ The correct answer is 1.75.

Additional Information
Mean

The arithmetic average of a set of numbers, calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total number of observations.

Median

The exact middle value of a sorted dataset. If the dataset has an even number of observations, the median is the average of the two middlemost values.

Mode

The value that appears most frequently in a dataset. A dataset can be unimodal, bimodal, multimodal, or have no mode at all.

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed continuous distribution, the fundamental relationship between mean, median, and mode is given by: Mode ≈ 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: The areas of the three adjacent faces of a closed cuboidal box are 120 cm^2, 60 cm^2 and 72 cm^2 respectively. Then, the total surface area of the box is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
The total surface area of a cuboid is exactly twice the sum of the areas of its three adjacent faces.

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × (Sum of adjacent faces)
⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × (120 + 60 + 72)
⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × 252 = 504 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 504 cm2.

Alternate Method
Given:
The areas of three adjacent faces of the closed cuboidal box are 120 cm2, 60 cm2, and 72 cm2.

Formula Used:
Total Surface Area of Cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)
Where l, b, and h are the length, breadth, and height of the cuboid.

Calculations:
Let the length, breadth, and height of the box be l, b, and h respectively.
⇒ Area of the first face (lb) = 120 cm2
⇒ Area of the second face (bh) = 60 cm2
⇒ Area of the third face (hl) = 72 cm2

Substitute these given areas directly into the total surface area formula:

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × (lb + bh + hl)
⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × (120 + 60 + 72)
⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × 252
⇒ Total Surface Area = 504 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 504 cm2.

Additional Information
Volume of a Cuboid

If A1, A2, and A3 are the areas of the three adjacent faces, the volume V is given directly by the square root of their product: V = √(A1 × A2 × A3).

Lateral Surface Area

The lateral surface area (area of the four vertical walls) of a cuboid is given by 2h(l + b), which excludes the top and bottom faces.

Length of Diagonal

The length of the longest diagonal possible inside a given cuboid is calculated as √(l2 + b2 + h2).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: At a dinner party, every two guests used a bowl of rice between them, every three guests used a bowl of dal among them and every four guests used a bowl of curd among them. There are altogether 65 bowls. What is the number of guests present at the party?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the total number of guests be the LCM of 2, 3, and 4, which is 12 units.
Number of bowls used = (12 ÷ 2) + (12 ÷ 3) + (12 ÷ 4) = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13 units.
Given total bowls = 65, so we equate: 13 units = 65 ⇒ 1 unit = 5.
Total guests = 12 units = 12 × 5 = 60 guests.
∴ The correct answer is 60 guests.

Alternate Method
Given:
One bowl of rice is shared between 2 guests.

One bowl of dal is shared among 3 guests.

One bowl of curd is shared among 4 guests.

Total number of bowls used = 65.

Calculations:
⇒ Let the total number of guests present at the party be x.
⇒ Number of rice bowls = x/2
⇒ Number of dal bowls = x/3
⇒ Number of curd bowls = x/4
⇒ Total bowls = x/2 + x/3 + x/4 = 65
⇒ Taking the LCM of the denominators 2, 3, and 4, which is 12:
⇒ (6x + 4x + 3x) ÷ 12 = 65
⇒ 13x ÷ 12 = 65
⇒ 13x = 65 × 12
⇒ x = (65 × 12) ÷ 13
⇒ x = 5 × 12
⇒ x = 60
∴ The correct answer is 60 guests.

Additional Information
LCM Method for Equations

Multiplying fractional terms by the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of their denominators converts them into whole numbers, making linear equations easier to solve.

Unitary Method

A technique that involves finding the value of a single unit first, and then multiplying it by the total parts to find the desired quantity. If n units = Total, then 1 unit = Total ÷ n.

Fractions in Sharing Problems

When items are shared among a group, the total items used equals the group size divided by the number of people sharing each individual item (Total Items = Total People ÷ Group Size per Item).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: A, B and C can reap a field in 2 days; B, C and D in 3 days; C, D and A in 7 days; D, A and B in 10 days. In what time can A, B, C and D together reap it?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let Total Work = LCM(2, 3, 7, 10) = 210 units.
Sum of 1-day work (efficiencies) of all 4 groups = (210 ÷ 2) + (210 ÷ 3) + (210 ÷ 7) + (210 ÷ 10) = 105 + 70 + 30 + 21 = 226.

Since each person is included in exactly 3 groups, their combined actual efficiency = 226 / 3 units/day.

Time required = Total Work ÷ Actual Efficiency = 210 ÷ (226 / 3) = 630 / 226 days.
∴ The correct answer is 630/226 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
Time taken by (A + B + C) = 2 days
Time taken by (B + C + D) = 3 days
Time taken by (C + D + A) = 7 days
Time taken by (D + A + B) = 10 days

Formula Used:
Total Work = LCM of time taken
Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time
Time Taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

Person	Days	Total Work	Efficiency
A + B + C	2	210	105
B + C + D	3	70
C + D + A	7	30
D + A + B	10	21

⇒ Sum of the efficiencies = 105 + 70 + 30 + 21 = 226 units/day
⇒ (A + B + C) + (B + C + D) + (C + D + A) + (D + A + B) = 226
⇒ 3A + 3B + 3C + 3D = 226
⇒ 3 × (A + B + C + D) = 226
⇒ Combined efficiency of (A + B + C + D) = 226 / 3 units/day
⇒ Time required = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency
⇒ Time required = 210 ÷ (226 / 3)
⇒ Time required = (210 × 3) / 226 = 630 / 226 days
∴ The correct answer is 630/226 days.

Additional Information
Time and Work LCM Method

Always assume Total Work as the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of the given days to make calculations fraction-free. Efficiency is calculated as Total Work ÷ Time.

Combined Group Work Principle

When individuals work in overlapping pairs or triplets, sum their combined group efficiencies and divide by the frequency of each person's appearance to find the actual joint efficiency.

Work and Time Relationship

Time and efficiency are inversely proportional. A higher combined efficiency directly results in proportionally less time taken to complete the assigned task.

questions.question: A distributor purchases electric heaters at a price 60% above the factory's basic cost C. He gives a 25% trade discount to a shopkeeper. Factory's basic cost = C

Distributor's price:

= 160% of C
= 1.6C

After 25% trade discount:

= 1.6C X 75/100
= 1.2C

After 30% markup by the shopkeeper:

= 1.2C X 130/100
= 1.56C

After 10% customer discount:

Final price = 1.56C X 90/100
= 1.404C

Given,

1.404C = 21,060
C = 21,060 ÷ 1.404
= ₹15,000

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 4
questions.question: A car travels for 6 hours at different speeds. For the first two hours at 60 m/s, for the next 2 hours at 50 m/s and for the remaining time at x m/s. If the average speed for the entire journey is 52 m/s, what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
For equal time intervals (2 hours each), the average speed over the entire journey is simply the arithmetic mean of the individual speeds.

⇒ Average Speed = (S1 + S2 + S3) ÷ 3
⇒ 52 = (60 + 50 + x) ÷ 3
⇒ 156 = 110 + x ⇒ x = 46
∴ The correct answer is 46.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total Time = 6 hours
Speed for the first 2 hours = 60 m/s
Speed for the next 2 hours = 50 m/s
Speed for the remaining time = x m/s
Average speed for the entire journey = 52 m/s

Formula Used:
Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time
Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:
⇒ Remaining time for the last part of the journey = 6 − 2 − 2 = 2 hours
⇒ Since time acts directly as a weight in the average calculation, the unit conversion factor from hours to seconds cancels out in the numerator and denominator.
⇒ Average Speed = [(S1 × T1) + (S2 × T2) + (S3 × T3)] ÷ Total Time
⇒ 52 = [(60 × 2) + (50 × 2) + (x × 2)] ÷ 6
⇒ 52 = (120 + 100 + 2x) ÷ 6
⇒ 52 × 6 = 220 + 2x
⇒ 312 = 220 + 2x
⇒ 2x = 312 − 220
⇒ 2x = 92
⇒ x = 46
∴ The correct answer is 46.

Additional Information
Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If a journey is covered in equal time intervals at different speeds, the average speed is simply the arithmetic mean of those speeds: Savg = (S1 + S2 + ... + Sn) ÷ n.

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If equal distances are covered at different speeds, the average speed is the harmonic mean of the speeds. For exactly two equal distances, the formula is: Savg = (2 × S1 × S2) ÷ (S1 + S2).

General Average Speed Formula

For any standard journey with varying times and distances, the average speed is universally calculated as the ratio of total distance to total time: Savg = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

questions.question: In a trapezium ABCD, AB || CD and perpendicular distance between them is 15 cm. Diagonals of trapezium cut at point O, shorter of the two parallel side is 12 cm long and if ratio of area of ∆AOB to the area of ∆COD is 1 : 4, then what will be the area of trapezium?

The ratio of areas of similar triangles is the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Ratio of sides AB and CD = √(1/4) = 1 : 2
Given the shorter side is 12 cm, so the longer side = 12 × 2 = 24 cm.
Area of trapezium = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height

Shorter side = 12 cm.
Area(ΔAOB) : Area(ΔCOD) = 1 : 4.

⇒ ∴ ΔAOB ∼ ΔCOD (by AA similarity criterion).
⇒ Area(ΔAOB) / Area(ΔCOD) = AB2 / CD2
⇒ 1 / 4 = AB2 / CD2
⇒ AB / CD = √(1 / 4) = 1 / 2
⇒ Since the ratio of AB : CD is 1 : 2, AB is the shorter side.
⇒ AB = 12 cm.
⇒ CD = 2 × 12 = 24 cm.
⇒ Area of Trapezium = 1/2 × (AB + CD) × h
⇒ Area = 1/2 × (12 + 24) × 15
⇒ Area = 1/2 × 36 × 15
⇒ Area = 18 × 15 = 270 cm2.
∴ The correct answer is 270 cm2.

Additional Information
Similar Triangles Area Theorem

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is strictly equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Properties of a Trapezium

A trapezium is a quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides. The diagonals of a trapezium intersect each other, dividing themselves proportionally.

Area of a Trapezium

The area formula is 1/2 × (a + b) × h, where 'a' and 'b' represent the parallel bases, and 'h' represents the perpendicular distance between them.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 4
questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 15 days and B is 25% more efficient than A. If A and B both work for 4 days and after 4 days C can complete the remaining work alone in 8 days, then find time taken by A, B and C together to complete the whole work.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Assume A's efficiency = 4 units/day → B's efficiency = 1.25 × 4 = 5 units/day.
Total Work = 15 × 4 = 60 units.
Work done by A & B in 4 days = (4 + 5) × 4 = 36 units → Remaining = 24 units.
C's efficiency = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 units/day → Total combined efficiency = 4 + 5 + 3 = 12 units/day.
∴ The correct answer is 5 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
Time taken by A = 15 days

B is 25% more efficient than A.

Time A and B worked together = 4 days
Time taken by C to complete the remaining work = 8 days

Formula Used:
Total Work = Efficiency × Time Taken

Calculations:
⇒ Efficiency ratio of A to B = 100 : 125 = 4 : 5
⇒ Time ratio of A to B = 5 : 4
⇒ Time taken by B = (15 ÷ 5) × 4 = 12 days
⇒ Combined efficiency of A and B = 4 + 5 = 9 units/day
⇒ Total Work = 15 × 4 = 60 units
⇒ Work done by A and B in 4 days = 9 × 4 = 36 units
⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 36 = 24 units
⇒ Efficiency of C = Remaining work ÷ Time taken = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 units/day
⇒ Time taken by C to complete whole work alone = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 days

Person	Days	Total Work	Efficiency
A	15	60	4
B	12	5
C	20	3

⇒ Total combined efficiency of A, B, and C = 4 + 5 + 3 = 12 units/day
⇒ Time taken by A, B, and C together = Total Work ÷ Total efficiency
⇒ Time taken = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 days
∴ The correct answer is 5 days.

Additional Information
Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the total work done by each individual. If all individuals work for the same number of days, wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When people work on alternate days, calculate the work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and then multiply to reach closer to the total work, the remaining work is done by the person whose turn it is next.

Pipes & Cisterns

Similar to Time & Work, inlet pipes have positive efficiency while outlet or leak pipes have negative efficiency. The net efficiency determines the time taken to fill or empty the tank.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 4
questions.question: The speed of a boat downstream is 2.5 times its speed upstream. If the total time taken by the boat for going 15 km downstream and the same distance upstream is 4 2/3 hours, then what is the speed (in km/h) of the boat downstream?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of downstream to upstream speed = 2.5 : 1 = 5 : 2.

For equal distance, the time ratio is inversely proportional to the speed ratio = 2 : 5.

Total time = 2 + 5 = 7 units → 14/3 hours.
Time taken downstream (2 units) = (14/3) × (2/7) = 4/3 hours.
Downstream speed = Distance ÷ Time = 15 ÷ (4/3) = 11.25 = 111/4 km/h.
∴ The correct answer is 111/4 km/h.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total distance downstream = 15 km
Total distance upstream = 15 km
Total time = 42/3 hours = 14/3 hours
Ratio of downstream speed to upstream speed = 2.5 : 1 = 5 : 2.
Let downstream speed = 5x and upstream speed = 2x.
Formula Used: Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Calculations:
⇒ (15 ÷ 5x) + (15 ÷ 2x) = 14 / 3
⇒ (3 / x) + (7.5 / x) = 14 / 3
⇒ 10.5 / x = 14 / 3
⇒ x = (10.5 × 3) ÷ 14
⇒ x = 31.5 ÷ 14 = 2.25
⇒ Downstream speed = 5x = 5 × 2.25 = 11.25 km/h
⇒ 11.25 km/h = 111/4 km/h
∴ The correct answer is 111/4 km/h.

Additional Information
Speed of Boat and Stream

If the speed of a boat in still water is B and the speed of the stream is S, then Downstream Speed (D) = B + S and Upstream Speed (U) = B − S.

Calculating Individual Speeds

Speed of boat in still water (B) = (D + U) ÷ 2 and Speed of stream
(S) = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Same Distance

If a boat travels the same distance upstream and downstream, the Average Speed = (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: The length of a room is 5.5 m and the width is 3.75 m. Find the cost of paving the floor with slabs at the rate of Rs. 800 per sq. meter.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total Cost = Length × Width × Rate per m2
Cost = 5.5 × 3.75 × 800

Multiply 3.75 by 800 first: 3.75 × 800 = 3000

Cost = 5.5 × 3000 = 16500
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 16500.

Alternate Method
Given:
Length of the room (L) = 5.5 m
Width of the room (W) = 3.75 m
Rate of paving = Rs. 800 per m2

Formula Used:
Area of a rectangle = Length × Width
Total Cost = Area × Rate per unit area

Calculations:
⇒ Area of the floor = 5.5 m × 3.75 m
⇒ Area = 20.625 m2
⇒ Total Cost = 20.625 × 800
⇒ Total Cost = 16500
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 16500.

Additional Information
Area of Rectangle

The total space enclosed within the boundaries of a rectangle. Formula: Area = Length × Breadth.

Perimeter of Rectangle

The total length of the boundary of a rectangle. Formula: Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Breadth). This is used for finding the cost of fencing or placing borders.

Area of Square

A square is a special type of rectangle where all four sides are equal. Formula: Area = Side2.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: A solid wooden toy is in the shape of a right circular cone mounted on a hemisphere. If the radius of the hemisphere is 5.6 cm and the total height of the toy is 11.6 cm, then what is the volume of the wooden toy (in cm³ ) (rounded off to the closest integral value)?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the combined volume formula for a cone on a hemisphere: V = (1/3) × π × r2 × (2r + h)
Cone height h = Total height − radius = 11.6 − 5.6 = 6 cm.
V = (1/3) × (22/7) × 5.6 × 5.6 × (2 × 5.6 + 6)
V = (1/3) × 22 × 0.8 × 5.6 × 17.2 ≈ 565.07 cm3

Rounding off to the closest integer gives 565 cm3.

∴ The correct answer is 565 cm3.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total height of the toy = 11.6 cm
Radius of hemisphere (r) = 5.6 cm

Formula Used:
Volume of a Cone = (1/3) × π × r2 × h
Volume of a Hemisphere = (2/3) × π × r3
Total Volume = (1/3) × π × r2 × (2r + h)

Calculations:
⇒ Height of cone (h) = Total height − Radius of hemisphere
⇒ h = 11.6 − 5.6 = 6 cm
⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × (5.6)2 × (2 × 5.6 + 6)
⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 31.36 × (11.2 + 6)
⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × 22 × 4.48 × 17.2
⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × 98.56 × 17.2
⇒ Total Volume = 1695.232 ÷ 3 ≈ 565.07 cm3
⇒ Rounding to the closest integral value, the volume is 565 cm3.
∴ The correct answer is 565 cm3.

Additional Information
Volume of a Hemisphere

V = (2/3) × π × r3, where r is the radius of the circular base.

Volume of a Right Circular Cone

V = (1/3) × π × r2 × h, where r is the radius of the base and h is the height.

Surface Areas

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a Cone = π × r × l, where slant height l = √(r2 + h2). CSA of a Hemisphere = 2 × π × r2.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: Aman's average score in a series of tests was ‘y’. He appeared in one more test and obtained score ‘z’. If Aman appeared in total ‘n’ tests, then which one of the following expression shows his average score for all the tests?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total number of tests taken by Aman = n.
Number of initial tests before the last one = n − 1.
Sum of scores in the first (n − 1) tests = Average × Count = y(n − 1).
Total sum of all n tests = Initial sum + Score of last test = y(n − 1) + z.
New Average = Total Sum ÷ Total Tests = [y(n − 1) + z] / n.
∴ The correct answer is [y(n − 1) + z] / n.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total number of tests appeared = n
Average score in the series before the last test = y
Score obtained in the last test = z

Formula Used:
Average = Sum of Observations ÷ Number of Observations
Sum of Observations = Average × Number of Observations

First (n − 1) tests
Sum = y(n − 1)
Last 1 test
Score = z
Total n tests
Total Sum = y(n − 1) + z

Calculations:
⇒ Number of tests taken before the final test = Total tests − 1 = n − 1
⇒ Sum of scores in the initial (n − 1) tests = y × (n − 1)
⇒ Total score for all n tests = Sum of (n − 1) tests + Score in the last test
⇒ Total score = y(n − 1) + z
⇒ Required Average = Total score ÷ Total number of tests
⇒ Required Average = [y(n − 1) + z] / n
∴ The correct answer is [y(n − 1) + z] / n.

Additional Information
Average (Arithmetic Mean)

Average is defined as the sum of all values divided by the total number of values. Formula: Average = Sum of all terms ÷ Number of terms.

Combined Average

If group 1 has n1 items with average A1 and group 2 has n2 items with average A2, then the combined average is (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Net Change in Average

When a new observation is added, the new average can also be calculated as: Old Average + (Difference between new value and old average ÷ Total new number of items).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: What is the area (in square units) of the triangle formed by the graphs of the equations: 2x - y + 8 = 0 and 8x + 3y - 24 = 0, and y = 0?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Put y = 0 to find the base points on the X-axis: 2x + 8 = 0 ⇒ x = −4 and 8x − 24 = 0 ⇒ x = 3.
The length of the base = 3 − (−4) = 7 units.

To find the height, find the y-coordinate of the intersection of 2x − y + 8 = 0 and 8x + 3y − 24 = 0.

Multiply the first equation by 4 to get 8x − 4y + 32 = 0, and subtract it from the second: 7y − 56 = 0 ⇒ y = 8.
Area = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 7 × 8 = 28 sq units.
∴ The correct answer is 28 sq units.

Alternate Method
Given:
Equation 1: 2x − y + 8 = 0
Equation 2: 8x + 3y − 24 = 0
Equation 3: y = 0 (This is the X-axis)

A(−4, 0)
B(3, 0)
C(0, 8)
Height = 8
Base = 7

Calculations:
⇒ To find Vertex A, substitute y = 0 into Equation 1:
⇒ 2x − 0 + 8 = 0 ⇒ 2x = −8 ⇒ x = −4
⇒ Vertex A = (−4, 0)
⇒ To find Vertex B, substitute y = 0 into Equation 2:
⇒ 8x + 3(0) − 24 = 0 ⇒ 8x = 24 ⇒ x = 3
⇒ Vertex B = (3, 0)
⇒ To find Vertex C, find the intersection point of Equation 1 and Equation 2:
⇒ From Equation 1, y = 2x + 8
⇒ Substitute y in Equation 2: 8x + 3(2x + 8) − 24 = 0
⇒ 8x + 6x + 24 − 24 = 0 ⇒ 14x = 0 ⇒ x = 0
⇒ Substitute x = 0 to get y: y = 2(0) + 8 = 8
⇒ Vertex C = (0, 8)
⇒ The distance between A(−4, 0) and B(3, 0) is the base of the triangle.
⇒ Base = 3 − (−4) = 7 units
⇒ The height of the triangle is the perpendicular distance from C(0, 8) to the X-axis.
⇒ Height = 8 units
⇒ Area of triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height
⇒ Area = 1/2 × 7 × 8
⇒ Area = 28 sq units
∴ The correct answer is 28 sq units.

Additional Information
Area of Triangle using Coordinates

Area = 1/2 × |x1(y2 − y3) + x2(y3 − y1) + x3(y1 − y2)|
Distance Formula

The distance between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is given by √((x2 − x1)2 + (y2 − y1)2).

Intercepts of a Line

The x-intercept is found by setting y = 0, and the y-intercept is found by setting x = 0 in the equation of the line.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: An electric fan lists at Rs.265.80 and is sold at a discount of 10%. The shopkeeper gives a further discount of 8% for cash payment. The selling price of the fan, when payment is made in cash, is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the multiplying factor method for successive discounts:

Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − D1)% × (100 − D2)%
SP = 265.80 × 0.90 × 0.92
SP = 265.80 × 0.828 = 220.0824 ≈ 220.08
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 220.08.

Alternate Method
Given:
Marked Price (MP) = Rs. 265.80
First discount (D1) = 10%
Second cash discount (D2) = 8%

Formula Used:
Selling Price (SP) = MP × [(100 − D1)/100] × [(100 − D2)/100]

Calculations:
⇒ Price after first discount of 10% = 265.80 × (100 − 10) ÷ 100
⇒ Price after 10% discount = 265.80 × 90 ÷ 100 = 239.22
⇒ Final Selling Price after further 8% discount = 239.22 × (100 − 8) ÷ 100
⇒ Final Selling Price = 239.22 × 92 ÷ 100 = 220.0824
⇒ Rounding to two decimal places, SP = Rs. 220.08
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 220.08.

Additional Information
Equivalent Single Discount

For two successive discounts of D1% and D2%, the single equivalent discount percentage is calculated using the formula: D = D1 + D2 − (D1 × D2) ÷ 100.

Marked Price (MP) vs Cost Price (CP)

Marked Price is the list price labeled on an item. All trade and cash discounts are exclusively calculated on the Marked Price, whereas profit or loss is calculated on the Cost Price.

tags.conceptTested: Calculating final selling price using successive discount multiplying factors.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: In a Maths quiz 10 students scored 20 marks, six students scored 19 marks, five students scored 18 marks, four students scored 17 marks, and two students scored 12 marks. The average marks scored by the class (correct to 2 decimal places) is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Use the Net Deviation Method by taking an Assumed Average = 18.
Net deviation = (10 × 2) + (6 × 1) + (5 × 0) + (4 × −1) + (2 × −6)
Net deviation = 20 + 6 + 0 − 4 − 12 = +10 marks
Average change per student = +10 ÷ 27 ≈ +0.37
Actual Average = 18 + 0.37 = 18.37
∴ The correct answer is 18.37 marks.

Alternate Method
Frequency Distribution of Marks
Marks Scored
2
12
4
17
5
18
6
19
10
20

Given:
Distribution of students and their marks:

10 students scored 20 marks

6 students scored 19 marks

5 students scored 18 marks

4 students scored 17 marks

2 students scored 12 marks

Formula Used:
Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

Calculations:
⇒ Total students = 10 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 2 = 27
⇒ Total marks = (10 × 20) + (6 × 19) + (5 × 18) + (4 × 17) + (2 × 12)
⇒ Total marks = 200 + 114 + 90 + 68 + 24
⇒ Total marks = 496
⇒ Average marks = 496 ÷ 27
⇒ Average marks ≈ 18.3703...
∴ The correct answer is 18.37 marks.

Additional Information
Weighted Average

When data sets have different frequencies or weights, the weighted average is calculated as Sum(wi × xi) ÷ Sum(wi), where w is the respective frequency and x is the value.

Assumed Mean Deviation Method

A faster way to find averages involves picking an assumed mean (A), calculating total deviation (D) of all items from A, and finding True Average = A + (D ÷ N).

Combined Average

For two groups with sizes n1 and n2 and averages A1 and A2, the combined average is given by the formula (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: To pack a set of books, Gautam got cartons of a certain height that were 48 inches long and 27 inches wide. If the volume of such a carton was 22.5 cubic feet, what was the height of each carton? [Use 1 foot = 12 inches.]
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Convert the given volume directly into cubic inches by multiplying by 123.

Volume in inches = 22.5 × 1728 = 38880 inch3
Since Volume = Length × Width × Height
Height = 38880 ÷ (48 × 27)
Height = 38880 ÷ 1296 = 30 inches
∴ The correct answer is 30 inches.

Alternate Method
Given:
Length (L) = 48 inches
Width (B) = 27 inches
Volume (V) = 22.5 ft3
1 ft = 12 inches

Formula Used:
Volume of a cuboid = L × B × H

Calculations:
⇒ Volume in inch3 = 22.5 × 12 × 12 × 12
⇒ Volume = 22.5 × 1728 = 38880 inch3
⇒ L × B × H = 38880
⇒ 48 × 27 × H = 38880
⇒ 1296 × H = 38880
⇒ H = 38880 ÷ 1296
⇒ H = 30 inches
∴ The correct answer is 30 inches.

Additional Information
Volume of a Cuboid

V = L × B × H, where L, B, and H denote length, breadth, and height respectively.

Surface Area of a Cuboid

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2(LB + BH + HL). Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 2H(L + B).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the longest space diagonal inside a cuboid is √(L2 + B2 + H2).

Unit Conversions

Since 1 foot = 12 inches, calculating volume requires taking the cube of 12. Thus, 1 cubic foot = 123 = 1728 cubic inches.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: A hemispherical bowl of diameter 16 cm is full of ice cream. Each student in a class is served exactly 6 scoops of ice cream. If the hemispherical scoop is having a radius of 2 cm, then ice cream is served to approximately how many students?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total number of scoops in the bowl = (Radius of bowl ÷ Radius of scoop)3
⇒ Total scoops = (8 ÷ 2)3 = 43 = 64 scoops
Since each student is served exactly 6 scoops:
⇒ Number of students served = 64 ÷ 6 = 10.66

Ice cream can be fully served to a maximum of 10 students with exactly 6 scoops each.

∴ The correct answer is 10 students.

Alternate Method
Given:
Diameter of the hemispherical bowl = 16 cm ⇒ Radius
(R) = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm
Radius of the hemispherical scoop (r) = 2 cm
Scoops served per student = 6

Formula Used:
Volume of a hemisphere = (2 ÷ 3) × π × radius3

Calculations:
⇒ Volume of the ice cream in the bowl = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 83 = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 512
⇒ Volume of a single scoop = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 23 = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 8
⇒ Total number of scoops = Volume of bowl ÷ Volume of single scoop
⇒ Total number of scoops = [(2 ÷ 3) × π × 512] ÷ [(2 ÷ 3) × π × 8] = 512 ÷ 8 = 64 scoops
⇒ Since each student receives exactly 6 scoops, the number of students = 64 ÷ 6 = 10.66
⇒ Thus, ice cream is fully served to 10 students, leaving exactly 4 scoops remaining in the bowl.
∴ The correct answer is 10 students.

Additional Information
Volume of a Hemisphere

A hemisphere is exactly half of a complete sphere. Its volume formula is V = (2 ÷ 3) × π × r3.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Hemisphere

The TSA encompasses the curved surface along with the flat circular base. The formula is TSA = 3 × π × r2.

Volume Proportionality Rule

For any pair of 3D shapes featuring identical proportions (like two spheres or hemispheres), the ratio of their total volumes equals the cube of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: In a bag, the number of ₹5 coins is 8 more than the number of ₹10 coins but 20% less than the number of ₹2 coins. If the total amount in the bag is ₹270, what is the number of ₹5 coins?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the number of ₹2 coins be 5y. Then ₹5 coins (20% less) = 4y, and ₹10 coins = 4y − 8.

Total value = 2(5y) + 5(4y) + 10(4y − 8) = 270.
10y + 20y + 40y − 80 = 270 ⇒ 70y = 350 ⇒ y = 5.
Number of ₹5 coins = 4 × 5 = 20.
∴ The correct answer is 20.

Alternate Method
Given:
Number of ₹5 coins is 8 more than the number of ₹10 coins.

Number of ₹5 coins is 20% less than the number of ₹2 coins.

Total amount in the bag = ₹270.

Formula Used:
Total Value = (Value of ₹2 coins) + (Value of ₹5 coins) + (Value of ₹10 coins)

Calculation:
⇒ Let the number of ₹2 coins be 5y.
⇒ Number of ₹5 coins is 20% less = 5y × (80 ÷ 100) = 4y
⇒ Number of ₹10 coins is 8 less than ₹5 coins = 4y − 8
⇒ Total value = (2 × 5y) + (5 × 4y) + 10 × (4y − 8) = 270
⇒ 10y + 20y + 40y − 80 = 270
⇒ 70y = 350
⇒ y = 350 ÷ 70 = 5
⇒ Number of ₹5 coins = 4 × 5 = 20
∴ The correct answer is 20.

Additional Information
Coins and Denominations

The total value of any denomination is calculated by multiplying the face value of the coin with the number of coins (Value = Denomination × Count).

Percentage Relationships

If quantity A is R% less than quantity B, then A = B × (100 − R) ÷ 100. This relationship is often used to find the ratio between multiple quantities quickly.

Linear Equations

Word problems often translate into linear equations format ax + b = c, where solving for the common ratio variable 'y' or 'x' gives the exact values for each parameter.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: The base of a triangular field is three times its altitude. If the cost of cultivating the field at Rs. 24.4/hect is Rs. 448.35, find its height. (in metres)
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total Area = Total Cost ÷ Rate per hectare
Area = 448.35 ÷ 24.4 = 18.375 hectares = 183750 m2
Area of a triangle = ½ × Base × Height
½ × 3h × h = 183750 ⇒ h2 = 122500
h = √122500 = 350 m
∴ The correct answer is 350 m.

Alternate Method
Given:
Base (b) = 3 × Height (h)
Total cost of cultivating = ₹448.35
Rate of cultivating = ₹24.4 per hectare
1 hectare = 10,000 m2

Formula Used:
Area of field = Total Cost ÷ Rate per hectare
Area of triangle = ½ × Base × Height

Calculations:
⇒ Area = 448.35 ÷ 24.4
⇒ Area = 18.375 hectares
⇒ Area in m2 = 18.375 × 10,000 = 183,750 m2
⇒ ½ × Base × Height = 183,750
⇒ ½ × 3h × h = 183,750
⇒ 1.5h2 = 183,750
⇒ h2 = 183,750 ÷ 1.5
⇒ h2 = 122,500
⇒ h = √122500
⇒ h = 350 m
∴ The correct answer is 350 m.

Additional Information
Area of Equilateral Triangle

The area is given by (√3 ÷ 4) × a2, and the height is (√3 ÷ 2) × a, where a is the side length.

Heron's Formula

For a scalene triangle with sides a, b, and c, Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where the semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.

Hectare Conversion

1 hectare is widely used in land measurement and is equal to exactly 10,000 square meters (m2).

questions.question: In a circle with centre O and radius 6.5 cm, a chord AB is at a distance 2.5 cm from the centre. If tangents at A and B intersect at P, then find the distance of P from the centre.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When tangents from an external point P intersect a circle, and the chord of contact is at a distance d from the centre:

Distance of P from centre OP = (Radius)2 ÷ d
⇒ OP = 6.52 ÷ 2.5

∴ The correct answer is 16.9 cm.

Alternate Method

Radius of the circle, OA = 6.5 cm
Distance of chord from the centre, OM = 2.5 cm

Formula Used:
Hypotenuse2 = Perpendicular2 + Base2

Calculations:

⇒ In right ΔOMA, by Pythagoras theorem:
⇒ AM = √(OA2 − OM2)
⇒ AM = √(6.52 − 2.52) = √(42.25 − 6.25) = √36 = 6 cm
⇒ Tangent PA is perpendicular to radius OA, so ∠OAP = 90°.
⇒ In right ΔOAP, AM is the altitude from the right angle to hypotenuse OP.

Additional Information
Tangent to a Circle

A tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.

Chord of Contact

The line joining the points of contact of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle is called the chord of contact.

Right-Angled Triangle Properties

In a right ΔABC right angled at A, if AD ⊥ BC, then AB2 = BD × BC and AC2 = CD × BC.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: Rohit scored at an average of 58 in his last five innings. Rohit scored 42, 56, 72 and 40 in the last four innings. How many runs did Rohit score in the first of these five innings?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
We can quickly solve this using the Net Deviation Method.

Target Average = 58
Deviations of the last 4 innings = (42 − 58) + (56 − 58) + (72 − 58) + (40 − 58)
⇒ Net Deviation = −16 − 2 + 14 − 18 = −22

To balance the average, the missing inning must compensate for this deviation.

Missing inning = 58 − (−22) = 80
∴ The correct answer is 80 runs.

Alternate Method
Total Runs = 5 × 58 = 290
x
1st Inning
42
56
72
40
Last 4 Innings = 210

Given:
Average runs of 5 innings = 58
Runs scored in the last 4 innings = 42, 56, 72, and 40

Formula Used:
Average = Total Sum of Observations ÷ Number of Observations

Calculations:
⇒ Total runs in 5 innings = Average × Number of innings
⇒ Total runs in 5 innings = 58 × 5 = 290
⇒ Sum of runs in the last 4 innings = 42 + 56 + 72 + 40 = 210
⇒ Runs in the 1st inning = Total runs in 5 innings − Sum of runs in the last 4 innings
⇒ Runs in the 1st inning = 290 − 210 = 80
∴ The correct answer is 80 runs.

Additional Information
Average

Average represents the central value of a dataset. It is calculated by dividing the sum of all values by the total number of values.

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. This property helps in finding a missing observation efficiently without calculating large sums.

Weighted Average

When combining groups of varying sizes, the combined average is calculated as: (n1x1 + n2x2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: ABCD is a rhombus in which ∠ADB = 25°. Then, the value of (2 ∠BAD - ∠ABC) is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
In a rhombus, adjacent sides are equal (AD = AB), making ΔABD an isosceles triangle.
⇒ ∠ABD = ∠ADB = 25°
⇒ ∠BAD = 180° − (25° + 25°) = 130°
⇒ ∠ABC = 2 × ∠ABD = 50° (Since the diagonal bisects the angle)
⇒ 2 × ∠BAD − ∠ABC = 2 × 130° − 50° = 210°
∴ The correct answer is 210°.

Alternate Method
Given:
ABCD is a rhombus.

∠ADB = 25°

Calculations:
In a rhombus, all four sides are of equal length, so AD = AB.
⇒ In ΔABD, sides AD and AB are equal, which means the angles opposite to them are also equal.
⇒ ∠ABD = ∠ADB = 25°

The sum of all interior angles in a triangle is 180°.

⇒ ∠BAD + ∠ABD + ∠ADB = 180°
⇒ ∠BAD + 25° + 25° = 180°
⇒ ∠BAD = 180° − 50° = 130°

We know that the diagonal of a rhombus acts as an angle bisector for the interior angles.

⇒ ∠ABC = 2 × ∠ABD
⇒ ∠ABC = 2 × 25° = 50°
Now, substitute these values into the required expression (2 × ∠BAD − ∠ABC):
⇒ 2 × 130° − 50°
⇒ 260° − 50° = 210°
∴ The correct answer is 210°.

Additional Information
Properties of a Rhombus

All four sides are of equal length. Opposite angles are equal, and any two adjacent angles are supplementary (their sum is 180°).

Diagonals of a Rhombus

The diagonals bisect each other at right angles (90°) and completely bisect the interior angles at the vertices they connect.

Area of a Rhombus

The area can be calculated using the lengths of the diagonals: Area = (d1 × d2) ÷ 2, or by using the base and height: Area = Base × Height.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: Three solid iron cubes of edges 8 cm, 10 cm and 12 cm are melted together to make a new cube. It is observed that 496 cm^3 of the melted material is lost due to improper handling. The area (in cm^2) of the whole surface of the newly formed cube is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total volume of given cubes = 83 + 103 + 123 = 512 + 1000 + 1728 = 3240 cm3
Volume of the new cube = 3240 − 496 = 2744 cm3
Side of the new cube (a) = 3√2744 = 14 cm
Total Surface Area = 6a2 = 6 × 142 = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 1176 cm2.

Alternate Method
Given:
Edges of the three solid iron cubes = 8 cm, 10 cm, and 12 cm
Melted material lost due to improper handling = 496 cm3

Formula Used:
Volume of a cube = a3
Total surface area of a cube = 6a2

Calculations:
⇒ Total volume of the three smaller cubes = (83 + 103 + 123) cm3
⇒ Total volume = 512 + 1000 + 1728 = 3240 cm3
⇒ Volume of the newly formed cube = Total Initial Volume − Material Lost
⇒ Volume of the new cube = 3240 − 496 = 2744 cm3
⇒ Let the edge length of the new cube be 'a' cm.
⇒ a3 = 2744
⇒ a = 3√2744 = 14 cm
⇒ Area of the whole surface of the new cube = 6a2
⇒ Surface Area = 6 × (14)2
⇒ Surface Area = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 1176 cm2.

Additional Information
Total Surface Area of a Cube

The total surface area of a cube is the combined area of its 6 identical square faces. Formula: TSA = 6a2.

Lateral Surface Area of a Cube

The lateral surface area includes only the 4 vertical faces, excluding the top and bottom faces. Formula: LSA = 4a2.

Volume of a Cube

The volume of a cube represents the 3D space occupied by it. Formula: Volume = a3.

Diagonal of a Cube

The length of the longest line segment connecting two opposite interior corners of a cube. Formula: Diagonal = a√3.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: A girl cycles from A to B, a distance of 25 km in 2 hours 20 minutes. The road from A is a levelled road for 15 km and then it slopes down to B. The average speed of the girl on the levelled road is 10 km/h. Her average downhill speed (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total time = 2 hr 20 min = 7/3 hours
Time spent on levelled road = 15 ÷ 10 = 3/2 hours
Remaining time for downhill = 7/3 − 3/2 = 5/6 hours
Downhill distance = 25 − 15 = 10 km
Downhill speed = 10 ÷ (5/6) = 12 km/h
∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total distance = 25 km
Total time = 2 hours 20 minutes = 2 + 20/60 = 7/3 hours
Distance of levelled road = 15 km
Speed on levelled road = 10 km/h

Formula Used:
Time = Distance ÷ Speed
Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Calculations:
⇒ Time taken to cover the levelled road = 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5 hours = 3/2 hours
⇒ Remaining distance (downhill) = Total distance − Distance of levelled road
⇒ Remaining distance = 25 − 15 = 10 km
⇒ Remaining time = Total time − Time on levelled road
⇒ Remaining time = 7/3 − 3/2 = (14 − 9) / 6 = 5/6 hours
⇒ Average downhill speed = Remaining distance ÷ Remaining time
⇒ Average downhill speed = 10 ÷ (5/6) = (10 × 6) / 5 = 12 km/h
∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.

Additional Information
Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance covered divided by the total time taken. Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, the average speed for the whole journey is given by 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed = |S1 − S2|. When moving in opposite directions, relative speed = S1 + S2.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: A cylindrical vessel 60 cm in diameter is partially filled with water. A sphere 30 cm in diameter is gently dropped into the vessel and is completely immersed. To what further height will the water in the cylinder rise?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When an object is immersed, the volume of water displaced equals the volume of the immersed object.

Volume of Cylinder part (Rise) = Volume of Sphere
π × R2 × h = (4 ÷ 3) × π × r3
h = (4 ÷ 3) × (r ÷ R)2 × r
Given R = 30 cm and r = 15 cm. Ratio (r ÷ R) = 1/2.
h = (4 ÷ 3) × (1/2)2 × 15 = (4 ÷ 3) × (1 ÷ 4) × 15 = 5 cm
∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Diameter of the cylindrical vessel = 60 cm
Radius of the cylinder
(R) = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm
Diameter of the sphere = 30 cm
Radius of the sphere (r) = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm

Formula Used:
Volume of Cylinder = π × R2 × h
Volume of Sphere = (4 ÷ 3) × π × r3

Calculations:
When the sphere is completely immersed, the volume of water displaced is exactly equal to the volume of the sphere.

Let the rise in the water level be h cm.
⇒ Volume of water raised = Volume of sphere
⇒ π × R2 × h = (4 ÷ 3) × π × r3
⇒ π × (30)2 × h = (4 ÷ 3) × π × (15)3

Cancel π from both sides:

⇒ 900 × h = (4 ÷ 3) × 3375
⇒ 900 × h = 4 × 1125
⇒ 900 × h = 4500
⇒ h = 4500 ÷ 900
⇒ h = 5 cm
∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.

Additional Information
Archimedes' Principle (Volume Displacement)

When an object is completely submerged in a fluid, it displaces a volume of fluid exactly equal to its own volume regardless of its shape.

Surface Area of Sphere

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 4 × π × r2

Cylinder Area Properties

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × r × h | Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2 × π × r × (r + h)

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: Sampark Kranti Express left Delhi for Chennai at 14:30 hours, travelling at a speed of 75 km/h, while Rajdhani Express left Delhi for Chennai on the same day at 16:30 hours, travelling at a speed of 90 km/h, travelling on the same route. How far away from Delhi will the two trains meet?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Direct formula for meeting distance: D = [S1 × S2 × Time Difference] ÷ (S2 − S1)
Here, S1 = 75 km/h, S2 = 90 km/h, and Time Difference = 16:30 − 14:30 = 2 hours.
D = [75 × 90 × 2] ÷ (90 − 75)
D = 13500 ÷ 15
D = 900 km
∴ The correct answer is 900 km.

Alternate Method
Given:
Speed of Sampark Kranti Express = 75 km/h
Departure time of Sampark Kranti = 14:30 hours
Speed of Rajdhani Express = 90 km/h
Departure time of Rajdhani = 16:30 hours

Formula Used:
Distance = Speed × Time
Relative Speed (same direction) = S1 − S2

Calculations:
⇒ Time difference between the departures = 16:30 − 14:30 = 2 hours.
⇒ Distance covered by Sampark Kranti Express in these 2 hours = 75 × 2 = 150 km.
⇒ This 150 km is the head start distance between the two trains.
⇒ Relative speed of Rajdhani Express with respect to Sampark Kranti = 90 − 75 = 15 km/h.
⇒ Time taken by Rajdhani Express to catch up = Distance ÷ Relative speed.
⇒ Catch up time = 150 ÷ 15 = 10 hours.
⇒ The meeting distance from Delhi = Speed of Rajdhani × Time taken.
⇒ Distance = 90 × 10 = 900 km.
∴ The correct answer is 900 km.

Additional Information
Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S1 − S2). When they move in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S1 + S2).

Catch-up Time Formula

Time to meet = Head start distance ÷ Relative speed. This determines the duration required for the faster object to overtake the slower one.

Average Speed

When a journey covers two equal halves at different speeds S1 and S2, Average Speed = (2 × S1 × S2) ÷ (S1 + S2).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: Vineet buys 2 chairs for Rs. 1500. He sold one at 20% profit and the other at 17.5% loss. On the whole, he receives neither loss nor profit. What was the cost of each chair?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Since the overall transaction results in 0% profit/loss, the profit amount equals the loss amount.

⇒ 20% of CP1 = 17.5% of CP2
⇒ Ratio of CP1 : CP2 = 17.5 : 20 = 7 : 8
⇒ CP1 = (7 ÷ 15) × 1500 = Rs. 700 & CP2 = (8 ÷ 15) × 1500 = Rs. 800
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 700, Rs. 800.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total Cost Price of two chairs = Rs. 1500
Profit on first chair = 20%
Loss on second chair = 17.5%
Net profit or loss = 0%

Formula Used:
When an overall transaction yields neither profit nor loss, the absolute profit earned on one item is exactly equal to the loss incurred on the other item.

Calculations:
⇒ Let the CP of the first chair be x and the second chair be y.
⇒ x + y = 1500
⇒ 20% of x = 17.5% of y
⇒ x ÷ y = 17.5 ÷ 20 = 175 ÷ 200
⇒ x ÷ y = 7 ÷ 8
⇒ Ratio of CP of first chair to second chair = 7 : 8
⇒ Total ratio parts = 7 + 8 = 15
⇒ 15 parts = 1500 ⇒ 1 part = 100
⇒ CP of first chair = 7 × 100 = Rs. 700
⇒ CP of second chair = 8 × 100 = Rs. 800
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 700, Rs. 800.

Additional Information
No Profit No Loss Condition

When a transaction results in no profit and no loss overall, the absolute profit earned on one item is exactly equal to the absolute loss on the other item.

Alligation Cross Method

Used for finding the ratio of base values (like Cost Price) when individual percentages and overall average percentage are given. CP Ratio = (Net % − Loss %) : (Profit % − Net %).

Base of Profit and Loss

Both profit percentage and loss percentage are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise. Profit = SP − CP and Loss = CP − SP.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: The denominator of a rational number is greater than the numerator by 10. If the numerator is increased by 1 and the denominator is decreased by 1, then expression for new denominator is _________. (where n is the numerator of the fraction)
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the numerator of the rational number be n.

The original denominator is 10 more than the numerator, which is n + 10.

When the denominator is decreased by 1, the new denominator becomes (n + 10) − 1.

Simplifying the expression, we get n + 9.

∴ The correct answer is n + 9.

Alternate Method
n
n + 10
Original Fraction
Num + 1
Den − 1
n + 1
n + 9
New Fraction
New Denominator = n + 10 − 1 = n + 9

Given:
⇒ The denominator of a rational number is greater than the numerator by 10.
⇒ The numerator is increased by 1.
⇒ The denominator is decreased by 1.

Calculation:
⇒ Let the numerator of the original rational number be n.
⇒ Original Denominator = n + 10
⇒ Original Rational Number = n / (n + 10)
⇒ The new denominator is formed by subtracting 1 from the original denominator.
⇒ New Denominator = Original Denominator − 1
⇒ New Denominator = (n + 10) − 1
⇒ New Denominator = n + 9
∴ The correct answer is n + 9.

Additional Information
Rational Numbers

A rational number is any number that can be expressed as a fraction p/q, where p and q are integers and q is not equal to zero.

Fraction Modification

If a fraction is represented as x/y, increasing the numerator by 'a' and decreasing the denominator by 'b' results in a new fraction expressed as (x + a) / (y − b).

Simplification of Algebraic Expressions

Simplifying algebraic expressions involves grouping and combining like terms. For constant numbers, basic arithmetic operations are applied directly, e.g., (n + a) − b = n + (a − b).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: There are 12 men on a Basketball team and in a game 5 of them play at any one time. If the game is 1 hour long and if each man plays exactly the same amount of time, how many minutes does each man play?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total active playing time on the court = Number of active players × Game duration.
Total playing time = 5 × 60 = 300 minutes.

Since this playing time is exactly equally distributed among all 12 players, we divide the total time by 12.

Time per player = 300 ÷ 12 = 25 minutes.
∴ The correct answer is 25 minutes.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total players on the basketball team = 12
Number of players active on the court at any one time = 5
Duration of the game = 1 hour = 60 minutes

Formula Used:
Total player-minutes = Number of active players × Game duration
Time per player = Total player-minutes ÷ Total number of players

Calculations:
⇒ Total player-minutes = 5 × 60
⇒ Total player-minutes = 300 minutes
⇒ As the total court time is shared equally among 12 players, we divide the total minutes by 12.
⇒ Time per player = 300 ÷ 12
⇒ Time per player = 25 minutes
∴ The correct answer is 25 minutes.

Additional Information
Man-Hours Concept

When an activity requires a constant number of individuals active at all times, the total accumulated effort is the product of the active individuals and the duration: Total Time = Active Members × Duration.

Equal Distribution (Average)

If a total continuous resource must be shared exactly equally among a group, the amount received per individual is calculated as Average = Total Quantity ÷ Total Number of Individuals.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: In a group of 260 people, one-fourth are women, two-fifth are men and the rest are children. The average age of women is five-sixth of the average age of men, average age of children is one-third of the average age of men. If the average age of men is 48 years, what is the average age of the group in years?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
We can find the average directly using fractions without calculating the total number of people.

Fraction of Women = 1/4, Men = 2/5 ⇒ Children = 1 − (1/4 + 2/5) = 1 − 13/20 = 7/20.
Average age of Men = 48 years.
Average age of Women = 5/6 × 48 = 40 years | Average age of Children = 1/3 × 48 = 16 years.
Group Average = (1/4 × 40) + (2/5 × 48) + (7/20 × 16) = 10 + 19.2 + 5.6 = 34.8.
∴ The correct answer is 34.8 years.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total people = 260
Number of Women = 1/4 of 260 = 65
Number of Men = 2/5 of 260 = 104
Number of Children = 260 − (65 + 104) = 91
Average age of Men = 48 years
Total Group (260 people)
Women (1/4)
Avg: 40
Men (2/5)
Avg: 48
Children (7/20)
Avg: 16
Weighted Average Calculation
Group Avg = 34.8 years

Formula Used:
Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

Calculations:
⇒ Average age of Women = 5/6 × 48 = 40 years
⇒ Average age of Children = 1/3 × 48 = 16 years
⇒ Total age of Women = 65 × 40 = 2600
⇒ Total age of Men = 104 × 48 = 4992
⇒ Total age of Children = 91 × 16 = 1456
⇒ Total age of the group = 2600 + 4992 + 1456 = 9048
⇒ Average age of the group = 9048 ÷ 260
⇒ Average = 34.8 years
∴ The correct answer is 34.8 years.

Additional Information
Weighted Average Method

When different sub-groups have unique averages, the overall combined average is calculated as (N1A1 + N2A2 + ...) ÷ (N1 + N2 + ...).

Independence from Absolute Totals

If the relative ratios or percentage fractions of multiple groups are known along with their respective averages, the overall average remains constant regardless of the actual base population size.

Properties of Averages

If all individual items in a data set are multiplied or divided by a specific constant, the overall average of the data set will also be multiplied or divided by that same constant.
