questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: Three solid iron cubes of edges 8 cm, 10 cm and 12 cm are melted together to make a new cube. It is observed that 496 cm³ of the melted material is lost due to improper handling. The area (in cm²) of the whole surface of the newly formed cube is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total volume of given cubes = 83 + 103 + 123 = 512 + 1000 + 1728 = 3240 cm3
Volume of the new cube = 3240 − 496 = 2744 cm3
Side of the new cube (a) = 3√2744 = 14 cm
Total Surface Area = 6a2 = 6 × 142 = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 1176 cm2.

Alternate Method
Given:
Edges of the three solid iron cubes = 8 cm, 10 cm, and 12 cm
Melted material lost due to improper handling = 496 cm3

Formula Used:
Volume of a cube = a3
Total surface area of a cube = 6a2

Calculations:
⇒ Total volume of the three smaller cubes = (83 + 103 + 123) cm3
⇒ Total volume = 512 + 1000 + 1728 = 3240 cm3
⇒ Volume of the newly formed cube = Total Initial Volume − Material Lost
⇒ Volume of the new cube = 3240 − 496 = 2744 cm3
⇒ Let the edge length of the new cube be 'a' cm.
⇒ a3 = 2744
⇒ a = 3√2744 = 14 cm
⇒ Area of the whole surface of the new cube = 6a2
⇒ Surface Area = 6 × (14)2
⇒ Surface Area = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 1176 cm2.

Additional Information
Total Surface Area of a Cube

The total surface area of a cube is the combined area of its 6 identical square faces. Formula: TSA = 6a2.

Lateral Surface Area of a Cube

The lateral surface area includes only the 4 vertical faces, excluding the top and bottom faces. Formula: LSA = 4a2.

Volume of a Cube

The volume of a cube represents the 3D space occupied by it. Formula: Volume = a3.

Diagonal of a Cube

The length of the longest line segment connecting two opposite interior corners of a cube. Formula: Diagonal = a√3.

cos (36° - A) cos (36° + A) + cos (54° - A) cos (54° + A)

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026: Officer’s Friday - Mega Live Test
questions.question: The average weight of the first thirteen persons among fourteen persons is 78 kg. The weight of the 14th person is 39 kg more than the average weight of all the fourteen persons. Find the weight of the 14th person.
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
The extra weight of the 14th person (39 kg) is distributed among the first 13 persons to equalize their average to the overall average.

Total Average = Average of 13 persons + (Extra weight ÷ 13)
Total Average = 78 + (39 ÷ 13) = 78 + 3 = 81 kg
Weight of 14th person = Total Average + Extra = 81 + 39 = 120 kg
∴ The correct answer is 120 kg.

Alternate Method
Given:
Average weight of 13 persons = 78 kg
Weight of 14th person = Average of 14 persons + 39 kg

Formula Used:
Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Number of observations

Calculations:
Let the average weight of all 14 persons be x kg.
⇒ Total weight of 14 persons = 14 × x = 14x
⇒ Weight of 14th person = x + 39
⇒ Sum of weights of 13 persons = 13 × 78 = 1014 kg
⇒ Total Weight = Sum of 13 persons + Weight of 14th person
⇒ 14x = 1014 + (x + 39)
⇒ 14x − x = 1053
⇒ 13x = 1053
⇒ x = 1053 ÷ 13
⇒ x = 81 kg
⇒ Weight of 14th person = 81 + 39 = 120 kg
∴ The correct answer is 120 kg.

Additional Information
Average Concept

Average is the central value of a set of data. Formula: Average = Total Sum ÷ Total Number.

Deviation Method

If a new member joins and the average increases, the new member's value = Old Average + (Increase in Average × New Strength).

Sum of Observations

Sum = Average × Number of observations. Any change in sum directly impacts the average by Change ÷ n.

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026: Officer’s Friday - Mega Live Test
questions.question: Aarav owns a watch worth Rs. 10,000. He sells it to Bhavin at a profit of 15%. After some days, Bhavin sells it back to Aarav at 15% loss. Find the percentage profit or loss faced by Aarav.
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Aarav sells the watch for ₹11,500 (15% profit on ₹10,000).

Bhavin sells it back at a 15% loss on his Cost Price (₹11,500).

Bhavin's Loss = 15% of 11,500 = ₹1,725.

Since Aarav gets the watch back, his net cash gain is exactly Bhavin's loss amount.

Net Profit % = (1,725 ÷ 10,000) × 100 = 17.25%.
∴ The correct answer is 17.25% profit.

Alternate Method
Given:
Initial Cost Price (CP1) of watch = ₹10,000
Profit percentage for Aarav = 15%
Loss percentage for Bhavin = 15%

Calculations:
⇒ Selling Price of Aarav (SP1) = 10,000 + (15 ÷ 100) × 10,000 = ₹11,500
⇒ Cost Price for Bhavin = ₹11,500
⇒ Selling Price of Bhavin (SP2) = 11,500 − (15 ÷ 100) × 11,500
⇒ SP2 = 11,500 − 1,725 = ₹9,775
⇒ This SP2 is the price Aarav pays to get the watch back.
⇒ Aarav's total profit = (Amount received from sale) − (Amount paid for buy-back)
⇒ Net Profit = 11,500 − 9,775 = ₹1,725
⇒ Profit % = (Net Profit ÷ Initial CP) × 100
⇒ Profit % = (1,725 ÷ 10,000) × 100 = 17.25%
∴ The correct answer is 17.25% profit.

Additional Information
Net Profit in Buyback Transactions

When an item is sold at a profit and bought back at a loss, the original seller's total profit is the sum of the initial profit amount and the savings made during the buy-back.

Effect of Different Base Values

A 15% profit and a 15% loss do not cancel each other out because the base Cost Price changes after the first transaction. The second percentage is calculated on the new Selling Price.

Profit and Loss Formulas
Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 | Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Always ensure the CP used is specific to the person making the transaction.

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026: Officer’s Friday - Mega Live Test
questions.question: The floor of a room 12 m long and 8 m wide is to be decorated with square designs having the maximum possible area. Find the number of square designs required.
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Side of the maximum possible square = HCF of length and width.
Side = HCF(12, 8) = 4 m.
Number of square designs = (Length × Width) ÷ (Side × Side).
Number of designs = (12 × 8) ÷ (4 × 4) = 96 ÷ 16 = 6.
∴ The correct answer is 6.

Alternate Method
Given: Length (L) = 12 m and Width (W) = 8 m.

Formula Used:
1. Area of rectangle = Length × Width
2. Side of square (max area) = HCF(L, W)
3. Number of squares = (Total Area) ÷ (Area of one square)

Calculations:
⇒ Total Area of the floor = 12 m × 8 m = 96 m2
⇒ To find the maximum possible area of square designs, find HCF of 12 and 8.
⇒ 12 = 2 × 2 × 3
⇒ 8 = 2 × 2 × 2
⇒ HCF(12, 8) = 2 × 2 = 4 m
⇒ Area of one square design = 4 m × 4 m = 16 m2
⇒ Number of square designs required = 96 ÷ 16
⇒ Number of square designs required = 6
∴ The correct answer is 6.

Additional Information
Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The HCF of two or more numbers is the largest positive integer that divides each of the numbers without leaving a remainder.

Minimum Number of Tiles

To minimize the number of tiles needed to cover a rectangular area, the side of each square tile must be the HCF of the length and breadth of the rectangle.

Area and Perimeter of a Square

Area = side2 and Perimeter = 4 × side. All four sides of a square are equal and each angle is 90°.

questions.question: If the volume of a hemisphere is 155232 cm^3, then half of the radius (in cm) of the hemisphere is: (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Solution

Given:
Volume of a hemisphere = 155232 cm3
π = 22 / 7

Formula Used:
Volume of a hemisphere = (2 / 3) × π × r3
Where r = radius of the hemisphere.

Calculation:
Given Volume = 155232 cm3

Using the formula:

(2 / 3) × (22 / 7) × r3 = 155232
⇒ r3 = (155232 × 3 × 7) / (2 × 22)
⇒ r3 = (155232 × 21) / 44
⇒ r3 = 74088

Taking the cube root:

⇒ r = ∛74088
⇒ r = 42 cm
Half of the radius = r / 2
⇒ Half of the radius = 42 / 2
⇒ Half of the radius = 21 cm

The half of the radius of the hemisphere is 21 cm.

questions.question: If 3^(2p+4) = 6561, then find the value of (p + 1)^4
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Convert 6561 into a power of 3: 6561 = 38.
Equating the exponents of base 3: 2p + 4 = 8 ⇒ 2p = 4 ⇒ p = 2.
Substitute p = 2 to find the required expression: (p + 1)4 = (2 + 1)4 = 34 = 81.
∴ The correct answer is 81.

Alternate Method
Given:
3(2p+4) = 6561

Formula Used:
If am = an for any base a > 1, then m = n.

Calculations:
⇒ 3(2p+4) = 6561

Factorizing 6561 gives:

⇒ 3(2p+4) = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3
⇒ 3(2p+4) = 38
Since the bases are the same, we can safely equate the exponents:
⇒ 2p + 4 = 8
⇒ 2p = 8 − 4
⇒ 2p = 4
⇒ p = 2
Now, substitute the value of p into the required expression (p + 1)4:
⇒ (2 + 1)4
⇒ 34
⇒ 81
∴ The correct answer is 81.

Additional Information
Law of Exponents (Multiplication & Division)

When multiplying terms with the same base, add their exponents: am × an = am+n. When dividing, subtract them: am ÷ an = am−n.

Power of a Power Rule

When raising a power to another power, multiply the exponents: (am)n = am×n.

Zero and Negative Exponents

Any non-zero base to the power of 0 is 1: a0 = 1. A negative exponent denotes the reciprocal of the base raised to the positive power: a−n = 1 ÷ an.

questions.question: What is the sum of digits of the number which when divided by 24, 40, and 48 leaves the remainder of 13, 29, and 37, respectively?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Find the common difference (k) between divisors and remainders: 24 − 13 = 11, 40 − 29 = 11, 48 − 37 = 11.

Calculate LCM of (24, 40, 48) = 240.

The required number is (LCM × n) − k. For n = 1, Number = 240 − 11 = 229.

Sum of digits of 229 = 2 + 2 + 9 = 13.
∴ The correct answer is 13.

Alternate Method
Given:
Divisors: D1 = 24, D2 = 40, D3 = 48
Remainders: R1 = 13, R2 = 29, R3 = 37

Formula Used:
When (D1 − R1) = (D2 − R2) = (D3 − R3) = k, the number is [LCM(D1, D2, D3) × n] − k.

Calculations:
⇒ Difference (k) = 24 − 13 = 11
⇒ Difference (k) = 40 − 29 = 11
⇒ Difference (k) = 48 − 37 = 11
⇒ LCM of 24, 40, and 48:
⇒ 24 = 23 × 3
⇒ 40 = 23 × 5
⇒ 48 = 24 × 3
⇒ LCM = 24 × 3 × 5 = 16 × 15 = 240
⇒ Smallest required number = 240 − 11 = 229
⇒ Sum of digits = 2 + 2 + 9 = 13
∴ The correct answer is 13.

Additional Information
LCM Method with Constant Remainder

If a number leaves the same remainder 'r' when divided by x, y, and z, the number is LCM(x, y, z) × n + r.

LCM Method with Constant Difference

If the difference between divisor and remainder is constant 'k', the number is LCM(divisors) × n − k.

Sum of Digits Property

The sum of digits of a number is often used in divisibility tests for 3 and 9, where the sum must be divisible by the divisor.

questions.question: The cost of plastering the four walls of a room is 25. The cost of plastering a room twice in length, breadth and height will be
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Area of four walls is proportional to (Length + Breadth) × Height.

If all dimensions (L, B, H) are doubled, the new area becomes 2 × 2 = 4 times the original area.

Cost is directly proportional to the area.
New Cost = 4 × Original Cost = 4 × 25 = 100.
∴ The correct answer is 100.

Alternate Method
Given:
Original cost of plastering = 25
New dimensions = 2 × Original dimensions

Formula Used:
Area of four walls = 2 × (Length + Breadth) × Height

Calculations:
⇒ Let original dimensions be L, B, and H.
⇒ Original Area (A1) = 2(L + B)H
⇒ New dimensions: L' = 2L, B' = 2B, H' = 2H
⇒ New Area (A2) = 2(2L + 2B) × 2H
⇒ A2 = 2 × 2(L + B) × 2H = 4 × [2(L + B)H]
⇒ A2 = 4 × A1
⇒ Since cost is proportional to area: New Cost = 4 × 25 = 100
∴ The correct answer is 100.

Additional Information
Lateral Surface Area

The area of the four walls of a cuboid is also known as the Lateral Surface Area (LSA), calculated as 2H(L + B).

Total Surface Area

If the floor and ceiling are included, the Total Surface Area (TSA) is 2(LB + BH + HL).

Scaling Effect on Volume

If all dimensions are doubled, the Volume increases by 23 = 8 times, whereas the Area increases by 22 = 4 times.

questions.question: Out of two numbers, the first number is three-fourth of the second number. If the average of the reciprocal of the two numbers is 7/48, then the first number is
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Ratio of the first number to the second number is 3 : 4. Let the numbers be 3x and 4x.
Sum of reciprocals = 2 × Average = 2 × (7/48) = 7/24.
According to the ratio: (1/3x) + (1/4x) = 7/24 ⇒ (4 + 3)/12x = 7/24.
7/12x = 7/24 ⇒ 12x = 24 ⇒ x = 2.
First number = 3 × 2 = 6.
∴ The correct answer is 6.

Alternate Method
Given:
First number (n1) = 3/4 of Second number (n2)
Average of reciprocals = 7/48

Formula:

Average of two values x and y = (x + y) ÷ 2
Let the second number be x. Then the first number is (3/4)x.

The reciprocals are 1/x and 4/3x.

⇒ [(1/x) + (4/3x)] ÷ 2 = 7/48
⇒ (1/x) + (4/3x) = (7/48) × 2
⇒ (3 + 4) / 3x = 7/24
⇒ 7 / 3x = 7 / 24
⇒ 3x = 24
⇒ x = 8 (This is the second number)
⇒ First number = (3/4) × 8 = 6

Thus, the first number is 6, which corresponds to Option (4).

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Additional Information
Reciprocal Property

The product of a number and its reciprocal is always 1. If a number is x/y, its reciprocal is y/x.

Average of Fractions

To find the average of two fractions, add them using a common denominator and then divide the sum by 2.

Ratio and Proportion

If A is k times B, the ratio A:B is k:1. This helps in representing variables as multiples of a common factor (e.g., 3x and 4x).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: A student got 20% marks and failed by 72 marks. If he scores 40% marks then he gets 8 marks more than the passing marks. Find the passing marks.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Difference in percentage = 40% − 20% = 20%
Difference in marks = 72 (shortfall) + 8 (excess) = 80 marks
Since 20% of maximum marks = 80 marks
Passing marks = 20% marks + 72 marks = 80 + 72 = 152
∴ The correct answer is 152 marks.

Alternate Method
Given:
Marks scored in case 1 = 20% (Failed by 72 marks)
Marks scored in case 2 = 40% (8 marks more than passing marks)

Calculation:
Let the total maximum marks be x.
⇒ Passing marks = 20% of x + 72
⇒ Passing marks = 40% of x − 8

Equating both the expressions:

⇒ 20% of x + 72 = 40% of x − 8
⇒ 40% of x − 20% of x = 72 + 8
⇒ 20% of x = 80
⇒ x = (80 × 100) ÷ 20
⇒ x = 400
⇒ Passing marks = 20% of 400 + 72
⇒ Passing marks = 80 + 72 = 152
∴ The correct answer is 152 marks.

Additional Information
Passing Marks Concept
When a student fails by a certain margin, Passing Marks = Obtained Marks + Shortfall Marks.

Excess Marks Concept

When a student scores above passing marks, Passing Marks = Obtained Marks − Excess Marks.
Difference Rule

The percentage difference between the two scenarios will always be equal to the sum of the shortfall marks and the excess marks.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 1
questions.question: If the average of a number, 50% of that number, and 25% of the same number is 280, then find the number.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the required number be 100%.

The three parts given are 100%, 50%, and 25%.

Sum of these parts = 100% + 50% + 25% = 175%
Average = 175% ÷ 3 = 280
⇒ 100% = (280 × 3 × 100) ÷ 175 = 480
∴ The correct answer is 480.

Alternate Method
Given:
The average of a number, 50% of that number, and 25% of the same number is 280.

Formula Used:
Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

Calculation:
⇒ Let the required number be x.
⇒ The other two values are 0.50x and 0.25x.
⇒ Sum of all three values = x + 0.50x + 0.25x = 1.75x
⇒ Average = 1.75x ÷ 3
⇒ 1.75x ÷ 3 = 280
⇒ 1.75x = 280 × 3
⇒ 1.75x = 840
⇒ x = 840 ÷ 1.75
⇒ x = 84000 ÷ 175 = 480
∴ The correct answer is 480.

Additional Information
Average of Multiple Quantities

The average (or arithmetic mean) is defined as the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Average = Sum ÷ Count.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Percentages can be directly represented as fractions or decimals to simplify calculations: 50% = 1/2 = 0.5 and 25% = 1/4 = 0.25.

Solving Linear Equations

When solving an equation in the form ax = b, dividing both sides by the coefficient a gives the value of x. Using fractions like 1.75 = 7/4 can make division easier (x = 840 × 4 ÷ 7 = 480).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: On a sum of money, the compound interest for 2 years is Rs. 832, while the simple interest for the same time period is Rs.800, then find out the difference amount for period of 3 years?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
SI for 1 year = 800 ÷ 2 = ₹400
Difference for 2 years = CI − SI = 832 − 800 = ₹32
Rate
(R) = (Interest on 1st year SI ÷ 1st year SI) × 100 = (32 ÷ 400) × 100 = 8%
For 3 years, Difference = 3 × (2-year Diff) + (R% of 2-year Diff)
Difference = 3 × 32 + (8% of 32) = 96 + 2.56 = 98.56
∴ The correct answer is ₹98.56.

Alternate Method
Given:
Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹832
Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹800

Formula Used:
Difference for 2 years (D2) = P × (R ÷ 100)2
Difference for 3 years (D3) = 3 × D2 + (R% of D2)

Calculations:
⇒ SI for 1 year = Total SI ÷ 2 = 800 ÷ 2 = ₹400
⇒ Difference between CI and SI for 2 years (D2) = 832 − 800 = ₹32
⇒ The difference of ₹32 is the interest earned exactly on the first year's SI (₹400).
⇒ Rate of Interest
(R) = (32 ÷ 400) × 100% = 8%
⇒ Difference for 3 years (D3) = 3 × D2 + (R% of D2)
⇒ D3 = 3 × 32 + (8 ÷ 100) × 32
⇒ D3 = 96 + 2.56
⇒ D3 = ₹98.56
∴ The correct answer is ₹98.56.

Additional Information
Tree Method for Compound Interest

It breaks down CI into simple interest and interest-on-interest components. The 1st row is always the Simple Interest. The lower rows sum up to represent the exact difference between CI and SI over the years.

CI vs SI Difference (2 Years)

Formula: Diff2 = P × (R ÷ 100)2. It strictly represents the interest generated on the first year's simple interest.

CI vs SI Difference (3 Years)

Formula: Diff3 = P × (R ÷ 100)2 × (3 + R ÷ 100). For fast calculation, simply multiply the 2-year difference by 3 and add the rate percentage of the 2-year difference.

questions.question: Two tangents TP and TQ are drawn to circle with centre O from an external point T, where P and Q are points on circumference of the circle. If ∠PTQ = 50°, then find the value of ∠TOQ.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
The line joining the external point to the centre bisects the angle between the two tangents.

⇒ ∠OTQ = ∠PTQ ÷ 2 = 50° ÷ 2 = 25°

In right-angled ΔOQT, the radius OQ is perpendicular to the tangent TQ at point Q (∠OQT = 90°).

⇒ ∠TOQ = 90° − ∠OTQ = 90° − 25° = 65°
∴ The correct answer is 65°.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Tangents TP and TQ are drawn from an external point T.
⇒ ∠PTQ = 50°

Concept Used:

⇒ The radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact.
⇒ The sum of the angles of a quadrilateral is 360°.

50°

Calculations:
In quadrilateral OPT
Q:

⇒ ∠OPT = 90° and ∠OQT = 90°
⇒ ∠OPT + ∠OQT + ∠PTQ + ∠POQ = 360°
⇒ 90° + 90° + 50° + ∠POQ = 360°
⇒ 230° + ∠POQ = 360°
⇒ ∠POQ = 360° − 230° = 130°
Since the line OT joining the external point to the centre bisects ∠PO
Q:
⇒ ∠TOQ = ∠POQ ÷ 2
⇒ ∠TOQ = 130° ÷ 2 = 65°
∴ The correct answer is 65°.

Additional Information
Properties of Tangents from an External Point

The lengths of the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are exactly equal to each other (TP = TQ).

Angle Subtended at the Centre

The two tangents subtend equal angles at the centre of the circle, meaning the line connecting the external point to the centre acts as an angle bisector (∠POT = ∠QOT).

Cyclic Quadrilateral Formation

The quadrilateral formed by the two tangents and the two radii to the points of contact has opposite angles that sum to 180°, specifically ∠PTQ + ∠POQ = 180°.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: A closed cylindrical tank with a height of 1 m and a base diameter of 140 cm must be constructed from a metal sheet. For the same, how many m^2 of the sheet are required? [Use π = 22/7]
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
For a closed cylinder, Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h)
Radius (r) = 140 ÷ 2 = 70 cm = 0.7 m, Height (h) = 1 m
Area = 2 × (22/7) × 0.7 × (0.7 + 1)
Area = 44 × 0.1 × 1.7 = 7.48
∴ The correct answer is 7.48 m2.

Alternate Method
Given:
Height of the closed cylindrical tank (h) = 1 m
Base diameter (d) = 140 cm = 1.4 m
⇒ Radius (r) = 1.4 ÷ 2 = 0.7 m

Formula Used:
Total Surface Area of a closed cylinder = 2πr(r + h)

Calculations:
⇒ Total Surface Area = 2 × (22/7) × 0.7 × (0.7 + 1)
⇒ Total Surface Area = 44 × 0.1 × 1.7
⇒ Total Surface Area = 4.4 × 1.7 = 7.48 m2
∴ The correct answer is 7.48 m2.

Additional Information
Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a Cylinder

The area of the curved sides excluding the top and bottom circular bases. Formula: CSA = 2πrh.

Open vs Closed Cylinder

A closed cylinder includes both bases where TSA = 2πr(r + h), whereas an open cylinder has no top and its area is calculated as 2πrh + πr2.

Volume of a Cylinder

The total space occupied by the cylinder. Formula: Volume = πr2h.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: A vessel can be filled by a tap A in 8 minutes, and by another tap B in 10 minutes. A third tap C can empty the vessel in 4 minutes. If all taps are opened simultaneously when the vessel is half full, then which of the following is true?

options.a: The vessel will be filled in 20 minutes.
options.b: The vessel will be filled in 40 minutes.
options.c: The vessel will be emptied in 40 minutes.
options.d: The vessel will be emptied in 20 minutes.

questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total Capacity = LCM(8, 10, 4) = 40 units.
Efficiency of taps → A: +5, B: +4, C: −10.
Net efficiency = 5 + 4 − 10 = −1 unit/min (Negative means vessel empties).
Since the vessel is half full, volume to empty = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 units.
Time to empty the vessel = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 minutes.
∴ The correct answer is emptied in 20 minutes.

Alternate Method
Given:
Time taken by tap A to fill the vessel = 8 min
Time taken by tap B to fill the vessel = 10 min
Time taken by tap C to empty the vessel = 4 min

The vessel is half full initially.

Tap	Time (min)	Total Capacity	Efficiency
A	8	40	+5
B	10	+4
C (Empty)	4	−10

Calculations:
⇒ Net efficiency of all taps together = 5 + 4 − 10 = −1 unit/min.
⇒ A negative efficiency indicates that the vessel is being emptied.
⇒ Quantity of water in the half-full vessel = 40 × (1/2) = 20 units.
⇒ Time required to empty the vessel = Total water ÷ Effective efficiency
⇒ Time = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 minutes.
∴ The correct answer is emptied in 20 minutes.

Additional Information
Pipes and Cisterns Basics

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its part filled in 1 hour is 1/x. If it empties a full tank in y hours, its part emptied in 1 hour is −1/y.

Net Work Method

Net part filled in 1 hour by both pipes = (1/x) − (1/y). If the result is positive, the tank is being filled. If negative, it is being emptied.
Total Capacity (LCM Method)

Total capacity is assumed to be the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of all given individual times. Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time taken.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 3
questions.question: What should come in place of both x in the equation x / √128 = √162 / x?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Cross-multiply the given values to solve for x2 directly:

x2 = √128 × √162 = √(128 × 162)
x2 = √(64 × 2 × 81 × 2) = √(64 × 81 × 4)
x2 = 8 × 9 × 2 = 144
x = √144 = 12
∴ The correct answer is 12.

Alternate Method
Given:
x / √128 = √162 / x

Calculation:
⇒ Cross-multiplying both sides, we get:
⇒ x × x = √128 × √162
⇒ x2 = √(128 × 162)
⇒ Factorizing the numbers into perfect squares:
⇒ x2 = √(64 × 2 × 81 × 2)
⇒ x2 = √(64 × 81 × 4)
⇒ Taking the square root of the perfect squares:
⇒ x2 = 8 × 9 × 2
⇒ x2 = 144
⇒ x = √144
⇒ x = 12
∴ The correct answer is 12.

Additional Information
Multiplication of Surds

When multiplying square roots, you can combine them under a single root: √a × √b = √(a × b). This helps in factoring out perfect squares easily.

Perfect Squares Identification

Breaking down large numbers into products of known perfect squares (like 64 = 82 and 81 = 92) simplifies square root calculations significantly without needing prime factorization.

Solving Quadratic Variables

An equation of the form x2 = a2 generally has two roots: x = a and x = −a. In quantitative aptitude simplification questions, the positive root is usually considered unless options suggest otherwise.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 4
questions.question: An equilateral triangle with side a units is cut on the vertices to make it a regular hexagon. What is the area of the hexagon?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When the vertices of an equilateral triangle are cut to form a regular hexagon, the side length is exactly trisected.

Side of the regular hexagon = Side of triangle ÷ 3 = a / 3.
Area of a regular hexagon = 6 × Area of small equilateral triangle = 6 × (√3 ÷ 4) × (side)2.
Area = 6 × (√3 ÷ 4) × (a / 3)2 = (3√3 ÷ 2) × (a2 ÷ 9).
Area = √3a2 ÷ 6 = a2 / (2√3).
∴ The correct answer is a2 / (2√3) square units.

Alternate Method
Given:
An equilateral triangle with side length a.

The vertices are cut out to make a regular hexagon.

Formula Used:
Area of an equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × a2
Area of a regular hexagon = 6 × (√3 ÷ 4) × x2 (where x is the side length)

Calculations:
⇒ Let the side length of the regular hexagon be x.
⇒ When cutting the vertices of an equilateral triangle to form a regular hexagon, the cut-out portions are smaller equilateral triangles of side length x.
⇒ The original side 'a' consists of three linear segments: one side of a cut-off triangle, one side of the hexagon, and one side of another cut-off triangle.
⇒ x + x + x = a
⇒ 3x = a
⇒ x = a / 3
⇒ The area of the regular hexagon is the combined area of 6 small equilateral triangles of side x.
⇒ Area = 6 × [(√3 ÷ 4) × (a / 3)2]
⇒ Area = 6 × (√3 ÷ 4) × (a2 ÷ 9)
⇒ Area = (6√3 × a2) ÷ 36
⇒ Area = (√3 × a2) ÷ 6
⇒ Multiplying numerator and denominator by √3 to simplify the fraction:
⇒ Area = (√3 × √3 × a2) ÷ (6 × √3) = 3a2 ÷ 6√3
⇒ Area = a2 / (2√3)
∴ The correct answer is a2 / (2√3) square units.

Additional Information
Area of an Equilateral Triangle

The area of an equilateral triangle with side 'a' is given by Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × a2, and its height is h = (√3 ÷ 2) × a.

Regular Hexagon Area

A regular hexagon with side 'x' is structurally made of 6 identical equilateral triangles. Its total area is 6 × (√3 ÷ 4) × x2 = (3√3 ÷ 2) × x2.

Inradius & Circumradius of Equilateral Triangle

For an equilateral triangle of side 'a', the inradius is r = a ÷ (2√3) and the circumradius is R = a ÷ √3. Note that the circumradius is always exactly double the inradius (R = 2r).

Max Area Hexagon in a Triangle

The largest regular hexagon that can be inscribed in any equilateral triangle is formed precisely by cutting off its corners, and its side length is always strictly one-third of the parent triangle's side.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: From 11 to 50, how many numbers are there which are exactly divisible by 7 but not by 3?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total multiples of 7 from 11 to 50 = (Largest multiple − Smallest multiple) ÷ 7 + 1 = (49 − 14) ÷ 7 + 1 = 6.

Total multiples of 21 (divisible by both 7 and 3) from 11 to 50 = (42 − 21) ÷ 21 + 1 = 2.

Total numbers divisible by 7 but not by 3 = 6 − 2 = 4.
∴ The correct answer is 4 numbers.

Alternate Method
Given:
Range of numbers: From 11 to 50.
Condition: Numbers must be divisible by 7 but not by 3.

Calculations:
⇒ First, list all the numbers between 11 and 50 that are exactly divisible by 7.
⇒ These multiples are: 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49.
⇒ Total count of these multiples = 6.
⇒ Next, identify the numbers from this list that are also divisible by 3.
⇒ A number divisible by both 7 and 3 must be divisible by their LCM, which is 21.
⇒ The multiples of 21 in the given range are: 21 and 42.
⇒ We must exclude these 2 numbers from our initial list.
⇒ The remaining numbers are: 14, 28, 35, 49.
⇒ Total count of the remaining numbers = 4.
∴ The correct answer is 4 numbers.

Additional Information
LCM of Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime (like 3 and 7, having no common factors other than 1), their Least Common Multiple (LCM) is simply their product (3 × 7 = 21). Any number divisible by both must be a multiple of this LCM.

Arithmetic Progression (AP) Counting

To find the number of terms in an AP, you can use the formula: Number of terms = (Last term − First term) ÷ Common Difference + 1.

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is exactly divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: The present population of a city is 17,500. The population decreases by 12% in the first year and increases by 8% in the second year. Find the population after 2 years.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Use the successive multiplying factor method for consecutive percentage changes:

Final Population = Initial Population × (1 − Decrease%) × (1 + Increase%)
Final Population = 17500 × (88 ÷ 100) × (108 ÷ 100)
Final Population = 17500 × 0.88 × 1.08 = 15400 × 1.08 = 16632
∴ The correct answer is 16,632.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Initial population of the city = 17500
⇒ First year percentage change = −12% (Decrease)
⇒ Second year percentage change = +8% (Increase)

Formula Used:
Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± R1 ÷ 100) × (1 ± R2 ÷ 100)

Calculation:
⇒ Population after the first year = 17500 × (1 − 12 ÷ 100)
⇒ Population after the first year = 17500 × 0.88 = 15400
⇒ Population after the second year = 15400 × (1 + 8 ÷ 100)
⇒ Population after the second year = 15400 × 1.08 = 16632
∴ The correct answer is 16,632.

Additional Information
Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes multiple percentage changes in succession, the net percentage change can be computed as: Net Change = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100.

Multiplying Factor Method

The most efficient way to compute final base values is by applying fraction multipliers: (1 + x ÷ 100) for an increase and (1 − x ÷ 100) for a decrease.

Base Change Principle

In consecutive changes, the new percentage operation always applies to the newly formed base (the result of the previous year), not the original starting base.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: In ∆ABC, ∠B = 90° and BD ⟂ AC. If AC = 9 cm and AD = 3 cm, then BD is equal to:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
By the Geometric Mean Theorem for a right-angled triangle:

Altitude to hypotenuse = √(Product of hypotenuse segments)
CD = AC − AD = 9 − 3 = 6 cm
BD = √(3 × 6) = √18 = 3√2 cm
∴ The correct answer is 3√2 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
In right-angled ΔABC, ∠B = 90°

BD ⊥ AC

AC = 9 cm, AD = 3 cm

Formula Used:
In a right triangle, when an altitude is drawn from the right angle to the hypotenuse, the square of the altitude equals the product of the lengths of the two segments on the hypotenuse: BD2 = AD × DC.

Calculations:
⇒ DC = AC − AD
⇒ DC = 9 − 3 = 6 cm
⇒ BD2 = AD × DC
⇒ BD2 = 3 × 6
⇒ BD2 = 18
⇒ BD = √18 = 3√2 cm
∴ The correct answer is 3√2 cm.

Additional Information
Geometric Mean Theorem (Altitude Rule)

In a right-angled triangle, the altitude drawn to the hypotenuse divides it into two segments such that the altitude is the geometric mean of these two segments. (Altitude2 = Segment 1 × Segment 2)

Leg Rule of a Right Triangle

Each leg of a right-angled triangle is the geometric mean of the hypotenuse and the segment of the hypotenuse adjacent to that leg. (Leg2 = Hypotenuse × Adjacent Segment)

Pythagorean Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two legs. (H2 = P2 + B2)

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: If cot 18° = p/q, then the value of cosec^2(378°) / (1 + tan^2(378°)) is
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Reduce the angle to the first quadrant: 378° = 360° + 18°.

The expression becomes cosec2 18° / (1 + tan2 18°).

Using 1 + tan2 θ = sec2 θ, it simplifies to cosec2 18° / sec2 18°.
Since cosec θ / sec θ = cot θ, the entire expression strictly reduces to cot2 18°.
Substitute cot 18° = p/q directly to get (p/q)2 = p2/q2.
∴ The correct answer is p2/q2.

Alternate Method
Given:
cot 18° = p/q

Formula Used:
cosec(360° + θ) = cosec θ
tan(360° + θ) = tan θ
1 + tan2 θ = sec2 θ
cosec θ = 1 / sin θ
sec θ = 1 / cos θ

Calculations:
⇒ Angle reduction: 378° = 360° + 18°
⇒ cosec 378° = cosec 18° and tan 378° = tan 18°
⇒ Substitute into the expression: (cosec2 18°) / (1 + tan2 18°)
⇒ Apply the trigonometric identity 1 + tan2 18° = sec2 18°:
⇒ Expression = (cosec2 18°) / (sec2 18°)
⇒ Convert sec and cosec functions into fundamental sine and cosine functions:
⇒ Expression = (1 / sin2 18°) × (cos2 18° / 1)
⇒ Expression = cos2 18° / sin2 18°
⇒ Expression = cot2 18°
⇒ Substitute the given value cot 18° = p/q directly:
⇒ (p / q)2 = p2 / q2
∴ The correct answer is p2/q2.

Additional Information
Trigonometric Quadrant Rule (ASTC)

In the first quadrant (0° to 90°), all trigonometric ratios are positive. Angles in the form (360° × n + θ) lie in the first quadrant, retaining exactly the original ratio and identical sign configuration.

Pythagorean Identities

The three fundamental identities mapping trigonometric pairs are: sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1, 1 + tan2 θ = sec2 θ, and 1 + cot2 θ = cosec2 θ.

Reciprocal Relations

Key inverse and quotient relations include: cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ, sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ, and cot θ = 1 ÷ tan θ = cos θ ÷ sin θ.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: Pabitra takes twice as long as Kader or three times as long as Rahim to complete a task. If they work together, they can complete the task in 2 days. How long will it take Kader to complete the task on his own?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of time taken by Pabitra, Kader, and Rahim = 6 : 3 : 2
Efficiency ratio = 1/6 : 1/3 : 1/2 = 1 : 2 : 3
Combined efficiency = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 units/day
Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Time = 6 × 2 = 12 units
Time taken by Kader alone = Total Work ÷ Kader's Efficiency = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 days
∴ The correct answer is 6 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
Pabitra takes twice as long as Kader and three times as long as Rahim to complete the task.

Let the time taken by Pabitra be 6x days.
⇒ Time taken by Kader = 6x ÷ 2 = 3x days
⇒ Time taken by Rahim = 6x ÷ 3 = 2x days
Method Used: LCM Method for Time & Work

Person	Days	Total Work	Efficiency
Pabitra	6x	6x	1
Kader	3x	2
Rahim	2x	3

⇒ Total efficiency = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 units/day
⇒ Total time taken working together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency = 6x ÷ 6 = x days
⇒ It is given that they complete the task together in 2 days.
⇒ Therefore, x = 2
⇒ Time taken by Kader alone = 3x = 3 × 2 = 6 days
∴ The correct answer is 6 days.

Additional Information
Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If a person takes 'd' days to complete a work, their efficiency (one day's work) is 1/d.

Total Work Concept

Total Work is considered as the LCM of the individual times taken by each person. Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Total Time Taken.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person. If people work for the same number of days, their wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: If a sum triples in 4 years at simple interest, find the time that it would take to become 5 times itself at the same rate of interest.
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
In Simple Interest, Interest is directly proportional to Time when Principal and Rate are constant.

For a sum to triple (3 times), Interest = 3 − 1 = 2 units.
For a sum to become 5 times, Interest = 5 − 1 = 4 units.
Time for 2 units interest = 4 years.
Time for 4 units interest = (4 ÷ 2) × 4 = 8 years.
∴ The correct answer is 8 years.

Alternate Method
Given: Time (T1) = 4 years, Amount1 = 3P, Amount2 = 5P (where P is Principal)
Formula: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100
Principal
(P)
3 × P
5 × P
Interest = 2P
(4 years)
Interest = 2P
(4 years)
Total Time = 4 + 4 = 8 years
⇒ SI1 = Amount1 − P = 3P − P = 2P ⇒ 2P = (P × R × 4) / 100 ⇒ R = (2P × 100) / (4P) = 50% ⇒ SI2 = Amount2 − P = 5P − P = 4P ⇒ 4P = (P × 50 × T2) / 100 ⇒ T2 = (4P × 100) / (50P) ⇒ T2 = 400 / 50 = 8 years
∴ The correct answer is 8 years.

Additional Information
Interest Proportionality

In simple interest, the interest earned is directly proportional to time (T) and rate
(R) since SI = (P × R × T) / 100.

Amount as n-times Principal

If a sum becomes n times itself, the interest earned is (n − 1) × P. For same rate and principal, T1 / (n1 − 1) = T2 / (n2 − 1).

Rule of SI vs CI

For the first year (or first compounding period), SI and CI are equal if the principal and rate are the same.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: A boat can go 54 km upstream in 6 hours. If the speed of the stream is 4.8 km/h, then how much time (in hours) will the boat take to cover a distance of 279 km downstream?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Upstream speed (U) = 54 ÷ 6 = 9 km/h.
Downstream speed (D) = U + 2 × Stream speed = 9 + 2 × 4.8 = 18.6 km/h.
Time downstream = Distance ÷ D = 279 ÷ 18.6 = 15 hours.
∴ The correct answer is 15 hours.

Alternate Method
Given:
Distance upstream = 54 km
Time upstream = 6 hours
Speed of the stream
(S) = 4.8 km/h
Distance downstream = 279 km

Formula Used:
Upstream speed (U) = Boat speed (B) − Stream speed
(S)
Downstream speed (D) = Boat speed (B) + Stream speed
(S)
Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Calculations:
⇒ Upstream speed (U) = 54 ÷ 6 = 9 km/h
⇒ U = B − S
⇒ 9 = B − 4.8
⇒ B = 9 + 4.8 = 13.8 km/h
⇒ Downstream speed (D) = B + S = 13.8 + 4.8 = 18.6 km/h
⇒ Time downstream = Distance ÷ Downstream speed
⇒ Time downstream = 279 ÷ 18.6 = 15 hours
∴ The correct answer is 15 hours.

Additional Information
Upstream and Downstream Speeds

When a boat travels against the flow of the river, it moves upstream (U = B − S). When it travels with the flow, it moves downstream (D = B + S).

Speed of Boat and Stream
If upstream speed (U) and downstream speed (D) are given: Speed of boat in still water (B) = (D + U) ÷ 2. Speed of stream
(S) = (D − U) ÷ 2.
Distance, Speed and Time
The fundamental relation is Distance = Speed × Time. For river problems, always determine the effective speed (downstream or upstream) first.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: Amount on compound interest is doubled to the original amount in 3 years. In how many years will it be eight times its original amount?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
If a sum becomes n times in T years at Compound Interest,

It will become nm times in m × T years.

Here, the sum becomes 2 times in 3 years.

We need the sum to become 8 times, which is 23 times (so m = 3).
Required time = 3 × 3 = 9 years.
∴ The correct answer is 9 years.

Alternate Method
Given:
Principal
(P) becomes 2P in Time (T) = 3 years.
Let Rate of Interest be R% per annum.

Formula Used:
Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)T

Calculation:
⇒ 2P = P(1 + R/100)3
⇒ 2 = (1 + R/100)3    ... (Equation 1)

We need to find the time (T') when the principal becomes 8P.

⇒ 8P = P(1 + R/100)T'
⇒ 8 = (1 + R/100)T'
Since 8 can be written as 23, substitute the value of 2 from Equation 1:
⇒ [(1 + R/100)3]3 = (1 + R/100)T'
⇒ (1 + R/100)9 = (1 + R/100)T'

Comparing the powers on both sides:

⇒ T' = 9
∴ The correct answer is 9 years.

Additional Information
Multiplying Factor in Compound Interest

If a sum of money becomes x times in T years at CI, it becomes xn times in n × T years due to successive compounding.

Simple Interest Linear Growth

Unlike CI, in Simple Interest, if a sum becomes 2 times in T years (i.e., Interest = P), it will become 8 times (Interest = 7P) in 7 × T years since interest remains constant.

Half-Yearly Compounding

When compounded half-yearly, the rate of interest becomes half (R/2) and the time period is doubled (2T). Formula: A = P(1 + R/200)2T.

CI and SI Difference

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years on a given principal is calculated as: D = P × (R/100)2.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: The value of $\rm \frac{\sin (\pi+\theta)\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\theta\right)}{\sin (2\pi -\theta)\cos(2\pi+\theta)} \times \frac{\tan \left(\frac{3\pi}{2}-\theta\right)\cot(2\pi-\theta)}{cosec (-\theta)\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}+\theta\right)}$ is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Put θ = 45° to evaluate the expression quickly without using complex trigonometric identities.
Given = [sin(225°) × cos(135°)] / [sin(315°) × cos(405°)] × [tan(225°) × cot(315°)] / [cosec(−45°) × sin(315°)]
⇒ [(−1/√2) × (−1/√2)] / [(−1/√2) × (1/√2)] × [1 × (−1)] / [(−√2) × (−1/√2)]
⇒ [(1/2) / (−1/2)] × [(−1) / 1]
⇒ (−1) × (−1) = 1
∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method
Given:
[sin(π + θ) × cos(π/2 + θ)] / [sin(2π − θ) × cos(2π + θ)] × [tan(3π/2 − θ) × cot(2π − θ)] / [cosec(−θ) × sin(3π/2 + θ)]

Formula Used:
Trigonometric conversions for allied angles:

⇒ sin(π + θ) = −sinθ | cos(π/2 + θ) = −sinθ
⇒ sin(2π − θ) = −sinθ | cos(2π + θ) = cosθ
⇒ tan(3π/2 − θ) = cotθ | cot(2π − θ) = −cotθ
⇒ cosec(−θ) = −cosecθ | sin(3π/2 + θ) = −cosθ

Calculation:
⇒ Substituting the conversions into the given expression:
⇒ [(−sinθ) × (−sinθ)] / [(−sinθ) × (cosθ)] × [(cotθ) × (−cotθ)] / [(−cosecθ) × (−cosθ)]
⇒ [sin2θ] / [−sinθ × cosθ] × [−cot2θ] / [cosecθ × cosθ]
⇒ [−sinθ / cosθ] × [−cot2θ] / [(1 / sinθ) × cosθ]
⇒ [−tanθ] × [−cot2θ / cotθ]
⇒ (−tanθ) × (−cotθ)
⇒ tanθ × cotθ = 1
∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information
ASTC Rule (Quadrants)

1st Quadrant: All positive | 2nd Quadrant: sin & cosec positive | 3rd Quadrant: tan & cot positive | 4th Quadrant: cos & sec positive.

Complementary & Supplementary Angles

For angles (90° ± θ) and (270° ± θ), trigonometric ratios change (sin ↔ cos, tan ↔ cot, sec ↔ cosec). For angles (180° ± θ) and (360° ± θ), the trigonometric ratios remain unchanged.

Negative Angle Identities

sin(−θ) = −sinθ | cos(−θ) = cosθ | tan(−θ) = −tanθ | cosec(−θ) = −cosecθ.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: A can make a divider in 20 days, while B can make it in 50 days. If they work together and get Rs.3500, then find the share of B in the amount.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Wages are distributed in the inverse ratio of time taken when persons work together.

Time ratio of A : B = 20 : 50 = 2 : 5
Efficiency (wage) ratio of A : B = 5 : 2
Share of B = (2 ÷ 7) × 3500 = 1000
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1000.

Alternate Method
Given:
Time taken by A = 20 days
Time taken by B = 50 days
Total wages = Rs. 3500

Formula Used:
Wages are distributed in the ratio of efficiencies when working together.

Total Work = LCM of days taken.
Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Days

Person	Days	Total Work	Efficiency
A	20	100	5
B	50	2

Calculations:
⇒ Efficiency ratio of A : B = 5 : 2
⇒ Total efficiency parts = 5 + 2 = 7
⇒ Share of B = (Efficiency of B ÷ Total efficiency) × Total wages
⇒ Share of B = (2 ÷ 7) × 3500
⇒ Share of B = 2 × 500 = 1000
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1000.

Additional Information
Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in proportion to the total work done. If multiple people work together for the exact same duration, their total wages are directly divided in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.

Efficiency vs Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If the ratio of time taken by A and B to complete a piece of work is a : b, then the ratio of their individual efficiencies will be b : a.

Pipes & Cisterns

Concepts of time and work apply identically to pipes and cisterns problems. The only key difference is that an outlet or emptying pipe is assigned a negative efficiency.
questions.conceptTested: Wages are distributed directly in the ratio of individual efficiencies, where efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: The average speed of a train is 180% of the average speed of a car. The car covers a distance of 990 km in 15 hours. The time taken (in hours) by the train to cover the distance of 891 km is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Speed of the car = 990 ÷ 15 = 66 km/h.
Speed of the train = 180% of 66 = 1.8 × 66 = 118.8 km/h.
Time taken by train = Distance ÷ Speed = 891 ÷ 118.8 = 7.5 hours.
7.5 hours is equal to 7½ hours.
∴ The correct answer is 7½ hours.

Alternate Method
Given:
Distance covered by car = 990 km
Time taken by car = 15 hours
Average speed of train = 180% of average speed of car
Distance to be covered by train = 891 km

Formula Used:
Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Calculations:
⇒ Speed of the car = 990 ÷ 15
⇒ Speed of the car = 66 km/h
⇒ Speed of the train = 180% of 66
⇒ Speed of the train = (180 ÷ 100) × 66 = 1.8 × 66 = 118.8 km/h
⇒ Time taken by the train = 891 ÷ 118.8
⇒ Time taken by the train = 8910 ÷ 1188
⇒ Time taken by the train = 7.5 hours
⇒ 7.5 hours = 7½ hours
∴ The correct answer is 7½ hours.

Additional Information
Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S1 − S2). In opposite directions, it is the sum (S1 + S2).

Conversion of Units

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: The present ages of three persons are in the proportion 4 : 7 : 9. Eight years ago, the sum of their ages was 56 years. The present age of the eldest person is
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total sum of ages at present = Sum 8 years ago + (3 persons × 8 years)
⇒ Present sum = 56 + 24 = 80 years
Total ratio parts = 4 + 7 + 9 = 20 parts
1 part = 80 ÷ 20 = 4 years
Eldest person's age (9 parts) = 9 × 4 = 36 years
∴ The correct answer is 36 years.

Alternate Method
Given:
Present ages of three persons are in the ratio 4 : 7 : 9.
Sum of their ages 8 years ago = 56 years.

Calculations:
Let the present ages of the three persons be 4x, 7x, and 9x.
⇒ Sum of their present ages = 4x + 7x + 9x = 20x

We know that 8 years ago, the sum of their ages was 56.

Since 8 years have passed for all 3 persons, the sum of their ages will increase by 3 × 8 = 24 years to reach the present day.

⇒ Present sum of ages = 56 + 24 = 80 years
⇒ 20x = 80
⇒ x = 80 ÷ 20 = 4

The present age of the eldest person corresponds to the largest ratio part, which is 9x.

⇒ Eldest person's age = 9 × 4 = 36 years.
∴ The correct answer is 36 years.

Additional Information
Sum of Ages over Time

When moving forward or backward in time by 'n' years, the sum of ages of 'k' individuals changes exactly by 'n × k' years.

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of any two people remains strictly constant regardless of the time period, past or future.

Age Ratios

If the present age ratio is a : b, the ratio after 't' years becomes (ax + t) : (bx + t), where x is the common multiplier representing the exact value of one ratio unit.

questions.question: The value of \(\frac{\sin (\pi+\theta)\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\theta\right)}{\sin (2\pi -\theta)\cos(2%\pi+\theta)} \times \frac{\tan \left(\frac{3\pi}{2}-\theta\right)\cot(2\pi-\theta)}{\csc (-\theta)\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}+\theta\right)}\) is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Put θ = 45° to evaluate the expression quickly without using complex trigonometric identities.
Given = [sin(225°) × cos(135°)] / [sin(315°) × cos(405°)] × [tan(225°) × cot(315°)] / [cosec(−45°) × sin(315°)]
⇒ [(−1/√2) × (−1/√2)] / [(−1/√2) × (1/√2)] × [1 × (−1)] / [(−√2) × (−1/√2)]
⇒ [(1/2) / (−1/2)] × [(−1) / 1]
⇒ (−1) × (−1) = 1
∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method
Given:
[sin(π + θ) × cos(π/2 + θ)] / [sin(2π − θ) × cos(2π + θ)] × [tan(3π/2 − θ) × cot(2π − θ)] / [cosec(−θ) × sin(3π/2 + θ)]

Formula Used:
Trigonometric conversions for allied angles:

⇒ sin(π + θ) = −sinθ | cos(π/2 + θ) = −sinθ
⇒ sin(2π − θ) = −sinθ | cos(2π + θ) = cosθ
⇒ tan(3π/2 − θ) = cotθ | cot(2π − θ) = −cotθ
⇒ cosec(−θ) = −cosecθ | sin(3π/2 + θ) = −cosθ

Calculation:
⇒ Substituting the conversions into the given expression:
⇒ [(−sinθ) × (−sinθ)] / [(−sinθ) × (cosθ)] × [(cotθ) × (−cotθ)] / [(−cosecθ) × (−cosθ)]
⇒ [sin2θ] / [−sinθ × cosθ] × [−cot2θ] / [cosecθ × cosθ]
⇒ [−sinθ / cosθ] × [−cot2θ] / [(1 / sinθ) × cosθ]
⇒ [−tanθ] × [−cot2θ / cotθ]
⇒ (−tanθ) × (−cotθ)
⇒ tanθ × cotθ = 1
∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information
ASTC Rule (Quadrants)

1st Quadrant: All positive | 2nd Quadrant: sin & cosec positive | 3rd Quadrant: tan & cot positive | 4th Quadrant: cos & sec positive.

Complementary & Supplementary Angles

For angles (90° ± θ) and (270° ± θ), trigonometric ratios change (sin ↔ cos, tan ↔ cot, sec ↔ cosec). For angles (180° ± θ) and (360° ± θ), the trigonometric ratios remain unchanged.

Negative Angle Identities

sin(−θ) = −sinθ | cos(−θ) = cosθ | tan(−θ) = −tanθ | cosec(−θ) = −cosecθ.
